Commentary of al-Sha'rawi on surah 33, verse 1:

In the Name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿O Prophet, fear God, and do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites. Indeed, God is ever Knowing and Wise.﴾ (33:1)

God's words, ﴿O Prophet...﴾ (33:1), are an address to the Messenger of God (ﷺ). The One who calls is God, glorified is He, and "Messenger of God" is his title (laqab). His name is Muhammad, and his name is also Ahmad, as mentioned in the Qur'an. When a person is born, he is given a name that identifies the one named, so that when the one who gave the name uses it, it refers to the named person. The people who were given that name have a circle in which they are known, and others who have the same names have another circle. So this Muhammad's circle is not the circle of that Muhammad.

A person is identified by his name (ism), by his kunya, or by his laqab. The ism is the proper name given to a named person so that he may be known by it, called by it, and distinguished from others. The kunya is a name that begins with "father of" or "mother of," as when we say Abu Bakr or Umm al-Mu'minin. If it is given as a first name and made the name of a person, it is an ism and not a kunya. The laqab is what conveys elevation or lowliness, as when you say "so-and-so the poet" or "so-and-so the clever one," etc.

When one name is applied to several named persons, so that they cannot be distinguished from one another, they must be described by something that distinguishes them. For example, a family that loves the name Muhammad names all its sons Muhammad, so we must say: Muhammad the Elder, Muhammad the Younger, Muhammad the Middle, etc.

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) has a name, a kunya, and a laqab. As for his name, it is Muhammad, and it occurs four times in the Holy Qur'an:

﴿Muhammad is only a messenger; messengers have passed away before him.﴾ (3:144)

﴿Muhammad is not the father of any one of your men, but he is the Messenger of God.﴾ (33:40)

﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of God, and those with him are severe against the disbelievers and merciful among themselves.﴾ (48:29)

﴿And who believe in what has been sent down to Muhammad, and it is the truth from their Lord...﴾ (47:2)

The name Ahmad occurs in one place: ﴿and a messenger coming after me, whose name is Ahmad.﴾ (61:6). We have previously discussed the reason for this naming.

As for his kunya, it is Abu al-Qasim, and his laqab is Messenger of God.

Thus our master, the Messenger of God (ﷺ), fulfilled the three forms of proper naming: the ism, the kunya, and the laqab.

The laqab may also be given by the father, the mother, or the people around a person. It either indicates elevation, out of optimism that he will have a great station, or it indicates lowliness. The latter usually happens to children who are feared to be struck by the evil eye, so they are given a laqab that indicates humiliation and lowliness and the like, such as (al-Fasukha), which they hang on small children for fear of the evil eye.

As for the laqab of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), his Lord, mighty and majestic, chose it for him. It is natural that his laqab (ﷺ) should convey elevation of the highest degree, for this elevation is not only among creatures but also with the Creator. When the Messenger of God was born, his grandfather named him with the dearest of names to God, and said: "I named him Muhammad so that he would be praised on earth and in heaven."(1)

When al-Qasim was born, the Messenger of God was given the kunya by him, and so he was called Abu al-Qasim. When God chose him for prophethood and as an envoy between Himself and creation, He gave him the laqabs Messenger of God and Prophet. These two laqabs carry a great degree of elevation even if they came from a human being. How much more so when they come from God! You set the standards according to your own knowledge and capacities.

So the Messenger (ﷺ) is the Messenger of God and the Prophet of God according to God's standards. He is therefore honored in your eyes, honored in the eyes of the One who sent him, and ﴿God knows best where to place His message.﴾ (6:124)

So the dearest thing to call the Messenger of God by is to say Muhammad, or Abu al-Qasim, or Messenger of God, or the Prophet. When God called His Messenger (ﷺ), He never called him by his name. He did not say "O Muhammad," but with a heart that feels his elevation before God, He said in His address: ﴿O Prophet...﴾ (8:65), and ﴿O Messenger...﴾ (5:41).

If you examine God's calling of the messengers from Adam (peace be upon him) onward, you will not find any messenger called by other than his name except Muhammad (ﷺ). The word "Muhammad" occurs in the Qur'an, but not in an address. It occurs as a statement that Muhammad is the Messenger of God.

Even in speaking about him (ﷺ), God referred to him by his laqab: ﴿There has certainly come to you a messenger from among yourselves...﴾ (9:128)

And He said: ﴿And the Messenger will say, "My Lord, indeed my people have taken this Qur'an as something abandoned."﴾ (25:30)

So in the address, the phrase "O Prophet" and "O Messenger" stands alone, whereas in a statement the name must be mentioned ("Muhammad, Messenger of God"); otherwise how would one know that he is the Messenger of God? So one first informs of him by name and by what he is named.

The Messenger (ﷺ) was addressed as "O Prophet" and "O Messenger" to honor him (ﷺ). When we want to honor someone we call, we precede the name with introductory words. We say: "O my master, so-and-so," "O Your Eminence the Shaykh," "O possessor of honor," etc.

Here the word ayyuha (O) precedes the addressed noun, because a noun with the definite article (al) is not addressed directly except in the case of the Divine Name (Allah), where we say "Ya Allah." It is as if God, glorified is He, was singular even in the address. This is for the address to a single person.

God addressed His Messenger as "O Prophet" and "O Messenger." The Messenger is the envoy between God and His creatures, to convey to them His method by which He wants their lives to proceed. So the Messenger is a conveyer, while the Prophet is also sent by God, glorified is He, but he does not bring a new law. He follows the law of those messengers who came before him. As for him, he is an example and a model of conduct for his people.

Muhammad (ﷺ) combined both qualities: he is a prophet and a messenger, with particular matters that he was commanded to keep and not to convey, and other matters that he was commanded to convey.

It is known from the statements of the scholars that every messenger is a prophet, but not every prophet is a messenger in the technical sense; otherwise they are all sent by God.

The word nabi (prophet) is derived from naba', which is an important news. News comes from humans to humans, but if it comes from the Creator of humans, it is a naba', that is, a great matter that deserves attention. Its root is nubuwwa, which is a high thing rising in the middle of something level.

When you say, "I saw so-and-so today," this is not called naba' but khabar (report). So God said: ﴿About what are they asking one another? About the great news.﴾ (78:1–2), that is, the enormous report that shook the whole world, filled the ears, and shook thrones.

Then God, glorified is He, says to His Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿Fear God﴾ (33:1). We have previously said that Arabic speech is divided into khabar (declarative speech) and insha' (performative speech). Khabar is a verbal relation that, before being uttered, was a mental relation, and after being uttered is a verbal relation. If it has meaning and signification, it is a real relation. Khabar is the speech that is described as true if it corresponds to reality, and as false if it contradicts it.

As for insha' (performative speech), it is the opposite of khabar, that is, speech that is not described as true or false. For example, if you say to a person, "Stop," this is not said to the speaker to be "truthful" or "lying."

So God's words to His Prophet, ﴿Fear God...﴾ (33:1), are a verbal relation from God to His Messenger, to bring about the signification of this command, which is taqwa (God-consciousness). But was the Messenger of God (ﷺ) not God-conscious, that his Lord would command him to be God-conscious?

We say: it is not necessary that the Messenger had disobeyed, so that God would command him to fear Him. Rather, God, glorified is He, creates with His Messenger a statement from the beginning without any prior disobedience. Or it is the first command to taqwa, as when you say to your son at the beginning of the school year: "Work hard and study your lessons," even though you know he is diligent, but it is necessary to establish the principle at the beginning.

Furthermore, an event occurs in three times: past, present, and future. If someone is asked to do something that he is already doing, as in God's words: ﴿O you who have believed, believe in God and His Messenger﴾ (4:136).

God commands them to believe, even though He described them and addressed them with the word "believe," because the meaning is: "You have believed before I spoke to you. This prior belief precedes My speech, and it is past. But I want you to renew your belief, present and future. I want you to renew your faith and to continue in it."

So the meaning of ﴿O Prophet, fear God﴾ (33:1) is: continue your taqwa in the present, as you did before, and continue it in the future, without ever ceasing from it.

Or: taqwa of God is a matter that binds a person to his Lord. God obligated you to certain things and then permitted you certain things of the same kind as the obligations. So when God says to His Messenger, ﴿Fear God﴾ (33:1), it is different from His saying to us, "Fear God," because the command to us is to be God-conscious, meaning: carry out what has been imposed on you. But regarding the Messenger of God, it means: enter the station of excellence (ihsan) and renew it constantly, because the degrees of acceptance from God never end, just as the perfections of His giving never end.

Therefore he (ﷺ) said: "Whoever has two equal days is a loser."(2) That is: whoever has a day equal to his yesterday in nearness to God is a loser. Why? Because the believer should increase in nearness and in love, and in his relationship with God day after day, because God's blessings upon you are continuous and require continuous gratitude and constant praise.

Moreover, God does not suffice from His Messenger with what He suffices from the rest of creation. So taqwa in relation to the Messenger of God is different from taqwa in relation to the rest of creation. Taqwa with regard to the Messenger of God has a wide field, and the Messenger has with God outpourings that never end.

Therefore, when your Lord calls you to prayer five times every day, know that His favor upon you is not repeated but renewed. His giving to you at noon is not His giving to you at afternoon, nor His giving to you at sunset, and so on. Thus taqwa becomes continuous, extended action.

For this reason, the people of goodness warn us against persisting in some act of obedience to God and then falling short of it. They also warn us against vowing to God what we cannot fulfill, because by vowing you impose obedience upon yourself. It is better for you to remain in the station of voluntary acts. If your soul is eager for obedience, increase it, and if you fall short, there is nothing upon you.

Your imposing upon yourself some acts of obedience of the same kind as what God has imposed upon you means: you loved obedience, and worship became sweet to you, so you added to what God had imposed. For example, you say: "I vow to God to pray such-and-such number of rak'ahs, or to give such-and-such in charity, or to give such-and-such of wealth," because you saw in the five prayers illuminations and outpourings from God, so you increased them.

God, glorified is He, asks us, when He calls us to prayer, to hasten to the mosque, even though the whole earth is a mosque and all of it is pure. But the mosque is specified for prayer, so it should be performed in it. As long as you are walking to prayer, you are in prayer. Whoever lives far from the mosque must come to prayer with tranquility and dignity, and must not depart from this bearing even if he arrives late for the opening takbir.

It has been related in a hadith of our master, the Messenger of God: "When the prayer is called, do not come to it running, but come to it walking with tranquility and dignity. Pray what you catch up with, and complete what you missed."(3)

There is both iman (faith) and ihsan (excellence) required. The requirement of iman is what God has made obligatory upon you. In a hadith qudsi it is stated: "My servant does not draw near to Me with anything more beloved to Me than what I have made obligatory upon him."(4)

So if you want to draw near to God, draw near to Him with what He loves, and of the same kind as what He has made obligatory upon you. God commanded you to pray, fast, and give zakat. If these acts of worship have become sweet to you, then increase them beyond what God has made obligatory. When you increase, know that a luminous illumination in worship has touched you, so you say: "God deserves from me more than what He has charged me with." This is the station of ihsan.

(1) Ibn Hisham mentions in al-Sira al-Nabawiyya (1/170) that Amina bint Wahb, or the Messenger of God (ﷺ), used to relate that when she was pregnant with the Messenger of God (ﷺ), she was told: "You have conceived the master of this community. When he falls to the earth, say: 'I seek refuge for him in the One from the evil of every envier,' then name him Muhammad..."

(2) Al-Zarkashi mentioned it in al-Tadhkira fi al-Ahadith al-Mushtahira (p. 138) in full: "Whoever has two equal days is a loser, and whoever has a worse last day is cursed, and whoever is not increasing is in decline, so death is better for him, and whoever longs for Paradise hastens to good deeds, and whoever fears the Fire refrains from desires, and whoever awaits death, pleasures become easy for him, and whoever renounces the world, calamities become easy for him." He said: "The author of Musnad al-Firdaws (al-Daylami) related it from the hadith of Muhammad ibn Suqa, from al-Harith, from Ali, as a marfu' report, and its isnad is weak." Al-Hafiz al-Iraqi said in his takhrij of the hadiths of Ihya' (4/335): "I know of this only in a dream of Abd al-Aziz ibn Abi Rawwad, who said: I saw the Prophet (ﷺ) in a dream and said: 'O Messenger of God, advise me.' He said that (with an addition at its end). It was related by al-Bayhaqi in al-Zuhd..."

(3) Related by Ahmad in his Musnad (2/237, 239, 270), and by Muslim in his Sahih (602), Kitab al-Masajid, from the hadith of Abu Hurayra (may God be pleased with him).

(4) Part of a hadith qudsi, related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (6502) from the hadith of Abu Hurayra, and related by Ahmad in his Musnad (6/256) from the hadith of Aisha. Our Shaykh Muhammad Mutawalli al-Sha'rawi expounded on this hadith in his book al-Ahadith al-Qudsiyya (1/87), edited by us.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 33, verse 2:

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And follow what is revealed to you from your Lord. Indeed, Allah is ever, of what you do, Acquainted.﴾

Here we notice a prohibition between two commands. The first is ﴿O Prophet, fear Allah...﴾ [al-Ahzab], and the other is ﴿And follow what is revealed to you from your Lord...﴾ [al-Ahzab]. Between them is the prohibition: ﴿And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites...﴾ [al-Ahzab]. The placement of this prohibition between these two commands is a natural order, because when you fear Allah you will raise high the methodology of truth, and this harms the people of falsehood and the corrupters who benefit from it. So they will necessarily come to you whispering in your ear to divert you from the methodology of your Lord, and you must therefore refer the matter to what is revealed to you and follow it.

We have said: wahy (revelation) is informing in secrecy. If it is openly done, it is not considered wahy. God, exalted is He, has many means of revelation with all His creation. He reveals, glory be to Him, to inanimate matter, since He is able to address inanimate matter, as in His saying, concerning the earth: ﴿That Day it will report its news, because your Lord has inspired it.﴾ [al-Zalzalah]

He reveals to the bee: ﴿And your Lord inspired to the bee: take for yourself among the mountains, houses, and among the trees and what they construct.﴾ [al-Nahl]

He reveals to someone who is neither a messenger nor a prophet: ﴿And when I inspired to the disciples: believe in Me and in My Messenger...﴾ [al-Ma'idah]

And He said: ﴿And We inspired to the mother of Moses: suckle him...﴾ [al-Qasas]

This is wahy in its general meaning. As for specific wahy, it comes from Allah, exalted is He, to a messenger sent by Him to creation, and it has various modes: sometimes it is by casting into the heart (al-nafth fi al-raw'), sometimes it is by speech whose speaker is not seen and whose source is not known, and sometimes it is through a messenger, an angel who descends with it.

He, exalted is He, says: ﴿It is not for a human that Allah should speak to him except by revelation or from behind a veil or that He sends a messenger...﴾ [al-Shura]

The Noble Qur'an did not come by inspiration (al-ilham) nor by speech from behind the unseen and veils. Rather it came through a messenger, an angel who descended with it upon the Messenger of Allah, and thus the Qur'an was established by this way.

In this matter there must be a meeting between the angelic messenger and the human messenger, for each has his own nature. For them to meet, one of two things must happen: either the human rises to the rank of angelhood so that he receives from it, or the angel descends to the level of humanity so that he can convey to it.

Therefore it came in the hadith that Jibril, peace be upon him, came to the gathering of the Messenger of Allah in human form to teach the people the matters of their religion. (2) When the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was at the beginning of revelation, he would be seized by a shuddering and his forehead would sweat profusely when Jibril brought him the revelation, and this was only due to the meeting of angelhood with humanity. The strain would reach such a degree that he would say: "Cover me, cover me, wrap me, wrap me."

When revelation came to him while he was sitting with his companions and his knee was upon the knee of one of them, he would feel its weight as if it were a mountain, (3) or revelation would come to him while he was on a mount and it would groan. (4) Therefore revelation paused from the Messenger of Allah for a period, so that he might rest from this exertion, and the sweetness of what had been revealed to him would remain, so that he would long for it anew. Afterwards his Lord addressed him: ﴿Did We not expand for you your breast? And We removed from you your burden, which had weighed upon your back, and We raised high for you your mention.﴾ [al-Sharh]

When the goal is precious and the aim is lofty, every effort becomes easy in its pursuit. Revelation returned to the Messenger of Allah after longing, and his Lord addressed him saying: ﴿And the Hereafter is better for you than the first. And your Lord is going to give you, and you will be satisfied.﴾ [al-Duha]

So: the Qur'an was established by revelation through the angelic messenger, and it was not established by inspiration, or casting into the heart, or speech from behind a veil. He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And thus We have revealed to you a spirit of Our command. You did not know what the Book was, nor [what] faith [was]...﴾ [al-Shura]

The wahy here: ﴿and follow what is revealed to you...﴾ [al-Ahzab] from whom? ﴿from your Lord...﴾ [al-Ahzab]. He did not say, for example, "Lord of the creation." Yes, He, glory be to Him, is Lord of all creation, but Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, is the master of creation, so he is Lord of creation all the more so. The word (your Lord) indicates love and concern, and that He, exalted is He, will never forsake you, and His connection to you is only for your good and the good of your community.

Then He, exalted is He, says: ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever, of what you do, Acquainted.﴾ [al-Ahzab] Khabir (the Acquainted) is one who has reached the furthest point of precise knowledge, and from it our saying: "Ask the people of expertise" (ahl al-khibrah). That is, one does not ask those of superficial knowledge. The khabir is the one from whom nothing is hidden.

You notice that the previous verse ended with His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing, Wise.﴾ [al-Ahzab] That is: knowing of what He legislates, wise, placing the matter in its proper place. Here He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever, of what you do, Acquainted.﴾ [al-Ahzab] That is: of what your affair comes to with the legislation, whether by acceptance or rejection. Your Lord will not legislate for you and then leave you; rather He is Acquainted with what you do, even the intentions of the hearts.

Khibrah (expertise) indicates the utmost of knowledge and wide knowledge, and this meaning is clear in His saying, exalted is He, in the story of Luqman: ﴿O my son, indeed it, if it should be the weight of a mustard seed and should be within a rock or within the heavens or within the earth, Allah will bring it forth. Indeed, Allah is Subtle, Acquainted.﴾ [Luqman]

Khibrah indicates wide knowledge that does not miss any detail however small, and lutf (subtlety) is penetration into things however fine they may be. We have said: the thing, as it is subtle, is also severe.

It is as if the Truth, glory be to Him, is saying to His Messenger: be at ease. However you are confronted by your opponents, and however they conspire against you, your Lord is behind you and will not abandon you. These opponents are My creation, and I give them thinking faculties, reasoning faculties, and scheming faculties, and I will give you victory over them at every stage of their plotting against you.

Therefore they were not able to overcome you in debate or argument, nor were they able against you when they plotted to strike you with one blow from one man, so that your blood would be scattered among the tribes. You came out from among them unharmed, while they threw dust upon their heads. Even when they sought help against you through sorcery and the jinn, I informed you of what they were plotting, and did not hand you over to their scheming.

1 Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir (7/3575): "The common reading is with the ta' as address (tana'lamuna... i.e., ta'malun), which is the choice of Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim. Al-Sulami, Abu 'Amr and Ibn Ishaq read ya'malun with the ya' as third person," meaning that Allah is:
- Acquainted with what you do of following what is revealed to us from our Lord in conveying His messages.
- Acquainted with what the disbelievers and hypocrites do of plotting against Islam and attempting to turn us away from following our religion.
2 Agreed upon; al-Bukhari recorded it in his Sahih (50), and likewise Muslim in his Sahih (8), from the hadith of Umar ibn al-Khattab: that Jibril came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, among his companions in the form of "a man of very white clothing, of very black hair, upon whom no trace of travel was seen, and whom none of them recognized."
3 Zayd ibn Thabit (the scribe of revelation) said: Allah sent down revelation upon His Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, while his thigh was upon my thigh, and it became so heavy upon me that I feared my thigh would be crushed. Recorded by al-Bukhari in suspended form (mu'allaq), with a definitive attribution, in the Book of Prayer, chapter "What is mentioned about the thigh," and he connected it in his tafsir of Surat al-Nisa'.
4 From Asma' bint Yazid, who said: "I was holding the rein of al-'Adba', the she-camel of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, when al-Ma'idah was revealed to him in its entirety, and it nearly broke the shoulder of the she-camel from its weight." Recorded by Imam Ahmad in his Musnad (6/455).

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿And put your trust in Allah; and sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs.﴾

That is: beware lest you think that any one of these will help you in your affair, or that he possesses for you harm or benefit. So do not put good trust in their commands or their prohibitions, and do not rely upon them in anything; rather, rely upon Allah alone.

Here we must distinguish between tawakkul (trust in God) and tawakkul's counterfeit, tawakul (reliance on others, or passive neglect of means). Tawakkul is that you are powerless in some matter, so you go to one who is stronger than you in it and depend on him to accomplish it for you, on condition that you exhaust in it the means Allah has created for you. Tawakkul, then, is that the limbs act and the hearts rely upon Allah.

Our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), gave us an illustrative example of this matter with the bird, saying: "If you were to rely upon Allah with the reliance due to Him, He would provide for you as He provides for the bird: it goes out hungry in the morning and returns full at evening."

As for tawakul, it is that you reject the means which Allah has provided for you, and refrain from taking them, and say: "I have put my trust in Allah," when in truth you have not exhausted the means that your Lord has made available to you. If the means become difficult for you, do not despair, for you have a Lord who is stronger than the means, since He, glorified is He, is the Creator of the means.

Therefore, many people say: "I supplicated to Allah and He did not answer me." We say: Yes, you have spoken truly, and Allah has spoken truly with you, for Allah the Exalted has given you the means and you neglected them. When you have exhausted your means, be certain that your Lord will respond to you when you turn to Him.

And recite His words, the Exalted: ﴿Is not He who responds to the distressed one when he calls upon Him and removes the evil...?﴾ (An-Naml 27:62). The mudtarr (the one in dire need) is the one whose means have failed him and gone beyond the bounds of his power, as happened to our master Musa (peace be upon him) when Pharaoh and his soldiers besieged him, until the people of Musa said: ﴿Indeed, we are overtaken!﴾ (Ash-Shu'ara 26:61).

Yes, they are overtaken, for the sea is before them and the enemy behind them; this is human opinion and the reality of the matter. But Musa had another outlet, so he said: "Never! Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me" (Ash-Shu'ara 26:62). Musa said this out of a store of faith and confidence that Allah would respond to him.

Some say: "I supplicated to Allah for such and such, and I took all the means, yet He did not respond to me." We say: Yes, but you are not in dire need; rather, you supplicate to Allah out of luxury, like one who lives, for example, in an apartment and asks Allah to live in a villa or a palace. In this condition, you are not in dire need.

Then the Truth, glorified is He, mentions the ground of tawakkul upon Allah, saying: ﴿And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs﴾ (Al-Ahzab 33:3). That is: it suffices you that Allah be your Disposer of affairs, for nothing resists Him and nothing is impossible for Him.

I will relate to you a story that actually happened to us. We were walking with some brothers and saw a blind man who wanted to cross the street. We said to a companion of ours: "Go and take him by the hand." So he went down and led him across the street, then said to him: "Where are you going?" He said: "To house number such-and-such on this street." Our companion took out ten pounds from his pocket and placed them in the man's hand. When the man grasped the ten-pound note, he did not turn to the giver; rather, he raised his face to the sky and said: "Nothing is ever impossible for You." Then he said to our companion: "My son, return me to where I was! You have fulfilled the need for which I was striving!"

Yes: ﴿And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs﴾ (Al-Ahzab 33:3), for means do not overpower Him, and nothing turns Him from His will: ﴿What is with you will end, and what is with Allah remains﴾ (An-Nahl 16:96).

There is another point regarding tawakkul that we should be mindful of: if you rely upon someone to accomplish a matter for you, then be sure that he will live long enough to fulfil your need. How can you rely upon a person and attach to him all your wealth, and in the morning you hear his death announced: "So-and-so has died"?

Therefore, one should rely only upon Allah, the Living who does not die: ﴿And put your trust in the Ever-Living who does not die, and glorify Him with His praise...﴾ (Al-Furqan 25:58), and seek the help of Allah's trusteeship over everything: ﴿And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs﴾ (Al-Ahzab 33:3).

1 al-mukhmasa: hunger, which is the emptiness of the belly from food due to hunger. The meaning of the hadith: the birds go out at dawn while hungry, and return at evening while their bellies are full. [Lisan al-Arab, root: kh-m-s]

2 Recorded by Ahmad in his Musnad (1/30, 25), Ibn Majah in his Sunan (4164), and al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan (2344) from the hadith of Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), and he said: "a hadith hasan sahih."

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Allah has not made for any man two hearts within his breast. Nor has He made your wives whom you divorce by zihar your mothers, nor has He made your adopted sons your sons. That is your saying by your mouths. But Allah says the truth, and He guides to the way.﴾

This verse is connected to the verses before it. Almighty Allah mentioned two camps: a camp that must be obeyed, so He said to His Messenger, ﴿O Prophet, fear Allah...﴾ [al-Ahzab], and He said, ﴿And follow what is revealed to you from your Lord...﴾ [al-Ahzab]. Between them is another camp, from which the Messenger of Allah was forbidden to obey: ﴿And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites...﴾ [al-Ahzab].

So here we are before two camps: one that represents the truth in its clearest meanings and forms, and another that represents falsehood. The heart has here a role that admits no ambiguity. Either it inclines to and sides with the people of truth, or it inclines to the side of falsehood. Since you face two contradictory matters that cannot coexist, the truth must prevail, because Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Allah has not made for any man two hearts within his breast...﴾ [al-Ahzab].

It is either the truth or falsehood. You cannot fear Allah and obey the disbelievers and hypocrites, because the heart that inclines and dominates is one heart.

It is known that the heart is the most important organ of the human body. When a person falls ill, for example, the doctor prescribes a medicine. The medicine is taken by mouth and passes through the digestive system, and it needs time to be absorbed into the body. If the case is more serious, he prescribes an intramuscular injection, so the medicine pours into the body directly. If the illness is more severe, he gives an intravenous injection. Why?

So that the required medicine reaches the blood directly, ready, and the heart pumps it to all the organs in the shortest time. Thus the blood is what carries the properties of healing and well-being to the whole body, and the heart is the (motor) that performs this task. Therefore you must keep it in good condition, by filling it with the truth so that falsehood does not corrupt it.

We have already explained that one space cannot contain two things at the same time, so what of two contradictory things? We illustrated this process with the empty bottle: if you want to fill it with water, the air must first come out so that the water can enter its place.

It is the same with meanings. Truth and falsehood never gather in one heart, and you cannot make one heart for the truth and another for falsehood, because the Creator made for you one heart and limited it so that it holds only your faith in your Lord. So do not crowd it with anything else.

It is related that there was among the Arabs a man called Jamil ibn Asad al-Fihri, who was famous for eloquence and intelligence. He used to say: "I have two hearts; with one of them I understand as much as Muhammad understands." Then it happened that Abu Sufyan saw him after the defeat following Badr, and said to him: "O Jamil, what happened to the people?" He said: "Some of them are killed and some have fled." He said: "What is wrong with you, that I see you like this?" He said: "What about me?" He said: "There is a sandal in your hand and a sandal on your foot." He said: "By Allah, I thought they were on my foot." Abu Sufyan laughed and said to him: "Then where are your two hearts?"

If the heart is the pump that pumps blood to all the limbs and organs, carrying nourishment, healing and well-being, then likewise, when the beliefs of goodness settle in the heart, the blood carries them to the limbs and organs, and they turn to obedience to Allah. The foot strives toward good, the eye looks only at what is lawful, the ear hears speech and follows the best of it, and the tongue speaks only truth.

So all the limbs produce only the truth that they have absorbed from the energies of goodness in the heart.

Therefore our master, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, teaches us this lesson, saying: "Indeed, in the body there is a piece of flesh; if it is sound, the whole body is sound, and if it is corrupted, the whole body is corrupted. Verily, it is the heart." (7)

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, takes from the matter of two contradictions gathering in one heart an introduction to speak of the matters of contradictions that were widespread among the Arabs, and He says, glory be to Him: ﴿Allah has not made for any man two hearts within his breast, nor has He made your wives whom you divorce by zihar your mothers...﴾ [al-Ahzab]

It was common in the Jahiliyyah that when a man disliked his wife, he would say to her: "You are to me like the back of my mother." It is known that the back of the mother is forbidden to the son with a permanent prohibition, so they considered this word to have the effect of divorce. When Islam came, it did not make it a divorce, but made for it an expiation (kaffarah) for a lie, because the wife is not your mother. It specified this expiation as either: freeing a slave, or feeding sixty needy persons, or fasting sixty days. (8)

This matter is addressed in the surah (Qad sami'a): ﴿Those of you who make zihar from their wives, they are not their mothers. Their mothers are only those who gave birth to them, and indeed they say an objectionable word and a falsehood...﴾ [al-Mujadilah], meaning a lie, because a wife cannot be a mother.

So the Truth, glory be to Him, brought a contradiction and introduced another contradiction within it. Just as one heart cannot contain obedience to Allah and obedience to the disbelievers and hypocrites, likewise a wife can never be a mother; she is either a mother or a wife.

Likewise, there was found among the Arabs another contradiction concerning adoption. A man would take a fancy to a small boy, or see in him signs of nobility, and adopt him. The boy would become his son, mixing into his household as his child, inheriting from him as his own child inherits, and having all the rights of a son.

This is contradictory too, like the previous one. Just as a man cannot have two hearts, and just as a wife cannot in any case be a mother, so the adopted child cannot be a son. So He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Nor has He made your adopted sons your sons...﴾ [al-Ahzab].

The *da'i* (adopted son, pl. *ad'iya'*) is the one whom you claim to be a son while he is not a son. This was widespread among the Arabs. Allah, glory be to Him, willed to abolish this custom, and similarly the matter of zihar. The Qur'an abolished these customs and said: place everything in its proper place. So it made an expiation for zihar and forbade adoption in this form.

When the Truth, glory be to Him, wants to annul a ruling, the one who makes the claim presents himself to have it applied before the people. Therefore He made our master, the Messenger of Allah, begin with himself, and annul the adoption that he had.

You know that our master, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, married Lady Khadijah, and she had a standing with the Messenger of Allah. Hakim ibn Hizam (9) bought for her a slave from the slave market, Zayd ibn Harithah, who was from the Banu Kalb. Thieves had stolen him from his family, and they claimed he was a slave and sold him. Then Lady Khadijah gave him as a gift to our master, the Messenger of Allah, so he became a freedman (mawla) of the Messenger of Allah, serving him for several years. And what of one who is in the service of the Messenger of Allah?

Zayd loved the Messenger of Allah and loved serving him. He said of the Prophet's treatment of him ﷺ: "I served the Messenger of Allah for ten years, and he never said to me about something I had done: why did you do it, nor about something I had left: why did you leave it." (10)

One day, a man of the Banu Kalb saw him in the streets of Makkah and informed his family. Zayd's father hurried to Makkah searching for his son, and they pointed him to him, that he was with Muhammad. He went to our master, the Messenger of Allah, informed him of the news of his son, and asked him to return with him to the Banu Kalb.

But the Messenger of Allah would not abandon his servant whom he loved so much. He said to his father: "Let him choose. If he chooses you, take him, and if he chooses me, then I am his father." When they gave him the choice, our master Zayd said: "By Allah, I would never choose anyone over the Messenger of Allah."

Then the Messenger of Allah wished to reward him for this position and his adherence to serving him, so he adopted him as the Arabs adopt, and afterwards they called him: Zayd ibn Muhammad. (11)

When Almighty Allah wanted to annul adoption, He began with the adopted son of the Messenger of Allah, so that he would be the example for others in this matter. How did Allah, exalted, annul this sonship?

The Messenger of Allah had married Zayd to his paternal aunt's daughter, Zaynab bint Jahsh, sister of Abdullah ibn Jahsh. The Messenger of Allah had labored to persuade Abdullah and Zaynab to this marriage, which Zaynab rejected (12). She said: "How can I marry Zayd when he is a slave and I am a Qurashi noblewoman?"

Then she married him to please the Messenger of Allah, in obedience to His saying: ﴿It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decided a matter, that they should have any choice about their affair...﴾ [al-Ahzab, 36].

But after the marriage she looked down on him, saying that she was of the nobility and he of the slaves. Zayd disliked this and could not bear it, so he wished to divorce her. He went to the Messenger of Allah and complained to him of what Zaynab had done, and presented to him his desire to divorce her.

The Messenger of Allah said to him: "Keep your wife for yourself." He returned to him again and he said: "Keep your wife for yourself." Zayd returned a second time, and then the Messenger of Allah knew that their desire for divorce and their aversion to married life was a matter decreed by Allah for a wisdom and a new legislative purpose. Allah willed that hatred be cast between Zayd and Zaynab. Zaynab's hatred of Zayd was arrogance and haughtiness, and Zayd's hatred of Zaynab was self-respect.

In order that Almighty Allah annul the Messenger of Allah's adoption of Zayd, He decreed that the Messenger of Allah marry Zaynab after her divorce from Zayd. It is known that the wife of a son is forbidden to his father, so the marriage of our master, the Messenger of Allah, to Zaynab means that Zayd is not the son of the Messenger of Allah, and it annuls the custom of adoption and its consequences.

The Messenger of Allah sensed something within himself and hesitated over this marriage, fearing that people would say: "Muhammad instructed Zayd to divorce Zaynab so that he himself could marry her," as some orientalists say now, and that he ﷺ harbored love for Zaynab in his heart. All of these are fabrications against the Messenger of Allah. The one who loves a woman does not strive to have her married to another, and when her husband wants to divorce her, he does not say to him: "Keep your wife for yourself."

Then it is not proper for anyone to delve into what the Messenger of Allah concealed in himself, whether he was a lover or one enamored. Rather, look at what Allah has revealed, for what Allah has revealed is what the Messenger of Allah concealed. Recite: ﴿And you concealed within yourself that which Allah is to disclose, and you feared the people, while Allah has more right that you fear Him...﴾ [al-Ahzab, 37].

So what the Messenger of Allah was concealing was that he feared the Arabs would speak about it and say about it what is not fitting for him in this matter.

And He, exalted, says: ﴿So when Zayd had no longer any need of her, We married her to you...﴾ [al-Ahzab, 37]. Why? ﴿So there will not be upon the believers any discomfort concerning the wives of their adopted sons...﴾ [al-Ahzab, 37].

Thus the Truth, glory be to Him, established the principle of annulling adoption in the person of the Messenger of Allah.

When the Truth, glory be to Him, annuls the custom of adoption, He is annulling a blameworthy custom that undermines the building of the family, destroys its entity, and leads to the mixing of lineages and the loss of rights. The adopted child lives in the family as its son; the mother treats him as her son while he is a stranger to her, and likewise the daughter treats him as her brother while he is not. There is in this corruption that is not hidden from anyone.

Also, how can the father whom Allah made the direct cause of your existence be denied by you, so that you transfer this causal relationship to someone other than its owner? When you deny the causal sonship to your father, it becomes easy for you then to deny the originator who created you first. Why not, since you have dared to deny the favor?

Likewise, one who denies causal sonship dares to attribute things to other than their owners, attributing worship to one not deserving it and creation to other than the Creator.

Otherwise, why does the Truth constantly urge us to be dutiful to parents? And why did He join the worship of Himself with good treatment of parents in more than one place in His Mighty Book, saying, glory be to Him: {And worship Allah...}

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 33, verse 5:

Then the Truthful One, glorified is He, says:

﴿Call them by [the names of] their fathers; that is more just in the sight of Allah. But if you do not know their fathers, then they are your brothers in religion and your clients. And there is no blame upon you for that in which you have erred, but [only for] what your hearts intended. And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ (5)

The meaning of ﴿Call them by [the names of] their fathers…﴾ (5) [al-Ahzab] is: say, "Zayd ibn Harithah." But how can this crown and this honour that the Master of Messengers, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, bestowed upon him be taken away from Zayd? Yes, this is hard on Zayd, may Allah be pleased with him, but it is ﴿more just in the sight of Allah…﴾ (5) [al-Ahzab], not in your sight.

And ﴿aqsat﴾ (more just) is a comparative form (af'al al-tafdil). We say "this is qist (just) and this is aqsat (more just)," like "adl (just) and a'dal (more just). The meaning of that is that what the Messenger of Allah chose regarding Zayd's attribution to himself is considered a human justice, in that the Prophet ﷺ felt the bond of sonship and became a father to the one he chose and preferred over his own father.

But the Truthful One, glorified is He, wants for us the more just, and the more just is that we call sons by their fathers. ﴿But if you do not know their fathers, then they are your brothers in religion and your clients…﴾ (5), i.e., we identify them as our brothers in religion.

The meaning of mawali (clients) is the servants and helpers, those whom they used to call "slaves." So a child whose father we do not know is a brother of yours in Allah; you choose for him a general name. We say, for example, regarding Zayd: Zayd ibn Abdullah, for we are all servants of Allah, exalted is He.

Lineage is established by two things: by reason and by the Shari'ah. A man who marries in a lawful marriage and begets a child, that child is his son both naturally (kawnan) and legally (shar'an). If a woman commits adultery, God forbid, on her husband's bed, the child is the husband's son legally, not naturally, because the legal principle says: "The child belongs to the bed, and for the fornicator is the stone"(1).

Likewise in the case of a wife who remarries after her husband's death or after divorce, but gives birth within six months, here there arises the doubt that the child belongs to the first husband; therefore he is considered a son legally, not naturally, because he was born on his bed.

But if the child comes from fornication, God forbid, outside the bed of marriage, then he is his son naturally, not legally; therefore we call him "an illegitimate son."

Also, in the saying of the Exalted: ﴿That is more just in the sight of Allah…﴾ (5), there is an honouring of the Prophet ﷺ. For had He said, "That is just," the Prophet's act would have been injustice and oppression. But "more just" means that the Prophet's act is just and fair.

And His saying: ﴿And there is no blame upon you for that in which you have erred, but [only for] what your hearts intended…﴾ (5) releases us from great hardship in this matter. We often hear, and say to those who are not our children: "O my son," as an expression of affection and tenderness, and we say to elderly people: "O my father, so-and-so," out of respect for them.

So the Truthful One protects us and relieves us from hardship and sin, for we say these words not intending true fatherhood, but intending the glorification and honouring of the elders and the affection and tenderness towards the young. So there is no sin or fault upon you in this matter if you err in it. Error is failing to reach the right, but without intention.

And if our Lord, blessed and exalted is He, has lifted hardship from us and permitted us idle oaths even in swearing by His Essence, glorified is He, saying: ﴿Allah will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths, but He will hold you accountable for what your hearts have intended in the oaths you have sworn…﴾ (89) [al-Ma'idah], then how would He not relieve us of hardship in this matter?

Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful﴾ (5) [al-Ahzab]. We have previously said that when the verb is attributed to the Truthful One, glorified is He, it is released from time; there is no past, present or future with Allah, for He is the Creator of time.

Therefore we say ﴿And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful﴾ (5) [al-Ahzab], meaning: He was and still is Forgiving and Merciful. For difference in the time of an event arises only from one subject to changes, whereas the Truthful One is not subject to alteration.

Therefore we fear the one subject to changes, for he is fickle. The people of knowledge say: "Change for the sake of your Lord," meaning: from deviation to uprightness, for Allah does not change for your sake; you change for the sake of Allah. Allah does not change for anyone's sake. Since the Truthful One was Forgiving and Merciful, and He does not change, He will therefore remain Forgiving and Merciful.

You notice in the style of the Qur'an that it always pairs these two attributes, Forgiving and Merciful, because forgiveness is the removal of the punishment for sin, and mercy is the coming of a new kindness after the sin that was forgiven. It is like finding a thief stealing in your house: you may take him to the police, or you may pardon him and let him go on his way and conceal him, and it is in your power to help him with what you can, so that he may be sustained in life. This is mercy towards him and kindness to him after forgiveness.

This matter has been addressed in His saying: ﴿And if you punish, then punish with the like of that with which you were punished﴾ (126) [al-Nahl]. This directive lays down for us the first foundation of forgiveness, for you can never fully establish this equivalence, nor can you ever guarantee, when you punish, that you will punish only in kind and not transgress; therefore you resort to the side of forgiveness, so as not to enter yourself into a maze of new transgression that would make retaliation due from you.

We have previously related the story of the usurer who stipulated with his debtor that if he did not repay what was owed by the appointed time, he would take a pound of his flesh. When the time passed, the usurer complained to the judge and mentioned the conditions between them, and the judge upheld his condition. But Allah inspired someone to say to the usurer: "Yes, take a pound of his flesh, but in a single stroke; if you exceed it or fall short, we will repay it from your own flesh." Thereupon the usurer retracted and abandoned his condition.

Thus: the Shari'ah permitted you retaliation in kind to make this stage difficult to carry out, then the Truthful One opens for you the door of pardon and forgiveness in the second stage: ﴿And if you pardon and overlook and forgive, then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ (14) [al-Taghabun].

Then He explains it with another aspect, saying: ﴿And those who restrain anger and pardon the people, and Allah loves the doers of good﴾ (134) [Al 'Imran].

The meaning of restraining anger (kazm al-ghayz) is that I do not react with an angry emotion that results in a vengeful response; I keep my anger in my heart and suppress it within myself. This is the first stage. The second is that you bring out what is in yourself of rage and anger, and you are forbearing and pardon.

Then the third stage is that you rise to the rank of doing good, so you do good to one who has wronged you. This is mercy. Mercy is that a person inclines with kindness toward one who is incapable of it; if the matter is the reverse, it is not called mercy, as when a servant inclines with kindness toward his master.

These are examples in which mercy came after forgiveness, and this is the principle in the matter. But mercy may also come before forgiveness: for example, you seize the thief who is stealing and you feel that he was compelled to it and bears no marks of criminality, so your heart softens toward him, your hand reaches out to him with help, then you release him and pardon him. Here mercy comes first and forgiveness follows it.

After that, someone may say: what was Zayd's position after Allah annulled adoption, so that Zayd ibn Harithah became (no longer) Zayd ibn Muhammad? How is he after this blessing has been taken from him and this honour denied him? In addition to that, he met the harm of the slanderers and the tongues of those who sowed enmity in his breast and set him against the Messenger of Allah, though it was he who had been chosen over his own father.

There is no doubt that the store of faith with which Zayd was armed raised him above all this, for the love of the Messenger of Allah had permeated his heart, and his mind was firmly set upon the saying of the Exalted: ﴿It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decreed a matter, that they should have any choice about their affair…﴾ (36) [al-Ahzab].

Then the verses come to make clear to the people: you are not more compassionate to Zayd than Muhammad, for Muhammad ﷺ is closer to the believers than their own selves, not Zayd alone.

(1) This is a hadith of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ related by Ahmad in his Musnad (1/239, 280, 386, 409), and likewise by Muslim in his Sahih (1458), Kitab al-Radâ' (Book of Suckling), Bab al-Walad lil-Firash (10), from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him.

The Almighty then says:

﴿The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves, and his wives are their mothers. And those of blood-relationship are nearer to one another in the Book of Allah than [are] the believers and the emigrants, except that you do [some] kindness to your allies. That is inscribed in the Book.﴾ (6)

So the meaning is: if the Prophet (ﷺ) is closer to all the believers than their own selves, then what about Zayd? In that case, you are not more compassionate toward Zayd than Allah, nor than the Messenger of Allah. And if you look at the distinction that was taken from Zayd when he became Zayd ibn Harithah after having been Zayd ibn Muhammad—

Then why do you shut your eyes to a greater excellence that Zayd attained from Allah the Exalted, when his name was mentioned explicitly in His Qur'an and in His Mighty Book, which is recited and worshipped by its recitation until the Day of Resurrection? What distinction is greater than this? His Exalted saying: ﴿So when Zayd had no longer any need for her, We married her to you﴾ (37) [al-Ahzab] is a statement by which the mention of Zayd is made eternal, and thus Allah compensated Zayd for what had escaped him of having his name changed.

As for His Exalted saying: ﴿The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves…﴾ (6) [al-Ahzab]: what is meant by this priority of the Prophet (ﷺ)?

They said: it is a series of elevations in the sphere of goodness: first toward oneself, then toward others. A person first does good to himself, then to close kin, then to distant kin, then to strangers. Therefore the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Begin with yourself, then with those you support" (1).

And they say: people's homelands differ according to the differences of their aspirations. A man's homeland is himself: he sees everything as for himself and does not see himself as belonging to anyone. Another's homeland is his children and family. Another extends beyond the roots to the branches. Another's homeland is his town or village. And another's homeland is the whole world and all of humanity.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) extended his goodness to all of humanity in general and to the believers in particular. Therefore, when a man of his community died while owing a debt and leaving no means of repayment, the Prophet (ﷺ) would not perform the funeral prayer for him, saying: "Pray over your brother" (2).

The superficial view here says: what was his fault if he died owing a debt? And why did the Messenger not pray over him?

They said: the Messenger did not withhold the prayer; he said "Pray over your brother" because he said in another hadith: "Whoever takes people's wealth intending to repay it, Allah will repay on his behalf; whoever takes it intending not to repay it, Allah will destroy him" (3).

As for one who died without paying what he owed, it is most likely that he did not intend to repay, so I do not pray over him. But when the saying of Allah the Exalted was revealed, ﴿The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves…﴾ (6) [al-Ahzab], the Messenger of Allah became responsible for the debts of any Muslim who died in debt, and the Messenger would pay on his behalf. This is the meaning of ﴿The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves…﴾ (6) [al-Ahzab]: the Prophet is closer to the Muslim than his own self.

Furthermore, did our master the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) not say before Umar: "None of you believes until I am more beloved to him than his own self, his wealth, and all people"? And out of Umar's sincerity toward himself, he said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah, you are more beloved to me than my family and my wealth, but [not] my own self..." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "By He in whose hand my soul is, none of you believes until I am more beloved to him than his own self" (4).

When Umar saw that the matter was a binding resolve, he perceived the correct answer: surely Allah caused His Messenger to express a love other than the love I know. It is the rational love: Muhammad (ﷺ) is more beloved to him than his own self. A person loves bitter medicine with his intellect, not with his emotions. Just as you love a clever child even if he is the son of your enemy, while your own son you love with your emotions, and you love whoever praises him even if he is a foolish, backward person.

Famous among the Arabs is the story of the wealthy man whom Allah blessed with a backward son. The son grew up in this state until he became a man. Those seeking gifts would come to him, praising this son to please his father and hoping for his generosity, although they knew his imbecility and backwardness. Until one of them was in need, and they advised him to go to this wealthy man, informing him of the weak point in his son.

Indeed, the man went to seek assistance, and sat with this wealthy man in the hall. Suddenly the son came down the stairs like a child at play, with no hiding the signs of foolishness and backwardness. The man looked at the master of the house and said: "Is this your son whom people praise?" He said: "Yes." He said: "May Allah relieve you of him, and provision is with Allah."

And His Exalted saying: ﴿and his wives are their mothers…﴾ (6) [al-Ahzab]: that is, the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) are mothers of the believers. Accordingly, Khadijah (may Allah be pleased with her) is a mother to the Messenger in this sense, since he was the first of the believers. Therefore she did not treat him as a wife treats a husband, but as a tender mother treats her child.

Do you not see how she would embrace him and cradle him when he first encountered the severity of revelation and the descent of the angel upon him? And how she would reassure him? Had she been a young girl, the matter would have been different, and he would have been suspected in his reason. So the Messenger at this stage needed a compassionate mother, not a young wife of little experience.

His wives (ﷺ) are considered mothers of the believers in him, because Allah the Exalted said, addressing the believers: ﴿And it is not for you to harm the Messenger of Allah or to marry his wives after him, ever.﴾ (53) [al-Ahzab]. Why? Because men who contest over a woman always harbor enmity and rancor among themselves.

A man divorces his wife while resenting her, but when another marries her she becomes sweet in his eyes again, so he hates whoever marries her. All these matters are unfitting with the person of the Messenger of Allah, and it is not proper for one who was a wife of the Messenger of Allah to become a bed for another, ever. Therefore Allah made them mothers of all the believers, and this sanctity does not extend from the mothers of the believers to their daughters; whoever has a daughter may marry her to whomever she wishes.

Thus it is not permissible for a person who believes in the Messenger of Allah and honors him as he deserves to succeed him in his wife.

Accordingly, plurality of wives in the Jahiliyyah had no fixed limit: a man could marry as many women as he wished. When Islam came, it wished to limit the number in this matter, so it commanded that a man keep four of them and separate from the rest (5). That is, he may not combine more than four wives.

As for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he kept nine wives. Orientalists have taken this as a point against the Messenger of Allah and the law of Allah, as have some Muslims who follow their line.

We say to them: you are foolish, and whoever follows your path is foolish like you, because this exception for the Messenger of Allah came from the saying of Allah to him: ﴿It is not lawful for you [to marry] women after [these], nor to exchange them for other wives…﴾ (52) [al-Ahzab].

That is: if any of them dies, you may not marry another in her place; even if they all die, it is not lawful for you to marry others besides them. Whereas his other community members may marry in place of one of their wives if she dies, or if he divorces her, and he may divorce whomever he wishes and marry whomever he wishes, on condition that he does not combine more than four. So upon whom has this ruling been made narrow? Upon the Messenger of Allah? Or upon his community? Therefore do not wrong the Messenger of Allah.

Moreover, these people should distinguish between an exception in the number and an exception in the thing counted. That the Messenger of Allah is content with these nine and does not go beyond them to others means the exception here concerns the counted thing: if this counted group ends, it is not lawful for him to take another. Had the exception been in the number, what you say would be permissible for you.

On another side: when a man keeps four and separates from the rest of his wives, they may marry others. But what of the wives of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) if he divorced five of them, and they are the mothers of the believers, and none of his community may marry them? Therefore the good and righteousness lie in the wives of the Messenger remaining under his marriage.

And since ﴿The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves…﴾ (6) [al-Ahzab], it is likewise necessary that the believers be closer to the Messenger than their own selves, so that they return this tribute to him, such that when he commands them, they obey him.

Then the Exalted says: ﴿And those of blood-relationship are nearer to one another in the Book of Allah than [are] the believers and the emigrants﴾ (6) [al-Ahzab].

The word ﴿those of blood-relationship (ulu al-arham)﴾ is derived from ar-rahim (the womb), the place of the fetus in its mother's belly, and it means relatives. Allah made them closer to one another because the earliest Muslims, when they emigrated to Madinah, left behind in Makkah their families, wealth, and homes, and the Helpers of the Messenger did not wish to leave them with hearts inclined toward wives.

Out of their great preference for their emigrant brethren, one of them would offer his brother the emigrant to divorce one of his wives so that he could marry her (6). This is a form of preference that the whole history of humanity has not witnessed, for a person will give his friend the most precious thing he possesses, except the matter of a woman; what these Companions did is a unique form of preference.

When the Prophet (ﷺ) established brotherhood between the emigrants and the Helpers, this brotherhood required that the emigrant inherit from his Helper brother. When Allah strengthened Islam and the emigrants found a way to make a living, Allah the Exalted willed that matters return to their natural course, and there was no longer any necessity for the emigrant to inherit from his Helper brother.

So the verses decreed that those of blood-relationship are closer to one another in the matter of inheritance. He the Exalted said: ﴿And those of blood-relationship are nearer to one another in the Book of Allah than [are] the believers and the emigrants…﴾ (6) [al-Ahzab]. Thus the affairs of the emigrants were settled, each knew his path and arranged his affairs, and relatives in this case are closer to this inheritance.

His Exalted saying: ﴿And those of blood-relationship…﴾ (6) [al-Ahzab] is an alert that a person must preserve the flesh of kinship even from Adam (peace be upon him), for when you reflect on the creation of man, you find that we are all from Adam, not from Adam and Hawwa' alone.

It is related that a chamberlain entered upon Mu'awiyah and said: "A man is at the door who says he is your brother." Mu'awiyah said: "How is it you do not know my brothers, when you are my chamberlain?" He said: "So he said." He said: "Admit him." When the man entered, Mu'awiyah asked him: "Which of my brothers are you?" He said: "Your brother from Adam." Mu'awiyah said: "Yes, a severed kinship. By Allah, I will be the first to join it."

His Exalted saying: ﴿except that you do [some] kindness to your allies﴾ (6) [al-Ahzab]: Allah leaves open the door of kindness to the emigrants. Whoever of them is present at a distribution should be given a share of it voluntarily, as came in His saying: ﴿And when the division takes place, if [other] relatives, orphans, and the needy are present, provide for them from it and speak to them words of kindness﴾ (8) [an-Nisa'].

His saying: ﴿That is inscribed in the Book﴾ (6) [al-Ahzab]: that is, in Umm al-Kitab, the Preserved Tablet, or "the Book" meaning the Qur'an.

1 From Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to a man of Banu Udhrah: "Begin with yourself and give charity to it. If something remains, then to your family. If something remains after your family, then to your relatives. If something remains after your relatives, then here and here." Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih (997), Kitab az-Zakat, Bab al-Ibtida' fi an-Nafaqah bin-Nafs. As for the phrase "then with those you support" (thumma bi-man ta'ul), it appears in another hadith also in Sahih Muslim (1034), Kitab az-Zakat, from Hakim ibn Hizam, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The best charity is that given out of surplus wealth; the upper hand is better than the lower hand; and begin with those you support."

2 From Abu Qatadah, who said: a man was brought to the Prophet (ﷺ) so that he might pray over him. The Prophet said: "Pray over your companion, for he has a debt." Abu Qatadah said: "It is on me." He (ﷺ) said: "Is it with full settlement?" He said: "With full settlement." So he prayed over him. Narrated by at-Tirmidhi in his Sunan (1069), who said it is a hasan sahih hadith.

3 Narrated by Imam Ahmad in his Musnad (2/361, 417), al-Bukhari in his Sahih (2387), and Ibn Majah in his Sunan (2411), from Abu Hurayrah.

4 From the grandfather of Zahrah ibn Ma'bad, who said: We were with the Prophet (ﷺ) while he was holding the hand of Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him). He said: "By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, you are more beloved to me than everything except my own self." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "By He in whose hand my soul is, none of you believes until I am more beloved to him than his own self." He said: "Then by Allah, you are now more beloved to me than my own self." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Now, O Umar." Narrated by Imam Ahmad in his Musnad (4/336).

5 From Ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both): Ghaylan ibn Salamah ath-Thaqafi embraced Islam while having ten wives in the Jahiliyyah, and they embraced Islam with him. The Prophet (ﷺ) commanded him to choose four of them. Narrated by at-Tirmidhi in his Sunan (1128) and Ibn Majah in his Sunan (1953), connected (mawsul). Imam Malik narrated it in his Muwatta' as mursal from Ibn Shihab az-Zuhri with the wording: "Keep four of them and separate from the rest."

6 This occurred with Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, an emigrant from Makkah, and Sa'd ibn al-Rabi' al-Ansari, when Sa'd said to him: "My brother, I am the wealthiest person in Madinah. Take half of my wealth, and I have two wives; look at whichever of them pleases you most, and I will divorce her for you." Abd al-Rahman said to him: "May Allah bless you in your family and your wealth; show me the market." The full report is narrated by Ibn Sa'd in al-Tabaqat (3/117).

Then the Almighty moves from this to a general matter concerning the whole procession of messengers: ﴿And [mention] when We took from the prophets their covenant, and from you, and from Noah, and Abraham, and Moses, and Jesus the son of Mary. And We took from them a solemn covenant﴾ [al-Ahzab 33:7].

The word ﴿إِذْ﴾ (idh, "when") and ﴿إِذَا﴾ (idha) are an adverbial of time for an event. You say: "If (idha) so-and-so comes to you, honour him," so the honouring is conditional upon the coming. The meaning here is: "And mention when Allah took from the prophets their covenant." This matter is general to all the messengers, and the Almighty then details it with His words: ﴿and from you, and from Noah, and Abraham, and Moses, and Jesus the son of Mary...﴾ [al-Ahzab 33:7].

The ﴿مِيثَاق﴾ (mithaq, covenant) is a pledge taken between two parties, like the covenant that Allah, exalted is He, first took from all creation while they were in the stage of the atoms (al-dharr), concerning which Allah said: ﴿And [mention] when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants, and made them testify concerning themselves, [saying], "Am I not your Lord?"...﴾ [al-A'raf 7:172].

So what is the covenant that Allah took from the prophets? The covenant here is: election and choosing by Allah of a human being to be a messenger and envoy between Allah, exalted is He, and creation. When Allah chooses a messenger to convey the law of Allah to people, this choosing is not refused; it is therefore an accepted offer. When the messenger accepts it, it is as if he has taken a covenant and pledge from Allah, exalted is He, to carry the message of Allah to creation. It is thus a matter of offer and acceptance.

So His words ﴿And when We took from the prophets their covenant...﴾ [al-Ahzab 33:7]: the one who takes is the Almighty, the one from whom it is taken are the prophets, and the ﴿مِيثَاق﴾ (mithaq) is the confirmed covenant. A covenant (ʿahd) is a mutual agreement between two parties on a matter that achieves the good of both of them together; if one of them dissents, the contract is not completed. If the two parties are equal, each one stipulates in the contract what he sees as for himself.

If the covenant is from the higher to the lower, then it is the one who takes the covenant for the lower. Why? Because you have placed him in a rank to give a pledge, and things are confirmed between you and him. Therefore the Almighty says: ﴿and His covenant with which He bound you...﴾ [al-Ma'idah 5:7].

The ﴿مُوَاثَقَة﴾ (muwathaqa, mutual binding) is a reciprocal act between the two parties: you bound Him with it, and He bound you with it. This is because when Allah chooses messengers, there is no doubt that He, exalted is He, knows where He places His message; so when Allah chooses a messenger, the messenger's acceptance of the message is his consent to what Allah wants by way of the covenant.

Have we seen a messenger in the procession of messages to whom the message was presented and who rejected it? So: acceptance of the message is like the covenant; it came from one side, dictating its conditions, because it is the higher party; and the basis of the binding is that Allah chose him and made him fit for election to the message.

Therefore we see in the story of our master Moses, peace be upon him, that when Allah chose him for the message, he felt that it was a great matter for him, yet he did not refuse it; rather he asked Allah that his brother Aaron support him in this responsibility. He said to the Almighty: ﴿And my brother Aaron — he is more eloquent than me in tongue, so send him with me as a supporter (ridan), to confirm me...﴾ [al-Qasas 28:34].

He did not say, "I am not fit for this matter"; rather he submitted to the command of Allah. Allah knows where He places His message, and the matter of the impediment in his tongue he sought help with through his brother.

So: the word ﴿الميثاق﴾ (al-mithaq) revolves around a thing that is confirmed and bound. From it is His words about the enemies: ﴿So when you meet those who disbelieve, [strike] the necks until, when you have inflicted slaughter upon them (athkhantumuhum), then bind firmly the bond (al-wathaq)...﴾ [Muhammad 47:4].

Then comes the detail of this general matter: ﴿and from you, and from Noah, and Abraham, and Moses, and Jesus the son of Mary...﴾ [al-Ahzab 33:7].

His words "from you" (minka) mean from our master the Messenger of Allah, the seal of the prophets and messengers. But why did he mention Muhammad (ﷺ) before Noah, peace be upon him, who is the second father of all mankind after Adam, peace be upon him?

We know that all of mankind is from the lineage of Adam, peace be upon him, until the time of Noah, peace be upon him, when they divided into believers and disbelievers. Then the flood came and none remained upon the face of the earth except Noah and those who believed in him, so he was the second father of mankind after our master Adam.

Therefore some say: Noah's message was general, just as the message of Muhammad, peace be upon him, is general. We say: the generality of Noah was for those who believed in him and the people of the ark, in a known time and a specific place; but the message of Muhammad is general in every time and every place.

As for mentioning Muhammad (ﷺ) first, it is because the conjunction "and" (waw) here usually does not require order or sequence, but is for mere togetherness. Then the Messenger of Allah was put first because he is the one addressed by this speech, and it is part of Allah's honouring of His Messenger that he be begun with in such a position. Then there is another point in this precedence, which we understand from his own words, peace be upon him: "I was a prophet while Adam was between water and clay" (3).

Then Noah is singled out here because he is the second father of mankind, then Abraham, Moses and Jesus. As for Abraham, it is because the Arabs believed in him, knew that he is the father of the prophets, appreciated his connection to the Ka'bah and the raising of its foundations, and that he is a model in the matter of sacrifice, the sa'y and other things.

As for Moses and Jesus, it is because Judaism and Christianity are two religions contemporary with the call of the Messenger of Allah, where the Jews were in Medina and the Christians in Najran; they are the People of the Book with whom the Messenger of Allah had various confrontations. They held scholarly, economic, architectural and military supremacy in the Arabian Peninsula, as though they were the owners of this land.

It is remarkable that Allah, exalted is He, in His covenant with their prophets, reserved them to bear witness to the truth of Muhammad's call. Therefore they used to seek victory through Muhammad against those who disbelieved, saying to the idolaters: "The time of a prophet has drawn near whom we will follow, and we will kill you with him, as the killing of ʿĀd and Iram." They knew the time of the Messenger of Allah and his homeland, and that he would be sent to a land of palm trees, with such-and-such characteristics. So when Allah scattered them over the earth as nations and dispersed them, those among them who were occupied with knowledge came to Yathrib awaiting his mission, peace be upon him.

Therefore He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "You are not a messenger." Say, "Sufficient is Allah as a witness between me and you, and [also] whoever has knowledge of the Book."﴾ [al-Ra'd 13:43].

So: the People of the Book were supposed to bear witness to the Messenger of Allah's truthfulness in the message, but after all this the Qur'an recounts about them: ﴿And when there came to them that which they recognized, they disbelieved in it, so the curse of Allah is upon the disbelievers﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:89].

How then did this transformation happen? How does the belief of the heart turn into rebellion of the body? They said: it is the temporal authority which they loved to remain and to last for them. The Messenger was sent while they were people of wealth and trade, people of crafts and construction, and they feared from the Messenger of Allah and the new religion that it would strip them of this status and put an end to this supremacy. Therefore the Qur'an said of them: ﴿Wretched is that for which they have sold themselves: that they disbelieve in what Allah has sent down, out of envy that Allah should send down His bounty upon whom He wills of His servants. So they returned having acquired wrath upon wrath, and for the disbelievers is a humiliating punishment﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:90].

For this reason the procession of the prophets, Moses and Jesus, peace be upon them, is singled out here.

We note that the context mentions Moses, peace be upon him, without mentioning a father for him, whereas for Jesus, peace be upon him, it says: ﴿Jesus the son of Mary...﴾ [al-Ahzab 33:7]. This is evidence that it affirms the originality of begetting: the father is the origin if he exists with the wife; if the father does not exist, the fatherhood belongs to the wife. Therefore he, peace be upon him, was attributed to his mother.

This matter came to demonstrate the absoluteness of divine power. The creation is not a mechanical process subject to a law; rather it is the power of Allah which created Adam without father or mother, created Eve from a father without a mother, created Jesus, peace be upon him, from a mother without a father, and created the rest of creation from a father and a mother. Thus creation exhausted the rational division in all its forms.

As for His words: ﴿And We took from them a solemn covenant﴾ [al-Ahzab 33:7], that is, from the prophets, and the "solemn covenant" means the confirmed one. He strengthened it and confirmed it when He informed His prophets and messengers that they would be persecuted and fought by their peoples.

Therefore the covenant is not described as "solemn" except in this subject, and in the relationship between a man and a woman when he divorces her, having set for her a dowry which he must pay her, even if it be a qintar. He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And how would you take it back while you have gone in to one another and they have taken from you a solemn covenant?﴾ [al-Nisa' 4:21].

So He named the covenant between the spouses a "solemn covenant", meaning strong and firm, because it is in the matter of honour; and the covenant is not described as solemn in anything less than that.

And this covenant which Allah, exalted is He, took from the messengers, the bearers of good news and warners, is detailed in His words: ﴿And when Allah took the covenant of the prophets: "Whatever I have given you of Book and wisdom, then there comes to you a messenger confirming what is with you, you must believe in him and support him." He said, "Do you affirm and accept My commitment upon that?" They said, "We affirm." He said, "Then bear witness, and I am with you among the witnesses."﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:81].

That which Allah bears witness to needs no judgment. But why did Allah take this covenant? They said: because the one who does not believe in a god has no religion for which he is zealous when a new messenger comes; but it is difficult for a person to have a religion and then a new messenger comes to dislodge him from his religion, and here lies the hardship which the messengers suffer.

Therefore Allah said to the messengers: "Among the completeness of your covenant is that you tell your peoples: if there comes to you a messenger confirming what is with you, you must believe in him and support him." Then you should have them affirm this and make them witness to it, and they bore witness. The meaning: beware of leaving your peoples who believe in you without laying down for them this principle, for in it is their protection.

1 *radaʾa*: strengthened and helped. The *ridʾ* is the helper and supporter. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/260].
