This was the first matter in which minds were absent and opinion was corrupted, so the Quraysh seized the first opportunity when they found someone to support them against Muhammad and his call. From here, the people of falsehood gathered: the Quraysh and their allies from Banu Fazara, from Banu Murra, from Ghatafan, Banu Asad, al-Ash'ariyyin, and others. They all gathered to eliminate the nascent religion.

Then came the first heroism of this battle, from a man who was not an Arab, but from Persia, the worshippers of fire, may Allah protect us. The Truthful One, glorified be He, was preparing to support the truth even through the side of falsehood. He is the honored Companion Salman al-Farisi(1), who spent his life wandering in search of the truth, until fate brought him to Madina, where he encountered the mission of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and believed in him.

Salman was the first hero in this battle, when he advised the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to dig the trench. He said: "O Messenger of Allah, when we in Persia were beset by the matter of war, we dug a trench, that is, we placed a trench between us and our enemies." This idea won the approval of the Muhajirun and the Ansar, and each of them wished to have Salman on his side. When they disputed over him, our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), said to them: "Rather, Salman is one of us, the People of the House"(2). This is the greatest honor placed upon the breast of Salman, may Allah be pleased with him.

This idea is evidence that the Truthful One, glorified be He, mobilizes even falsehood in the service of truth. We had never seen a trench, nor had the people of the Persian (who brought this idea) known it, but Allah drove it to us and made it one of His soldiers through this honored Companion, so that we would know, as He, exalted be He, said: ﴿And know that Allah intervenes between a man and his heart...﴾ (24) [al-Anfal].

We have clarified this meaning in the story of Pharaoh, who used to slaughter the infants after the prophecy he had heard. Then a child came to him, contrary to custom, carried to him in his box, and it is not hidden from anyone that his family intended by this to remove him from the danger of Pharaoh. Yet Allah intervened between Pharaoh and what was in his heart, so he took the child and raised him in his house.

The poet who expressed this meaning did well, when he said:

If you do not find care in your sons,
then the hopeful one has lied and the expectant one has failed.
Musa, whom Jibril raised, is a disbeliever,
and Musa, whom Pharaoh raised, is a messenger.

The second hero in this battle was a man called Nu'aym ibn Mas'ud al-Ash'ari(3), who came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, my heart has inclined to Islam, and no one among my people knows of it." The Messenger of Allah said to him: "What can you do? But weaken them for us"(4). That is: push the people away from us by any means, keep them away from us, mislead them from our path, or tell them that we are many, so that they may fear us, and so on.

Here is a man who was a disbeliever yesterday. What did faith do to his heart, being so recent? Nu'aym looked and saw the Quraysh and their followers coming from below, and Banu Qurayza and their followers coming from above. He wished to enter between them through intrigue. He went to Abu Sufyan and said: "O Abu Sufyan, I am your friend, and you know my separation from the religion of Muhammad. But I have heard a whisper that Banu Qurayza have reconsidered their affair with Muhammad and said: the Quraysh and their allies are not residents of Madina as we are. If they encounter victory, they win, and if they encounter defeat, they flee to their lands, leaving Banu Qurayza to Muhammad. Therefore they have decided not to fight with you unless you give them ten of your notables to be hostages with them."

Abu Sufyan heard these words, went to his people, and said to them: "You are the ones who reside here, and this is not the place of Banu Qurayza. They will leave you to face Muhammad alone. If you want to keep their pact to fight Muhammad, ask them for hostages with which to secure their support for you."

Afterward Abu Sufyan went to speak with Banu Qurayza about this matter, and said: "The hoof and the hoofed have perished," meaning the camels and the horses, "and we are not a place of residence for us. Come, let us grapple with(5) this Muhammad." After they had remained for more than twenty days, going back and forth and consulting, they said to him: "This is Saturday, and we will not corrupt our religion for the sake of fighting Muhammad. In any case, we will not join you in fighting unless you give us ten of your notables to be hostages with us." At that moment Abu Sufyan knew that the words of Nu'aym al-Ash'ari were true. He gathered his people and said to them: "The land is not a place of residence for us, and the hoof and the hoofed have perished. Come, let us escape."

They said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was visited by Nu'aym ibn Mas'ud and informed him of what had happened, and the Messenger of Allah found the atmosphere calm, he said: "Is there not a man among you who will go and bring us news of them now, and he will be my companion in Paradise?" The intended meaning was that he should infiltrate the ranks of the enemy to learn their news.

Despite this good news with which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave glad tidings to whoever would perform this task, none of those present rose. This shows that the terror at that moment was great, the danger was immense, and the people were in a state of exhaustion, hunger, and fear that made them hold back from standing up. None of them found in himself the strength to perform this task.

Therefore the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) assigned a man called Hudhayfa ibn al-Yaman to this task. Hudhayfa said: "The Messenger of Allah had said to me: do not do anything until you return to me. So when I went and slipped away at night, I sat among the people. Abu Sufyan came with the news from Banu Qurayza, wishing to depart with those with him, and said: 'Let each one of you recognize the one sitting beside him, lest there be a stranger among the people.'"

Here Hudhayfa's skill and good conduct appeared. He said: "I hurried and said to the one on my right: 'Who are you?' He said: 'Mu'awiya ibn Abi Sufyan.' And I said to the one on my left: 'Who are you?' He said: 'Amr ibn al-As'(6).' I heard Abu Sufyan say to the people: 'The hoof and the hoofed have perished, and the land is not a place of residence, so come, and I am the first of you,' and he mounted his mount, which was hobbled(7) because of his great haste. Hudhayfa said: 'I intended to kill him. I took out my bow, strung it, and placed the arrow in its middle. But I remembered the words of the Messenger of Allah: Do not say anything until you come to me, so I did not wish to kill him. When I went to the Messenger of Allah, I found him praying. When he sensed me, he opened his legs, and the weather was extremely cold, so I entered between his legs, and he spread his cloak over me to warm me. When he finished the prayer he said to me: What is your matter? So I related my story to him(8).'"

After the Truthful One, glorified be He, had mobilized both Nu'aym al-Ash'ari and Hudhayfa to support the truth, other soldiers came that they had not seen. That night was cold and the winds were severe. A storm arose that uprooted their tents, overturned their cooking pots, and scattered them, so whoever remained fled.

This is the meaning of His saying, exalted be He: ﴿And Allah is ever Strong and Mighty.﴾ (25) [al-Ahzab]. ﴿And none knows the soldiers of your Lord except Him.﴾ (31) [al-Muddaththir].

After the Truthful One had turned back the disbelievers of Makka in their rage, and had spared the believers the fighting, He wished to turn to the other front, the front of Banu Qurayza. When the Messenger of Allah returned from the Confederates, Jibril (peace be upon him) met him and said: "Have you laid down your armor(9), O Muhammad, while the angels have not laid down their weapons for war? Go and avenge yourself on Banu Qurayza." So the Messenger of Allah said to the people: "Whoever is listening and obedient, let him not pray the afternoon prayer except in Banu Qurayza(10)."

The Companions disagreed about this matter. Some of them complied with it literally and hastened to Banu Qurayza intending to pray the afternoon prayer there. Others feared that the time of the afternoon prayer would pass, so they prayed and then went. When they gathered before the Messenger of Allah, he acknowledged both groups and approved both opinions.

This matter became a reference point among the sources of ijtihad (independent juristic reasoning) in Islamic thought. An event has a time and a place. Some Companions looked to the time, saw the sun about to set, and prayed. Others looked to the place and did not pray except in Banu Qurayza. Therefore the Messenger of Allah approved this and that(11).

The Muslim must beware of delaying the prayer beyond its time. For instance, the time of the afternoon prayer begins when the shadow of everything becomes twice its length and ends at Maghrib. This does not mean that you should delay the afternoon prayer until its last time. True, if you pray at the last part of the time, nothing is upon you. But who guarantees that you will live until the last part of the time?

So you do not sin if you pray at the last part of the time, but you sin in the last moment of your life, when death attends you and you have not prayed. Therefore our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), said: "The best of deeds is prayer at its proper time"(12). So the extension of the time is not permission to delay.

In the matter of the Confederates there is another heroism of our master, Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him. This heroism appeared when the disbelievers found a weak point in the trench, through which they could dare to attack the Muslims and send their horses across. When they charged their horses to the other side, the horses roamed in the salt flat between the trench and Mount Sal'. One disbeliever stood forth, 'Amr ibn 'Abd Wudd al-Amiri(13), who was at that time the bravest and strongest of the Arabs; they counted him in battles as worth a thousand horsemen.

'Amr ibn 'Abd Wudd stood before the camp of the Muslims, saying while brandishing his sword: "Who will duel?" Ali said to the Messenger of Allah: "Shall I duel him, O Messenger of Allah?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Sit down, O Ali, it is 'Amr." 'Amr repeated: "Where is your paradise that you were promised for whoever is killed in this path? Answer me!"

Ali said: "Shall I duel him, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Sit down, O Ali, it is 'Amr." And at the third time 'Amr said:

I have grown hoarse calling to your assembly: "Is there any challenger?"
And you stood still, when the brave one fell back, like a stand-off opponent in combat.
Courage in a youth, and generosity, are among the best of dispositions.

At that, Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, sprang up and said: "I will face him, O Messenger of Allah." The Messenger of Allah gave him permission. Ali gestured to 'Amr and said:

Do not hasten, for one has come to you who answers your call, not feeble,
One of intention and insight, for truthfulness saves every victor.
Indeed I hope to make a wailing woman for the dead over you,
From a wide-gaping blow whose memory will remain...

1 Salman al-Farisi, a Companion among their foremost, originally from the Magians of Isfahan. He travelled to Syria, then to Mosul, then to Nasibin. He read the books of the Persians, the Romans, and the Jews. He learned of the news of Islam, so he made for the Prophet and heard his words. He did not enter Islam until he had been freed from slavery. He used to weave wool and eat barley bread earned by the work of his hands. He died in 36 AH. [al-A'lam by al-Zirikli, 3/112].

2 From Amr ibn Awf al-Muzani, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) dug the trench in the year of the Confederates, from the rocky ground at the edge of the lands of Banu Haritha, when the ink reached it, then he marked out forty cubits, ten for each group. The Muhajirun and the Ansar disputed about Salman al-Farisi, and he was a strong man. The Ansar said: "Salman is one of us." The Muhajirun said: "Salman is one of us." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Salman is one of us, the People of the House." Narrated by al-Bayhaqi in Dala'il al-Nubuwwa (3/418) and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak (3/598). al-Dhahabi declared its chain weak because of Kathir ibn Abd Allah.

3 Nu'aym ibn Mas'ud ibn Amir al-Ash'ari, Abu Salama. A well-known Companion who embraced Islam during the nights of the trench. He is the one who caused discord between the two clans, Qurayza and Ghatafan, during the battle of the trench, so that they opposed each other and departed from Madina. Nu'aym was killed at the beginning of the caliphate of Ali, before his arrival in Basra at the Battle of the Camel. It is said he died during the caliphate of Uthman, and Allah knows best. [al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba, entry no. 8780].

4 Ibn Hisham mentioned in the Sira (3/247) that Nu'aym ibn Mas'ud came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have embraced Islam, but my people do not know of my Islam, so command me as you wish." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "You are one man among us, so weaken them for us if you can, for war is deception."

5 Munajaza in fighting: fighting and combat, which is when two horsemen engage in combat until each kills the other or one of them is killed. And tanajaza the people: they shed each other's blood, as though they hastened to it. [Lisan al-Arab, root: n-j-z].

6 Al-Bayhaqi mentioned in Dala'il al-Nubuwwa (3/451), from the report of Hudhayfa, that "Abu Sufyan sensed that someone from outside had entered among them, so he said: 'Let each man take the hand of the one beside him.' I struck my hand on the one on my right and took his hand, then I struck my hand on the one on my left and took his hand." (Narrated by al-Hakim in his Mustadrak, 3/31). In another narration mentioned by Ibn Kathir in his Tafsir (3/471), attributed to Muhammad ibn Ishaq: "Abu Sufyan said: 'O assembly of Quraysh, let each person look at his neighbor.' Hudhayfa said: I took the hand of the man beside me, and I said: 'Who are you?' He said: 'I am so-and-so, son of so-and-so.'" It does not mention Mu'awiya or Amr ibn al-As at all. And Allah knows best.

7 The camel's 'aql: he tied it and fastened it. [Lisan al-Arab, root: '-q-l], with modification.

8 Mentioned by al-Bayhaqi in Dala'il al-Nubuwwa (3/451). See also Ibn Kathir's Tafsir (3/471).

9 Al-La'ma: armor. It is said: weapons. The "la'mat al-harb" is its equipment. Some said: al-La'ma is the sturdy armor, named la'ma for the soundness of its construction and the quality of its rings. [Lisan al-Arab, root: l-'-m].

10 Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani mentioned this wording in his commentary on al-Bukhari (Fath al-Bari 7/408), as a saying of Ibn Ishaq. The original hadith is in al-Bukhari's Sahih (4119), from Ibn Umar, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said on the day of the Confederates: "None of you should pray the afternoon prayer except in Banu Qurayza."

11 A hadith agreed upon (Muttafaq 'alayh). Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (4119), and likewise Muslim in his Sahih (1770), Book of Jihad, chapter on hastening to the raid (23), from the hadith of Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both. Its wording is that some of the Companions were overtaken by the afternoon prayer on the road. Some said: "We will not pray until we reach them." Others said: "Rather, we will pray; he did not intend that from us." This was mentioned to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he did not rebuke either of them.

12 From Ibn Mas'ud, who said: I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Which deeds are best?" He said: "Prayer at its proper time." I said: "Then what?" He said: "Then kindness to parents." I said: "Then what?" He said: "Then jihad in the path of Allah." Agreed upon hadith, narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (2782), and likewise Muslim in his Sahih (85), Book of Faith.

13 He is Amr ibn Abd Wudd, a Qurashi from the Banu Lu'ayy, the knight (fāris) of Quraysh in the pre-Islamic era. He lived to see Islam but did not embrace it. He lived until the Battle of the Trench (al-Khandaq) took place, attended it although he had passed eighty years of age, and insisted on fighting. Ali ibn Abi Talib fought him and killed him in the year 5 AH. Source: al-A'lam by al-Zirikli (5/81).

14 A wide stab (ṭa'na najlā'): that is, wide and clearly gaping. Sinān minjal: a wide wound. And najalahu bil-rumḥ: he stabbed him with the spear and widened its tear. Source: Lisan al-Arab, entry: n-j-l.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 33, verse 28:

Then Allah, glorified and exalted is He, moves us to the houses of the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ). So He, glorified is He, says:

﴿O Prophet, say to your wives: If you desire the life of this world and its adornment, then come, I will provide for you and release you in a graceful release.﴾ (33:28)

A questioner may ask: what is the secret of this great shift in the discourse from the matter of the Confederates (al-Ahzab) and the war of Banu Qurayza to this address to the wives of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?

They said: because the matter of the Confederates ended with His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And He caused you to inherit their land, their homes, and their wealth, and a land you had not trodden.﴾ (33:27). So perhaps the wives of the Messenger asked that he provide for them and spend on them from the bounties that Allah would open to him from the lands of this region. Thus this verse came: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives﴾ (33:28), to establish that Islam did not come to secure a privilege for the Messenger of Allah, nor for the family of the Messenger of Allah; even zakat is not valid for any poor person of Banu Hashim.

But the verse coming in this form, in the imperative: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives: If you desire...﴾ (33:28), is evidence that something had occurred from them indicating their longing for the adornment and enjoyments of life. It is narrated from Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) that they gathered and asked the Messenger of Allah for maintenance, and that he should widen their provision, after the Prophet (ﷺ) had said concerning the disbelievers: "They will not invade us; rather, we will invade them," and after the verses had given them glad tidings of what would be opened of new lands.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿so come, I will provide for you and release you in a graceful release﴾ (33:28), it means: I do not have with me what you long for of the world's adornment and its ornaments. The meaning of ﴿fa-ta'alayna﴾ (so come): we say "ta'alayna," meaning "aqbilna" (come forward). But here it means "irtafa'na" (rise up) from height: rise above the methods of humans and the earth, and ascend to the methods of the Creator of humans and the Creator of the earth; for sovereignty lies in the method of Allah, not in the enjoyments of life and its ornaments.

This meaning has also occurred in His saying: ﴿Say: Come, I will recite to you what your Lord has forbidden you﴾ (6:151). So "ta'alaw" means: rise above the laws of humans and the laws of the earth to the laws of the heavens; because whoever enacts a law must be one who does not benefit from that law, and must be fully aware of all the particulars the law addresses; and humans, however great their capacity, know some things and are ignorant of others. Therefore none should legislate for them except their Creator, mighty and majestic is He.

The meaning of ﴿I will provide for you﴾ (33:28) is: I will give you the legal provision (mut'a shar'iyya) that is imposed for a wife upon separation from her husband, concerning which Allah said: ﴿And for divorced women is a provision according to what is reasonable, a duty upon the righteous.﴾ (2:241)

His saying: ﴿and release you﴾ (33:28) — that release here means divorce. ﴿In a graceful release﴾ (33:28) indicates that separation between spouses, if it occurs, occurs with grace, that is: with gentleness, tenderness, and mercy, without ugliness and without violence; because release in itself is a painful parting, so Allah does not combine upon it two hardships: the hardship of divorce and the hardship of violence and harshness.

You may observe that the word "beauty" (jamal) comes in the Qur'an with difficult matters that require firmness. Read His saying: ﴿So patience is beautiful﴾ (12:83). Patience is beautiful when it is not accompanied by impatience, complaint, or going beyond the bounds of moderation.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) offered his wives the graceful release, free of quarrel and enmity, if they chose it for themselves. And the Messenger of Allah would not keep a wife who chose something else over him, whatever it might be.

The scholars have lengthy discussion on this matter: does divorce take effect by this option (takhyir)? They said: the option is a form of desire for separation which gives the woman, as we say for example: the bond is in her hand, so she chooses for herself. If she accepts the first option, divorce takes effect. If she chooses the other, it is good and the matter ends.

The command of Allah to His Messenger to say these words to his wives must have had a basis in thoughts that passed through the minds of the wives of the Messenger (ﷺ) when they saw Islam opening lands for him and the bounties being brought to him, so they longed for some provision.

The word "al-azwaj" is the plural of "zawj," and it is said of a man and of a woman. "Zawj" does not mean two together, as some suppose; rather, zawj means an individual who has with him a like of his own kind. It is exactly like the word "tawam" (twin): it means "one," but with it is its like. The proof of this is His saying: ﴿And of everything We created pairs (zawjayn)﴾ (51:49), meaning: male and female. The male alone is a zawj, and the female alone is a zawj, and this division exists in all creatures. "Zawj" is also pluralized as "zawjat."

We note in the style here that when Allah, glorified is He, presents to His Messenger that he should give his wives the choice between the adornment of the world and the bliss of the Hereafter, He uses ﴿in (if)﴾, which indicates doubt, and does not use, for example, ﴿idha (when)﴾, which indicates certainty. In this is an indication of not exaggerating their accusation; the matter is no more than thoughts that passed through the minds of some of his wives.

You know that our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), gathered nine women together at once, of whom five were from Quraysh: Aisha, Hafsa, Umm Habiba, Sawda bint Zam'a, and Umm Salama daughter of Abu Umayya; and from outside Quraysh: Safiyya bint Huyayy ibn Akhtab, whose story we mentioned in (the chapter of) the Confederates; then Juwayriyya bint al-Harith of Banu al-Mustaliq; then Maymuna bint al-Harith al-Hilaliyya, and whoever goes to al-Tan'im finds there the well of Maymuna; then Zaynab bint Jahsh of Banu Asad. These are the nine Mothers of the Believers whom the Messenger of Allah gathered together.

When they asked the Messenger of Allah for maintenance, the boldest of them in this was Sayyida Hafsa bint Umar, and there occurred between her and the Messenger of Allah a dispute in speech. He said to her: "Do you not love that I summon a man between us?" She agreed, so he sent for Umar. When he came, the Messenger of Allah said to her: "Speak, you" (meaning: state your need). She said: "No, you speak, and say only what is true."

This word provoked the ire of our master Umar. He flared up, went to his daughter and struck her; the Messenger of Allah restrained him. He took hold of her again and struck her, then said to her: "The Messenger of Allah says only what is true. By Allah, were it not that I am in his assembly, I would not leave you until you die." The Messenger of Allah rose from the gathering to end this dispute, went to his chamber, and secluded himself there, and he abstained from the whole matter for a period of one month.

Reflect on the saying of Allah: ﴿If you desire the life of this world and its adornment﴾ (33:28). What description is more belittling and more diminishing of this life than that it is called "dunya" (the lower)? And what enjoyments it contains are only adornment, meaning: luxury in appearance, not in substance, as He, glorified is He, said elsewhere: ﴿Know that the life of this world is but play and amusement and adornment and boasting among you and competition in wealth and children﴾ (57:20).

1 Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir (7/5422): "Our scholars said: this verse is connected in meaning to what preceded concerning the prohibition of harming the Prophet (ﷺ), for he had been harmed by some of the wives. It was said: they asked him for something of the goods of this world. It was said: an increase in maintenance. It was said: their harm to him was through the jealousy of some of them toward others."
2 This matter has differing reports: some of them attribute it to Aisha and her father Abu Bakr, and others to Hafsa and her father Umar. As for the first, Abu Sa'd recorded it in al-Tabaqat (10/79). As for the second, al-Bukhari recorded it in his Sahih (2468) within a long hadith. It is possible that the incident occurred more than once, and Allah knows best.

Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ presents to his wives the second option, which stands opposite the life of this world: ﴿And if you desire Allah and His Messenger and the Last Abode, then indeed Allah has prepared for the good-doers among you a great reward﴾ (33:29).

The one who considers the two sides of this choice finds that comparing them is a difficult matter, which suggests a rejection of being given a choice between the two ends of this issue. For who would accept to have the life of this world in exchange for Allah, and its adornment in exchange for the Messenger of Allah? Add to that the Last Abode, against which nothing was mentioned on the other side. Moreover, the life of this world that we live, even if it is not described as "the lower world" (dunya), ought to be renounced.

The truth is that they understood this text and chose Allah, His Messenger and the Last Abode, and "who would accept other than these as a substitute?" Praise be to Allah.

﴿And Allah sufficed the believers in the fighting...﴾ (33:25).

Then comes the reward of the one who chose Allah, His Messenger and the Last Abode: ﴿then indeed Allah has prepared for the good-doers among you a great reward﴾ (33:29). The "good-doer" (al-muhsinat) is the wife who gives, out of the mercy and conjugal affection, beyond what is asked of her.

The Almighty, glory be to Him, after He gave the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) the choice, and they chose God, His Messenger and the Last Abode, wished to give them the method and principles they would follow in their lives. We note that the verse of choice was spoken by the Prophet (ﷺ) on behalf of his Lord, whereas here the speech comes directly from God to the wives of the Prophet.

﴿O wives of the Prophet...﴾ (30). The beginning of the matter was ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives...﴾ (28). So when they chose God, His Messenger and the Last Abode, it is as if they had risen to the level of direct address from God Most High; it is as if they had fulfilled the intent of the earlier command: ﴿...then come, I will provide for you...﴾ (28).

The word ﴿nisa'...﴾ (30) we know to be a plural, but we do not find a singular of it from its own root; its singular is from another word, which is imra'a (woman) (1). In the language there are plurals whose singular has been forgotten through the fame of another singular that is more delicate or easier in use. Imra'a, or (mura), may also derive from (imru') (2). This word differs from all other words of the language in that its case-inflection (i'rab) is not confined to the last letter but extends also to the letter before the last. We say: qala Imru' al-Qays (Imru' al-Qays said), wa-sami'tu Imra' al-Qays (I heard Imra' al-Qays), and qara'tu li-Imri' al-Qays (I read to Imri' al-Qays).

Some researchers in the language have said that (nisa') derives from (nasa', delay and postponement), on the basis that their creation came later than the creation of man, so its singular would be (nas'). But this is a strained view for which there is no need.

After this address, ﴿O wives of the Prophet...﴾ (30), comes the first ruling of the method addressed to them: ﴿Whoever of you commits a clear indecency, the punishment will be doubled for her, double...﴾ (30). We note that the Almighty did not begin His speech to the wives of the Prophet by saying, for example, "Whoever of you fears God", but began with a warning against committing indecency, because the legal principle in legislation and reform rests on the rule that "averting harm takes precedence over securing benefit", just as before we perform ablution for prayer we cleanse ourselves of impurity.

Let us illustrate this: suppose one person threw an apple at you and another threw a stone; which would deserve your attention first? Without doubt you would be eager first to ward off the stone and be saved from its harm. Likewise, if you wished to iron your garment, for example, while it is dirty, you must first wash it.

Therefore the Almighty began His direction to the wives of the Prophet with the words ﴿Whoever of you commits a clear indecency...﴾ (30). But indecency is an unlikely matter; how could the ultimate sins be expected from the wives of the Messenger of God? They said: why not, since God Most High addressed His Prophet (ﷺ) with the words: ﴿If you were to associate partners with God, your deeds would surely be nullified...﴾ (65) [Az-Zumar].

It is well known that the Messenger of God is not liable to fall into shirk. So the meaning is: O Muhammad, your being chosen does not mean that you are above accountability. The same holds for his wives: if any of you commits an indecency, We shall double the punishment for her, and We will not overlook it because of her station with the Messenger of God. So beware lest you think this station will intercede for you, or the matter would fall under the saying: when a person of low standing steals, they enforce the penalty upon him, but when a person of high standing steals, they leave him alone (3).

Thus: the standing of each of you does not lie in being merely a wife of the Messenger of God; rather her standing is measured by the extent of her adherence to God's commands. Otherwise, there were wives of prophets who betrayed their husbands. Recite: ﴿God presents an example for those who disbelieve: the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot; they were under two of Our righteous servants, but they betrayed them, so they availed them nothing against God, and it was said: Enter the Fire along with those who enter﴾ (10) [Al-Ahzab].

You may ask: this is the ruling for a clear indecency, that its punishment is doubled; but what of indecency from them if it is not clear?

They said: this ruling is specific to the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ). If a sin occurs from one of them between herself and herself, it is a single sin confined to her; but if it is openly done, it is doubled, because they are a model and an exemplar toward whose conduct eyes are turned. If indecency appears from them, it becomes an encouragement to others, and why not, since indecency came from the wife of the Prophet.

So the doubling of the punishment is because the corruption extended from the self to others and set a bad example in the Prophet's house, so she deserved the doubling of the punishment, because she hurt the feelings of the Messenger of God, did not value his station, and preferred another over him to commit indecency with him. This requires multiplied punishment. That God doubled the punishment for her, only twofold, is a kindness toward her and consideration for her past in the marriage of the Messenger of God.

Likewise, if one of them does a good deed, she will also have its reward doubled, because she has done a righteous act in herself as any other person would, and then she has given a good example and a fine model to others.

If we take into account the Prophet's saying (ﷺ): "Whoever establishes a good practice in Islam will have its reward and the reward of whoever acts by it until the Day of Resurrection, and whoever establishes a bad practice will bear its burden and the burden of whoever acts by it until the Day of Resurrection" (5),

we learn that the reward of a good deed is not merely doubled twice, but multiplied according to the number of those influenced by the example. There is a difference between "al-day'f" (doubling) and "al-du'f" (weakness): "al-day'f" means the thing's like, that is its equal, while "al-du'f" means the loss of that equal, so it is less (6).

Then He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And that is easy for God...﴾ (30). That is: the matter of doubling the punishment is an easy thing; your station with the Messenger of God will not avail you anything. This is a matter in which no one can question Me, and I show favoritism to no one, and I must arrange affairs as they ought to be, and no one can oppose Me in them. Therefore the rulings of the Almighty are often concluded with His saying: ﴿God is Mighty and Wise﴾ (220) [Al-Baqarah]. Might requires that the ruling be binding, which no one can alter and no one can object to.

This meaning is clear in His saying, Exalted is He, to our master Jesus, peace be upon him: ﴿And when God says, "O Jesus, son of Mary, did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as two gods besides God?'" He will say, "Glory be to You! It is not for me to say what I have no right to. If I had said it, You would have known it. You know what is in my soul, and I do not know what is in Your soul; indeed You are the Knower of the unseen. I said to them only what You commanded me: 'Worship God, my Lord and your Lord.' And I was a witness over them as long as I was among them; but when You took me up, You were the Watcher over them, and You are Witness over all things. If You punish them, they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, You are the Mighty, the Wise﴾ (116-118) [Al-Ma'idah].

His saying ﴿And if You forgive them...﴾ (118) would seem to call for "then You are Forgiving and Merciful", but the Almighty turned instead to ﴿then You are the Mighty, the Wise﴾ (118), because the sin into which the people fell is a sin at the summit, in the divinity they took from God and attributed to Jesus, peace be upon him. By reason, this requires severe punishment. But the Almighty is not questioned about what He does; He punishes whom He wills and forgives whom He wills. If He forgives them, it is by the attribute of might which no one can oppose. It is as if the logical expectation would be to ask God: why did You not punish these people for what they committed? Therefore it came here from the aspect of might, which is not opposed, and wisdom, which does not err.

1 Ibn Manzur said in [Lisan al-Arab – root: nasa]: "Al-nisa', and al-niswan and al-niswan: plural of al-mar'a from outside its own form. Ibn Sida said: al-nisa' is the plural of niswa when they are many."
2 Al-Layth said: imra'a is the feminine of imri'; Ibn al-Anbari said: the Arabs have three dialects for "mar'a": one says hiya imra'atuhu, another hiya imra'tuhu, and another hiya mirtuhu. [Lisan al-Arab – root: mara'].
3 A hadith agreed upon, related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (6788), and likewise Muslim in his Sahih (1688), from A'isha, may God be pleased with her, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "O people, those before you went astray because when a person of high standing stole among them, they left him, and when a person of low standing stole among them, they enforced the penalty upon him. By God, if Fatimah daughter of Muhammad stole, Muhammad would cut off her hand."
4 Ibn Kathir said in his Tafsir (4/393): "The meaning of His saying (but they betrayed them) is not in indecency but in religion, for the wives of the prophets are protected from falling into indecency out of reverence for the prophets... Ibn Abbas said: they did not commit adultery; as for the betrayal of Noah's wife, she used to tell people that he was mad, and as for the betrayal of Lot's wife, she used to direct his guests to her people."
5 Related by Imam Ahmad in his Musnad (4/361, 362), Ibn Majah in his Sunan (207), and al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan (2675), from Jarir ibn Abdullah. Al-Tirmidhi said: "a hasan sahih hadith."
6 Al-day'f and al-du'f are the opposite of strength, whether in the body or in judgment and intellect. God Most High said: ﴿God is He who created you in weakness, then made after weakness strength, then made after strength weakness﴾ [Ar-Rum].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 33, verse 31:

After Allah, glory be to Him, mentioned the matter of immorality (fahisha) and the punishment that follows from it, He mentioned the counterpart, saying, may He be exalted:

﴿And whoever of you devoutly obeys Allah and His Messenger and does righteousness - We will give her her reward twice, and We have prepared for her an honorable provision.﴾

The meaning of ﴿yaqnut﴾ (devoutly obeys) is: submits to Allah, the complete submission, and is humble and lowly before Allah in her supplication. Allah, may He be exalted, chose the word qunut because He does not like the obedient person to boast to people of her obedience. Therefore the gnostics (al-'arifun) say: "A sin that leaves one with humility and brokenness is better than an act of obedience that leaves one with pride and arrogance."(1)

Or, ﴿whoever yaqnut﴾ means: she has gone to the utmost in righteousness and in piety, to the point of reaching qunut, which is submission and humility.

The result: ﴿We will give her her reward twice﴾. The previous verse affirmed the doubling of punishment for the one who commits immorality, and this verse establishes the doubling of reward for the one who submits to Allah, is humble, and does righteousness.

﴿And We have prepared for her an honorable provision﴾ means: We have readied and equipped it for her from now on; it is awaiting her.

When we contemplate the Qur'anic style in these two verses, the eloquence of the expression becomes apparent. When mentioning immorality and the doubling of punishment, the verb ﴿yudaa'af﴾ (is doubled) came in the passive voice (mabni lima lam yusamma fa'iluh), whereas when speaking of devotion to Allah, He said ﴿nu'tiha ajraha﴾ (We will give her her reward), so the verb was attributed directly to Allah, glory be to Him. It is as though Allah, may He be exalted, did not wish to confront [the sinner] with His Essence in the station of punishment; rather, He confronted her only with the punishment.

The mere construction of the verb ﴿yudaa'af﴾ in the passive indicates the mercy and gentleness of Allah in the expression. Allah, may He be exalted, loves all of His creation, draws near to them and shows affection toward them, and He hopes that the sinner will return. He, glory be to Him, rejoices at the repentance of His believing servant more than one of you rejoices when he finds his riding beast, which had strayed from him in a desert.(2)

It has come in a report (athar): "O son of Adam, do not fear anyone holding authority as long as My authority remains, and My authority never ends. O son of Adam, do not fear shortage of provision while My treasuries are full, and My treasuries never run out. O son of Adam, I created you for worship, so do not play; and by play is meant the action that has no benefit. And I have apportioned your provision, so do not exhaust yourself."

What is meant here is: do not exhaust yourself, and do not occupy your heart, for fatigue belongs to the limbs, as the noble Prophetic hadith says: "Whoever spends the night weary from the work of his hands spends the night forgiven."(3) When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw a hand roughened by work, he said: "This is a hand that Allah and His Messenger love."(4)

Thus, fatigue is the fatigue of the heart. Whatever your chest can bear, and you are able to carry, does not weary you. That is why we find a man free of worries working at the rock, calm of mind, singing a beautiful chant and a wonderful anthem that strengthens his resolve and helps him continue, so you see him, despite this exertion, joyful and of expanded breast.

The Arab poet was also perceptive of this matter, and said:

It is not a load that the back can bear;
the load is only what the chest holds.

The meaning is: exhaust your limbs, but do not exhaust your heart. Weariness and exhaustion do not reach the limbs but the heart; so tire your limbs in serious, beneficial work, from whose fruit you take according to your need, and pour out the surplus upon those unable to earn.

Then He says: "If you are content with what I have apportioned to you, you relieve your heart and body, and you are praised by Me. But if you are not content with what I have apportioned to you, then by My might and majesty I will set the world upon you, so that you run in it like wild beasts in the wilderness, and then you will have from it only what I have apportioned to you, and you will be blamed by Me. O son of Adam, I created the heavens and the earth and I did not tire (a'i) of their creation; would a loaf that I drive toward you tire Me? O son of Adam, do not demand of Me tomorrow's provision, just as I did not demand of you tomorrow's work. O son of Adam, I have not forgotten those who disobey Me, so how about those who obey Me?"

Our witness here is His saying, may He be exalted, at the end of the sacred hadith: "O son of Adam, I love you; so by My right over you, love Me."(6)

Your Lord reveals Himself to you in His very Essence in the station of good and of bringing benefit to you, whereas in evil He alludes to you from afar, and draws your attention gently.

We also note in the style of the verse His saying, and the address is to the wives of the Prophet: ﴿whoever of you (minkunna)﴾

He did not say "taqnut," then He made the verb feminine in ﴿wa ta'mal salihan﴾ (and does righteousness). Sometimes He observes the wording, and sometimes He observes the meaning. We have previously stated that ﴿man﴾ (whoever) is a relative pronoun that comes for the singular, the dual, and the plural, and for the masculine and the feminine.

We also pause here at the description of the provision as honorable (karim), ﴿wa a'tadna laha rizqan karima﴾. We have said that provision is everything one benefits from, whether food, drink, clothing, shelter, or utilities, and it may come in an immaterial form such as knowledge and forbearance, etc. Provision in this world is not described as honorable; rather, the Honorable is Allah, glory be to Him, the Provider. So why is provision described as honorable?

They said: There is a difference between provision in this world and provision in the Hereafter. Provision in this world has causes; the cause is the provider, whether a parent, a ruler, a hired worker, or a merchant, etc. The one through whose hands provision reaches you is the one described as generous. In the Hereafter, however, provision comes to you without causes, so it is fitting that it be described as honorable itself. There is also another point: if provision is described as honorable, what then of the true Provider, glory be to Him?

2 Related by Muslim in his Sahih (2747) from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him.
