He said: "It was related by al-Tabarani in al-Awsat, and in it are a group whom I do not know." al-Hafiz al-'Iraqi said in his takhrij of the hadiths of the Ihya' (2/90): "In it is weakness."
4 Among what is related on this: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No one has eaten food better than that which he eats from the work of his own hand, and the Prophet of Allah Dawud (peace be upon him) used to eat from the work of his own hand." Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (2072) from the hadith of al-Miqdam ibn Ma'dikarib.
5 'Ayya bi al-amr fa-huwa 'ayy wa 'iyyi: he was unable to do it and could not perfect it. [Lisan al-'Arab, root: '-y-a]
6 This piece of the report was cited by Imam Abu Hamid al-Ghazali in "Ihya' 'Ulum al-Din" (4/296), where he said: "In some books: My servant, I love you by your right, so by My right over you, love Me."

The Almighty then says:

﴿O wives of the Prophet, you are not like any other women. If you are mindful of God, then do not be soft in speech, lest one in whose heart is a disease should be moved with desire; but speak in a good, fair manner.﴾ (33:32)

The word (aḥad) is used in the language in several ways. For example, in counting we say aḥad ʿashara (eleven) if the thing counted is masculine, and iḥdā ʿashrata (eleven) if it is feminine. In negation, however, it is used only in one form, (aḥad), and it refers to the singular, the dual and the plural, and to the masculine and the feminine. So you say: "There is no one (aḥad) with me," meaning neither a man nor a woman, neither two men nor two women, neither men nor women. Hence the words of God Most High: ﴿And there is none comparable to Him, anyone (aḥad)﴾ (112:4).

His words, glorified is He: ﴿You are not like any (aḥad) of the women..﴾ (33:32) are a specificity (khuṣūṣiyya) for them, because things represent genera (ajnās), and beneath the genus are species (anwāʿ). Man, for example, is a genus, and within it is the male and the female, and each of these two species has individuals beneath it. The male and the female did not separate into two species after being one genus except because of a difference that arose between them after agreement in the genus. The genus is a common boundary: a living, speaking, thinking being. When the two separated into two species, each of them acquired a specificity that distinguishes it from the other.

As we have said of time, for instance: it is the container of events. If the events are movement, it is daytime; if the events are stillness, it is night. Night and day are two species beneath one genus, which is time, and each has its specificity, and we must observe this specificity and not confuse the two.

Consider the words of God Most High: ﴿By the night when it covers, and by the day when it manifests itself, and by Him who created the male and the female, indeed your efforts are diverse.﴾ (92:1–4)

Night and day are complementary, not opposed; likewise the male and the female, and each has its own role and particular task. If you try to make the night day, or the male female, or the reverse, you have contravened this nature which the Creator, glorified is He, has chosen.

We have related the story of the man who passed by the village headman and found him beating a watchman (ghafīr) who was with him. He defended the watchman and said to the headman: "Why are you beating him, Uncle Ibrahim?" He said: "I passed by him and found him sleeping." The man said: "He slept, because he spent the day irrigating your land for you, and whoever plows does not also guard."

So: beneath the genus is the species, and this species is not equal; for if it were equal it would be a repetition with no benefit. Individuals differ and are distinguished. Therefore do not think that you are superior to others, for God Most High has distributed talents among His creatures: you excel in one thing, and another excels in something else. This is so that people may be bound together in the movement of life by need, not by favour, as we have said.

Therefore the man who sweeps the street for you is distinguished from you, because he performs a task you disdain to perform; and when this worker does a task for you, you must give him his wage. Whereas if he asks you a question, and you are the scholar or the holder of office... and so on, you answer him, but without taking any payment for that answer. You spent long years gathering knowledge, reading and listening until you reached this rank, and you acquired a specificity. So each of us, male or female, has a personal individuality that distinguishes him.

Here God Most High says to the wives of the Prophet: ﴿You are not like any (aḥad) of the women..﴾ (33:32). This is the specificity that distinguishes them from other women in general. The women in general are not exemplars, but the wives of the Prophet in particular are an exemplar for other women and a model to be followed.

The condition after this negation, ﴿if you are mindful of God..﴾ (33:32), means: their being wives of the Messenger of God is not in itself a distinction; the distinction and specificity lie in their piety toward God. Otherwise there have been wives of prophets who were not pious.

His words, Exalted is He: ﴿so do not be soft in speech, lest one in whose heart is a disease should be moved with desire..﴾ (33:32) mean: cut off the path to immorality from its beginning, do not approach its causes, and leave aside doubtful matters. The meaning of softness (khuḍūʿ) in speech is that a woman's speech, when she addresses men, has suppleness, affectation, or languor, or that the speech is accompanied by glances or closeness.

If they are compelled to speak with men, let them beware of these qualities. ﴿Lest one in whose heart is a disease should be moved with desire..﴾ (33:32). The meaning is: I do not accuse you, but any one of you cannot guarantee the man she speaks to; perhaps there is a disease in his heart,(1) so do not give him the opportunity.

Not being soft in speech does not mean speaking to people with harshness and roughness; rather, the intent is that matters be kept within their proper limits. Therefore He says after it: ﴿but speak in a good, fair manner (qawlan maʿrūfan)﴾ (33:32). Having forbidden improper conduct, the Qur'an offers the appropriate alternative, namely "fair speech" (al-qawl al-maʿrūf), which for a woman means moderate speech, and listening with the ear without letting her eye reach out to her interlocutor, because that may incite his desire for her and embolden him against her, and this is what God Most High wishes to prevent.

Thus it is related that a man saw his maidservant at the door speaking with a handsome young man, who was asking her about something, but she prolonged the conversation with him. The master of the house beat her and rebuked her for this conduct. The next day another young man came asking her about the same thing that his companion had asked about the day before, and she rushed at him with insults and abuse, after it had become clear to her what was in the heart of this one, and of those like him, of disease.

In another place in this surah it will come: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives and your daughters and the women of the believers that they should draw their outer garments close around them; that is more suitable so that they will be known and not be harmed. And God is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ (33:59), because when a man finds a woman modest, covering the allure of her body, he does not dare to approach her, and knows that she is not of this cheap category, so he stays within his limits.

The wise have said: as for a woman who displays her charms to men who are not her mahram, and insists on offering herself to men, it is as if she is saying to the man, "Fath, ya Bajam!" as one says to the heedless to alert them, thereby arousing his lust so that he becomes bold toward her.

God Most High therefore wills that the wives of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, first speak to people from behind a screen, and speak to people in a fair manner, a speech without softness or affectation, so that they are not exposed to evil, and no insolent or dissolute person is emboldened against them.

(1) Ibn ʿArafa said: disease in the heart is slackening from the truth; in the bodies it is the slackening of the limbs; in the eye it is the slackening of the gaze. A diseased eye is one in which there is slackness, and from this is His saying: ﴿so that one in whose heart is a disease should be moved with desire..﴾ (33:32), i.e., slackness regarding what He commanded and forbade. Ibn Manẓūr transmitted this in [Lisān al-ʿArab, entry: marḍ], and Ibn Kathīr said in his tafsir: "marḍ means dughl," and dughl is corruption; its root is the dense tree in which the people of corruption hide. [Lisān al-ʿArab, entry: dughl].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 33, verse 33:

Then the Truthful One, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And abide in your houses, and do not display yourselves as was the display of the former times of ignorance, and establish prayer, and give zakah, and obey Allah and His Messenger. Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, [O] people of the household, and to purify you with [complete] purification.﴾ (33)

The meaning of ﴿And abide in your houses...﴾ (33) [al-Ahzab]: stay in them (alzimna) and do not go out of them often. This is a code of conduct for women in general, because when a woman occupies herself with the work required of her in her house, with serving her husband and children and their affairs, she will not have the time for going out. For this reason, the husband often returns to find his wife busy with the work of the house, and perhaps he himself becomes impatient with this, because he does not find her free for him.

So: the woman who is idle in her house is the one who goes out often and handles her household's affairs from outside the house. If she had learned simple crafts, she would have taken care of her household's affairs and spared her husband [expense]. They have told us, for example, about the women in Damietta, how the woman there does everything and helps her husband, so much so that the daughter learns a trade and does not burden her father at her marriage, and even saves money that helps her husband after she marries.

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and do not display yourselves as was the display of the former times of ignorance...﴾ (33) [al-Ahzab]. The word tabarruj comes from burj, which is a fortress. The meaning of tabarruja is that she came out of the burj and appeared from it. The meaning is: do not come out of the fortress of concealment, and do not display adornment and the charms which must be covered.

He said ﴿the display of the former times of ignorance﴾ (33) [al-Ahzab], i.e. what was of display before Islam. A woman, by which we mean a female slave and not a free woman, would reveal the attractions of her body, even appearing almost naked, and they felt no shame in that. We have seen something like this, for example, in Africa.

As for free women in the time of ignorance, they had dignity and chastity, whereas places of prostitution were established for slave women, may Allah protect us. For this reason, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took the pledge from the believing women that they would not commit adultery, the wife of Abu Sufyan(1) said: "Does a free woman commit adultery, O Messenger of Allah?" She meant: this is something a free woman would disdain, even in the time of ignorance.

Among the meanings of burj is expansion, so the meaning is: do not widen the circle of display that the Shari'ah has defined, which is the face and the two hands.

In another place, He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And [as for] women past child-bearing(2) who have no [further] hope of marriage, there is no blame upon them for putting aside their [outer] clothing without displaying adornment...﴾ (60) [al-Nur].

And I marvel at a woman who reaches fifty or sixty, and then you see her applying rouge and white powder, not ashamed of the wrinkles of her face, and not respecting the age she has reached.

Then He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿and establish prayer, and give zakah...﴾ (33) [al-Ahzab]. The Qur'an often couples prayer and zakah, and begins with prayer, because it is the foundation of all obligations. Although in zakah you spend part of your wealth, and wealth is a branch of work, and work is a branch of time, in prayer you spend time itself and sacrifice it. So in prayer you are spending, as it were, ninety-seven and a half percent, besides the two and a half percent of zakah.

It is also understood from the giving of zakah here that a woman has her own independent financial liability, separate from the liability of others, whether father, husband or someone else, as evidenced by the fact that God obligated her to give zakah. But modern civilization has made a woman's wealth before marriage belong to her father, and after marriage to her husband, and has stripped the woman of her attribution to her father, and her attribution after marriage to her husband.

This matter is harder on a woman than depriving her of wealth, because attributing her to her husband is an erasure and an encroachment upon her identity. Look, for example, at Lady Aisha: we still say "Aisha bint Abi Bakr" until now, and no one has said that she is "Aisha, wife of Muhammad."

Then He, exalted is He, says: ﴿and obey Allah and His Messenger...﴾ (33) [al-Ahzab], because the matter is not limited to establishing prayer and giving zakah; there are many other matters that require obedience to Allah and obedience to the Messenger of Allah.

We note here that the verse conjoins the Messenger of Allah with his Lord, exalted is He, and the command comes in a single verb: ﴿and obey Allah and His Messenger...﴾ (33) [al-Ahzab]. When we survey this command in the Noble Qur'an, we find that sometimes it repeats the verb, as He says: ﴿and obey Allah and obey the Messenger...﴾ (12) [al-Taghabun].

And sometimes: ﴿and obey Allah and the Messenger﴾ (132) [Al 'Imran].

And sometimes He, exalted is He, says: ﴿Obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those in authority among you...﴾ (59) [al-Nisa'].

These formulations each have their own significance and meaning. When He says "Obey Allah and obey the Messenger," it is as if Allah has obedience in the general command, and the Messenger has obedience in the detail. The Truthful One, glory be to Him, commanded prayer and commanded zakah as a general command, then the Messenger explained that generality and detailed it, so he said: (Pray as you have seen me pray)(3), and he said: (Take from me your rites)(4).

So: the verb is repeated here because Allah has obedience in the general ruling, and the Messenger has obedience in its detailing. But if the verb comes singular, ﴿and obey Allah and the Messenger﴾ (132) [Al 'Imran], this means the command of Allah, exalted is He, coincides with the command of His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. So obedience is one; suppose Allah has an act and His Messenger has an act, then neither is separated from the other, as evidenced by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and they did not resent except that Allah and His Messenger had enriched them from His bounty...﴾ (74) [al-Tawbah].

He did not say "and His Messenger enriched them," lest someone say: each enriches according to his measure. Rather the verb came singular: ﴿Allah and His Messenger enriched them﴾ (74) [al-Tawbah].

Read also His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Allah and His Messenger have more right that they should satisfy Him, if they were believers﴾ (62) [al-Tawbah], and He did not say "that they should satisfy them both." As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those in authority among you...﴾ (59) [al-Nisa'], He did not repeat the command to obey with those in authority, because there is no obedience to those in authority except from within the obedience to Allah and the obedience to the Messenger of Allah.

Then He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, [O] people of the household, and to purify you with [complete] purification.﴾ (33) [al-Ahzab]. The rijs with a sin is the rijz with a zay, and it is filth, whether sensory, like carrion for example, and like wine, or moral, like sins and wrongdoings. The verse has gathered them: ﴿Indeed, intoxicants, gambling, [sacrificing on] stone alters [to other than Allah], and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan, so avoid it that you may be successful.﴾ (90) [al-Ma'idah]. Rijs may also mean hypocrisy and sickness.

The word ahl is said of a man's clan, but in customary usage it is applied to his wife. Among the other idioms for this meaning is what we say now when we go to visit a friend, for example: "I have with me the ahl (family) or the group," and some say: "I have with me the children," meaning by that the wife. Why? They said: because the woman's affair is built upon concealment, so if her name is built upon concealment, then likewise most of her obligations are built upon concealment, in the case of a man, and rarely does a ruling come specifically concerning her.

Therefore, Lady Asma' bint Umays(5), the wife of our master Ja'far ibn Abi Talib, who had emigrated to Abyssinia, when she returned asked: "Has anything been revealed concerning women during my absence?" They told her: "Nothing has been revealed." So she went to our master the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, how great is our disappointment and our loss, for there is nothing for us in the rulings." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to her: "Indeed you women are concealed within the men."(6)

Nevertheless, the Noble Qur'an was revealed with His saying, exalted is He:

﴿Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women, the believing men and believing women, the devoutly obedient men and devoutly obedient women, the truthful men and truthful women, the patient men and patient women, the humble men and humble women, the charitable men and charitable women, the fasting men and fasting women, the men who guard their private parts and the women who do so, and the men who remember Allah often and the women [who do so] - Allah has prepared for them forgiveness and a great reward.﴾ (35) [al-Ahzab].

And you note in this verse also: ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the impurity, [O] people of the household, and to purify you with [complete] purification﴾ (33) [al-Ahzab], that it speaks of women, but it observes the matter of women's concealment, so it returns to the masculine pronoun: ﴿to remove from you﴾ (33) [al-Ahzab], and did not say "from you" (feminine); likewise in ﴿and purify you with [complete] purification﴾ (33) [al-Ahzab]. And it is valid that He intends the people of the household all together, men and women.

1 She is Hind bint Utbah ibn Rabi'ah. Her reports before Islam are well known; she was an unbeliever at Uhud and did what she did to Hamzah. She embraced Islam on the day of the Conquest, after her husband Abu Sufyan. She died during the caliphate of Uthman. [al-Isabah of Ibn Hajar 8/206] Ibn Sa'd in his Tabaqat (10/226) mentioned that this occurred at the pledging of women to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Hind is the mother of Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan.
2 Al-qawa'id are those who have sat back from husbands. It is the plural of qa'id, meaning the elderly, aged woman. A woman "qa'adat" from menstruation and childbearing, i.e. it ceased for her. [Lisan al-Arab, root q-‘-d]
3 Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (231), and Ahmad in his Musnad (5/53), from the hadith of Malik ibn al-Huwayrith, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When the prayer comes, let one of you give the call to prayer and establish the iqamah, and let the eldest of you lead you, and pray as you see me pray."
4 From Jabir ibn Abd Allah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "I saw the Prophet (ﷺ) throw [pebbles] from his mount on the Day of Sacrifice, saying to us: 'Take your rites from me, for I do not know, perhaps I shall not perform Hajj after this Hajj of mine.'" Related by Ahmad in his Musnad (3/318), al-Nasa'i in his Sunan (5/270), and Muslim in his Sahih (1297).
5 She is Asma' bint Umays ibn al-Harith al-Khath'ami: a Companion who embraced Islam before the Prophet (ﷺ) entered the house of al-Arqam in Mecca, and emigrated to the land of Abyssinia with her husband Ja'far ibn Abi Talib. Then Ja'far was killed as a martyr at the battle of Mu'tah (8 AH), and she was married by Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, and bore him Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr. When Abu Bakr died, she was married by Ali ibn Abi Talib, and bore him children, and she died after Ali. Abu Nu'aym described her as one who made both emigrations and prayed towards both qiblas. [al-A'lam of al-Zirikli 1/306]
6 I have not found this hadith, but Imam Ahmad related in his Musnad (6/256), from the hadith of Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her: "Women are the counterparts of men," and likewise al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan (113). Al-Khattabi said in "Ma'alim al-Sunan" 1/79: "That is: their equals and their likes in creation and disposition, as though they were split from men."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 33, verse 34:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of Allah and wisdom.﴾ [al-Ahzab] That is: the wives of the Prophet. ﴿Of the verses of Allah﴾ [al-Ahzab]: that is, the verses of the Noble Qur'an. ﴿And wisdom﴾ [al-Ahzab]: that is, the sayings (hadith) of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Or: the conjunction of "wisdom" with "the verses of Allah" is an attribution of a quality to what it qualifies (ʿatf al-ṣifa ʿalā al-mawṣūf). But the first opinion is preferable, since the matter admits of latitude.

As for the meaning of ﴿remember﴾ [al-Ahzab]: we have said that dhikr (remembrance) is the summoning and recalling of a known matter from the periphery of consciousness to the focal point of consciousness. The meaning is: call to mind the remembrance of Allah and keep it constantly in your mind. This is why He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And the remembrance of Allah is greater﴾ [al-ʿAnkabut]: that is, greater than any act of worship, because acts of worship, as we have mentioned, require preparation, time, hardship, and freedom from preoccupation.

As for the remembrance of Allah, it runs on your tongue at any time and without preparation or hardship; your tongue is occupied with it at any time and in whatever state you are in. Read in this regard His saying in Surat al-Jumu'a: ﴿And when the prayer is concluded, disperse in the land and seek of the bounty of Allah, and remember Allah much that you may succeed﴾ [al-Jumu'a]. So since remembrance is that you keep Allah in your mind, no striving or work prevents you from it, for remembrance is the lightest of acts of worship and the easiest on the soul, and the heaviest in the scale.

Then reflect: ﴿Certainly there is for you in the Messenger of Allah an excellent pattern for whoever hopes in Allah and the Last Day and remembers Allah much﴾ [al-Ahzab].

From the greatness of our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), is that his mind was never free of the remembrance of his Lord, not for a moment. Therefore it was reported from him (ﷺ) that he said of himself: "My eyes sleep, but my heart does not sleep."(1)

Then the verse concludes with His saying: ﴿Indeed Allah is ever Subtle and Acquainted﴾ [al-Ahzab]. Lutf (subtlety) is precision in dealing with things and excellence in accomplishing affairs, whatever their means may be narrow. We have previously explained this meaning and said: harmful things, for example, the more subtle they are, the more severe they become. The iron you place on windows to protect you from wolves is not the iron that protects you from snakes, or from mosquitoes and flies, and so on. Therefore we find that the most deadly diseases come from subtle viruses that were not known.

Excellence in accomplishing affairs means penetrating things however fine they are. For example, you may be compelled to put your hand into a narrow space to take something inside it, and you cannot, so you seek help in that by a small child, because his hand is finer than yours, or you seek help with a more precise tool to accomplish this purpose.

The description of the Subtle is completed by the description of the All-Aware (al-Khabir). If lutf means precision in dealing with things and excellence in accomplishing them, then khibra (expertise) means knowing the place, and lutf is only achieved through expertise.

(1) A hadith agreed upon (muttafaq ʿalayh), related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (2113), Kitab Salat al-Tarawih, and likewise related by Muslim in his Sahih (738), Kitab Salat al-Musafirin, from the hadith of ʿAisha, that she said: "O Messenger of Allah, do you sleep before you pray witr?" He said: "O ʿAisha, my eyes sleep but my heart does not sleep."

Then the Exalted says:

﴿Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women, the believing men and believing women, the devout men and devout women, the truthful men and truthful women, the patient men and patient women, the humble men and humble women, the charitable men and charitable women, the fasting men and fasting women, the men who guard their chastity and the women who guard theirs, and the men who remember Allah much and the women who remember Him—Allah has prepared for them forgiveness and a great reward.﴾ (33:35)

We have said that this verse was revealed to comfort the heart of al-Sayyida Asma' bint Umays, the wife of our master Ja'far ibn Abi Talib, when she spoke to our master the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about the rulings, that they are revealed and directed mostly at men, and it appears that she spoke to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) concerning women, and that among them are those who, like men, are Muslims and believers... etc.

We observe that the verse began by mentioning Islam, then faith (iman). Which of the two precedes the other? The answer to this question is found in the words of the Exalted: ﴿The Bedouins say, "We have believed." Say, "You have not believed; but say, 'We have submitted,' and faith has not yet entered your hearts..."﴾ (49:14).

Islam is that you perform the acts of Islam regardless of whether your performance of them is out of faith or not, because Islam is the receiving of a ruling, whereas faith (iman) is that you believe in the One who issued the ruling and affirm the one who conveyed it to you. Accordingly, faith precedes Islam.

Therefore this verse came to expose those Bedouins who hid behind the outward acts of Islam while not believing in them. Faith may come after Islam when the acts of Islam are performed and become sweet to you, drawing you toward faith and affirmation.

Thus, those Bedouins rejoiced at His saying, ﴿and faith has not yet entered your hearts﴾ (49:14), and said, "Praise be to Allah," because (lammā, "not yet") is only used with what may yet come to be, as when you say: "Our orchard has not yet borne fruit," while the orchards have already borne fruit, and the meaning is that it will bear fruit later.

They said: Because there are many rulings whose lawgiver you do not believe in unless you perceive and taste their sweetness. The man who came to our master Ibrahim (peace be upon him) and asked him to spend the night with him, or to host him, and Ibrahim (peace be upon him) asked him about his religion, and he said that he was a Magian. So Ibrahim turned him away from his door, and his Lord rebuked him for that, saying to him: "O Ibrahim, do you want him to change his religion for the hospitality of one night, while I sustain him all his life though he disbelieves in Me?" Ibrahim hastened after the man until he caught up with him and invited him to his house. The man said: "Did you not rebuke me a little while ago? What has happened?" He said: "My Lord has rebuked me concerning you." The man said: "What a Lord! A Lord who rebukes His beloved concerning His enemies! I bear witness that there is no god but Allah."

This verse contains ten attributes, beginning with "the Muslim men and Muslim women" and ending with "the men who remember Allah much and the women who remember Him." It is as though Allah has realized the wish of al-Sayyida Asma' bint Umays in these ten attributes, which encompass men and women and include all kinds of obligation. It is a signal showing that the legal obligation of women is hidden within that of men, and these are the foundations.

The meaning of ﴿the devout men and devout women﴾ (33:35) is those who persist in worshipping Allah and obeying Him with humility and supplication. As we understand from His saying, ﴿the charitable men and charitable women﴾ (33:35), that a woman has her own independent financial responsibility and freedom to dispose of her money without her husband's permission, if she possesses an inheritance or a gift from her husband or from someone else; no one has guardianship over her.

We had already explained this matter in our discussion of zakat. This is one of the distinctions of women in Islam, for before Islam, and even in modern civilizations, a woman was dependent on her father or her husband. Charity (sadaqah) includes zakat, because Allah said concerning it: ﴿Alms are only for the poor and the needy and those employed to collect them...﴾ (9:60).

Charity is the more general heading. Its meaning is that you confirm (saddaqta) the Truth, the Exalted, when He entrusts you with a good thing, so you develop it through your effort and striving on the earth which He created. This is like what our master Abu Bakr did when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked him what he had done with his wealth that he had earned from the spoils. He said: "I gave all of it in charity." He said to him: "And what have you left for your family?" He said: "I left them Allah and His Messenger." When he asked Umar (may Allah be pleased with him), he said: "I gave half of it in charity, and I have left half for myself."(2)

Each of them dealt with his wealth in a manner logically appropriate to him.

If zakat is intended to increase and purify wealth, then charity is a gift intended only for the face of Allah and His reward in the Hereafter. It is as though the one who gives charity wishes to be dutiful and to acknowledge to Allah, the Giver, His favor, for Allah has enabled him with wealth that He did not enable the weak or the one unable.

Then the Exalted mentioned the obligation of fasting: ﴿the fasting men and fasting women﴾ (33:35). Fasting has taken a unique ruling among all the obligations, and the Exalted has given every obligation a special "scale" of reward except fasting, which has no fixed "scale." Therefore the Exalted said of it: "All of the son of Adam's deeds are for himself except fasting, for it is for Me, and I will reward it." (3) That is, it is a decision elevated above all. So why has fasting taken this rank?

They said: Because fasting is the only act of worship that no human has ever worshipped another human with. For example, in the testimony that there is no god but Allah, one might find someone praising another, saying to him: "There is nothing in existence but you; you are the one who benefits and the one who harms," and someone has said of himself: "I am the sole leader." Likewise in prayer we see someone bowing and prostrating to other than Allah, as we bow and prostrate in prayer; and likewise in zakat we draw near to the great or the powerful with gifts to them or to those around them.

But has a human ever said to another human: "I fast a month, or a day, to draw near to you"? No. Because fasting for a similar being is a subordination of the one fasted for, not of the one fasting, since he will be compelled to remain watching you all day: did you eat or did you not?

And because fasting is the only act of worship by which no human has drawn near to another human, Allah said of it in the sacred hadith: "Every deed of the son of Adam is for himself except fasting, for it is for Me, and I will reward it" (4). That is, its reward is outside what is determined, as we said.

Among the greatness of the obligation of fasting is also that Allah the Exalted has made lawful for us things and has forbidden us other things permanently. The one who bears the obligation grows accustomed to the lawful and does not become accustomed to what is forbidden to him, and this belief is firmly rooted in his soul, so much so that the forbidden never occurs to his mind at all; it never came to his mind once, for example, to drink wine or eat carrion. This matter is settled for him. So Allah wanted to perpetuate the pleasure of obligation for mankind, and He prescribed fasting, which makes forbidden to you today what was permitted to you yesterday and familiar until it became a habit.

So there is a difference between the permanence of habit and the pleasure of worship. Consider, for example, the day of Fitr. Breaking the fast is a habit for you on other days, and you are free to eat or not eat. But when the day of the Eid al-Fitr comes, your Lord takes you out of habit into worship, and makes it an obligation for you to break your fast before going out to the prayer (5).

Then the Exalted says: ﴿and the men who guard their chastity and the women who guard theirs﴾ (33:35). The matter of guarding chastity came after the mention of fasting, because fasting is abstention from the two desires of the belly and the private parts. The desire of the belly Allah made for preserving life through food and drink, and the desire of the private parts Allah made for preserving the species through marriage and procreation.

We have said that Allah the Exalted pleased al-Sayyida Asma', may Allah be pleased with her, who represents the female sex, so He mentioned the types of obligation sometimes for the masculine and sometimes for the feminine, but in doing so He observed the veiling of women, and here too He observes this matter. He says: ﴿and the men who guard their chastity and the women who guard theirs﴾ (33:35). When speaking of the masculine, He said ﴿the men who guard their chastity﴾ (33:35) and did not say "the women who guard their chastity," because the affairs of women should be concealed and protected.

Then the Exalted says: ﴿and the men who remember Allah much and the women who remember Him﴾ (33:35), and returns to the matter of concealment once more in His saying: ﴿Allah has prepared for them forgiveness and a great reward﴾ (33:35). He said "for them" by way of predominance of the masculine, and the veiling of women within men. This is an intended matter, meant as an honor for women and a protection of them, not neglect of them as some claim. Among this protection is what we say about women: "My family is with me," or "the children," or "the group," meaning by that their concealment and protection, not neglect of them or belittling of their standing.

Thus, when the Exalted pleased al-Sayyida Asma' on behalf of the Muslim woman, mentioning the feminine plural that corresponds to the masculine plural, He intended to build around women a wall of concealment in everything, even in the obligations.

We also observe in the context of the verse here that He placed forgiveness before reward, because the principle, as we have said, is that averting harm takes precedence over securing benefit. The Exalted promises His servants a reward for the good deed they performed, although He benefits nothing from it; its benefit returns to the obligated person himself. He benefits by obedience and receives its reward in the Hereafter.

As for the Exalted, He is free of need of us and of our obedience. Read the sacred hadith: "O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, were upon the most pious heart of one man among you, that would not increase My kingdom in anything; and if the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, were upon the most wicked heart of one man among you, that would not decrease My kingdom in anything" (6).

So: we are the beneficiaries of the obligations; in them is our welfare in this world, and then we receive the reward for them on the Day of Resurrection.

Therefore we find many of the messengers saying to their peoples: ﴿I do not ask you for any reward for it﴾ (26:109). As if he were saying: what I perform for you by conveying Allah's call, in the custom of economics and exchange, requires that I take a wage for it, because I am rendering you a service. But what would I take from you, you the destitute? My reward is great, which the obligated person cannot afford: ﴿My reward is only from Allah﴾ (10:72). He alone is able to repay me with what I deserve.

Describing the reward as "great" indicates magnitude in size, excellence in qualities, and extension in time, and these are the elements of greatness in a thing. And what reward is greater than Allah's reward for His servants in the Hereafter?

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 33, verse 36:

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says:

﴿It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decided a matter, that they should have any choice about their affair. And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly strayed into clear error.﴾ (36)

This verse also combines the masculine and feminine in ﴿It is not for a believing man or a believing woman...﴾ (36). It is a continuation of the previous verse: it serves what comes before it and also serves what comes after it. The root of its cause is that it was revealed concerning Abdullah ibn Jahsh and his sister Zaynab, when they refused Zaynab's marriage to Zayd ibn Harithah. So the believing man is Abdullah ibn Jahsh, and the believing woman is his sister Zaynab, in terms of them being the occasion of the revelation. Otherwise, the verse applies to all believing men and all believing women.

We have already mentioned the story of Zayd ibn Harithah. Its summary is that he was stolen from his family and sold in the slave market as a slave. Hakim ibn Hizam bought him, then gave him as a gift to the Lady Khadijah, Mother of the Believers. Khadijah, may Allah be pleased with her, then gave him to our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so he became a freedman (mawla) of the Messenger of Allah.

One day, while he was in the market, a group of his people saw him and recognized him, and they informed his father that he was in Medina. His father and his uncles came and told the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) his story, and asked for his return with them. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Let him choose. If he chooses you, then he is yours, and congratulations to you. If he chooses me, then it is not for me to surrender him." Zayd responded: "By Allah, I would never choose anyone over the Messenger of Allah."

Our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), wanted to reward Zayd for this act, so he ascribed him to himself, according to the custom of the Arabs at that time. So he called him Zayd ibn Muhammad (2).

When Allah, glorified is He, wished to end this custom, and a similar custom, the custom of zihar (a pre-Islamic form of divorce in which a man likened his wife to his mother), He revealed His saying: ﴿Allah has not made for any man two hearts within his body, nor has He made your wives whom you declare unlawful [by zihar] your mothers, nor has He made your adopted sons your sons...﴾ (4)

Just as a man does not have two hearts, so he does not have two fathers. Allah willed to begin with the adopted son of the Messenger of Allah, so that he would be a practical model before the people. The consequence of this phenomenon was that the adopted son would inherit from the adopter after his death, and that the adopter's marriage to the wife of the adopted son would be forbidden.

It is true that ending this custom meant ending a corrupt social system that existed in the Arabian Peninsula. But at the same time, it was evidence that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had adopted in the manner the Arabs adopted, and that Allah, the Exalted, nullified this act of the Messenger of Allah. This would open the door for the enemies of the Messenger of Allah to gloat over it and for their tongues to attack it. Therefore, the Truthful, glorified is He, addressed this matter with the treatment of a Lord, by enforcing the command in support of a beloved of His, so that the Messenger's action was not tarnished. Rather, He made his act just, and His judgment is more just. So He said: ﴿Call them by [the names of] their fathers; that is more just in the sight of Allah...﴾ (5)

The meaning is: if you considered it a matter of justice and love to sponsor these children and attribute them to yourselves, then this is human justice. But the judgment of Allah is more just and more equitable. It is also an honor for the Messenger of Allah that Allah returns his judgment to the judgment of his Lord, and an honor for the Messenger of Allah that the principle in the matter is his, and that he judges, and then Allah returns his judgment to His judgment. This is a dignity given to the Messenger of Allah.

So His saying, exalted is He, ﴿That is more just in the sight of Allah...﴾ (5) means: the act of Muhammad was just and equitable by the law of men. But Muhammad came to change the laws of men with the laws of the Lord of men. By this, our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), got out of this predicament.

As for Zayd, Allah compensated him for the harm that befell him due to his lineage being ended from the Messenger of Allah. Zayd ibn Harithah, after having been Zayd ibn Muhammad, was compensated and vindicated by Allah, who made him the only one of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah whose name is mentioned in the Noble Qur'an explicitly and clearly. He, glorified is He, said: ﴿So when Zayd had no longer any need for her, We married her to you...﴾ (37) So Zayd was immortalized in a Book that is recited and worshipped through its recitation until the Day of Resurrection.

The connection of Zayd ibn Harithah to what we are concerned with, His saying, exalted is He, ﴿It is not for a believing man or a believing woman...﴾ (36), is that he married the Lady Zaynab bint Jahsh. The Messenger of Allah married her to him, and this verse was revealed concerning Zaynab and her brother Abdullah (3).

The meaning of ﴿It is not for a believing man or a believing woman...﴾ (36): the phrase "it is not" (ma kana) means that it is something remote that cannot occur to the mind; that is, it is a matter that is unlikely and unimaginable. The negation indicates the denial of this matter. The believing man and the believing woman, since faith has entered their hearts, cannot leave the command of Allah and His judgment, or the command of His Messenger, to their own choice.

﴿It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decided a matter, that they should have any choice about their affair...﴾ (36). Otherwise, there is no faith in Allah, nor in the Messenger of Allah.

If you say: how is this consistent with Allah having affirmed choice? We say: there is a difference between a choice that falls within the obligation, where if you wish you do it or you do not do it, and something that is about establishing the obligation itself at the beginning. The servants have no part in establishing the thing that they are obligated to do. Rather, if I obligate them, then I am the owner of the obligation. Whether they obey it or disobey it is another matter. The servants have no right to propose the obligation according to their own desires, because the obligation belongs to Me, and they have the choice in obeying it and accepting it. Since it has been established that they believed in Allah and believed in the Messenger of Allah, it was obligatory upon them to accept the command and not to turn away from it to something else.

As for the story of Zayd's divorce from Zaynab, and then the marriage of our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), to her, it is a story about which the orientalists and the malicious have spoken much, and they have dared to say about the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) words that are not fitting regarding him (ﷺ). Among what they say is that Muhammad loved Zaynab and wanted her for himself, so he ordered her to provoke Zayd until he divorced her and he married her.

We say to these fools: first, Zaynab bint Jahsh al-Asadiyya is the daughter of the aunt of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was responsible for managing her money and taking care of her affairs, and she grew up under his eye. If he had wanted her for himself, he would have married her from the beginning. This is by the explicit text of the Qur'an: ﴿And you concealed within yourself that which Allah was to disclose...﴾ (37)

If you want to know what the Messenger of Allah concealed, take it from what Allah disclosed. What Allah disclosed is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿so that there will be no difficulty for the believers concerning the wives of their adopted sons...﴾ (37) This demolishes all your claims against the Messenger of Allah.

As for their claim that the heart of the Messenger of Allah was preoccupied with Zaynab, we say: why do you make the preoccupation of Muhammad's heart a sexual preoccupation? If you followed the story from its beginning, something else would become clear to you. When the Messenger of Allah sent someone to propose to Zaynab, her brother Abdullah and her sister Hamnah thought that he had come to propose to her for the Messenger of Allah. When they learned that he was proposing to her for his freedman Zayd, they were all angry. How could a noblewoman of Quraysh and the daughter of the aunt of the Messenger of Allah marry a slave? But when they knew that the matter was from Allah, they submitted to it and agreed.

Then, after Zaynab married Zayd, she looked down on him, and he even felt that she despised him because of the difference between them. Zayd used to complain to the Messenger of Allah about his wife's bad treatment of him, and that, as we say, she was making his life miserable, and that she lived with him in the marital home in form but not in heart. But his love for the Messenger of Allah prevented him from divorcing her, and he also did not want to lose this honor that he had gained by marrying the daughter of the aunt of the Messenger of Allah.

Each time Zayd complained about Zaynab, our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), would say to him: ﴿Keep your wife and fear Allah...﴾ (37) If the Messenger had wanted her for himself, he would have said to him: divorce her, and he would have found the opportunity open before him.

Here we must examine the relationship of woman to man. The Creator, glorified is He, created man for woman and woman for man. Therefore, we find the Arab woman Umm Iyas, when she advised her daughter when Harith proposed to her, saying: "O my daughter, if you were left without advice, you would be the most independent of people from it. And if a woman were to be independent of a husband because of the wealth of her parents and their great need for her, you would be the most independent of people. But men were created for women, and women were created for men. And if advice were left out because of the superiority of manners, you would be left out of it. But it is a reminder for the heedless and a help for the wise."

We have said that a person can live in the best state of food, drink, clothing and shelter, but nevertheless he can never do without a wife, and likewise the woman. Therefore the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If I were to order anyone to prostrate to anyone, I would order the wife to prostrate to her husband" (4).

Why? Because the husband gives her what her father, mother and brothers give, and adds to that what they cannot and are not able to give.

The point is that woman is for man, and man is for woman, however much they put up walls of honor, or of tyranny, or other things.

As for Zayd, the matter was difficult, because Allah, the Exalted, made marriage have three stages, which are mentioned in His saying: ﴿And among His signs is that He created for you from yourselves mates that you may find tranquility in them; and He placed between you affection and mercy...﴾ (21)

The first is that the husband should find tranquility in his wife, feel secure with her, and be at rest beside her when she wipes his sweat and embraces him after the fatigue of the day and the hardships of life. If tranquility is prevented by the troubles of life, then let there be affection between them that unites them. And why not? When you accompany a friend, for example, for a long time, you find affection for him in your heart, and you find that this affection has a price, so you bear with him if he errs, and forgive him if he wrongs you. How much more so with a wife: is she not more deserving of this affection?

If affection is also lost, then let mercy remain between the spouses, so that each of them has mercy on the other if old age or illness or something else befalls him.

Zayd and Zaynab reached a stage in which tranquility, affection and mercy were lost because of the difference between them.

Another matter: if the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had thought about Zaynab's matter, why do you turn him toward thinking about instinct? Why do you not turn him toward the rank of fairness? He was the one who compelled Zaynab to marry Zayd, though she was a noblewoman of Quraysh and he was a owned slave. When he put her in this predicament, he wanted to console her and to correct what had happened by taking her to himself, so that she would become one of the Mothers of the Believers.

Then, who prevented a messenger whom Allah described as a human from having this desire? All the earlier messengers had this... on the assumption that the Messenger of Allah desired Zaynab. But people did not think well.

What shows us that this matter was a purely divine arrangement is the spiritual sportsmanship we find among our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), his freedman Zayd, and his cousin Zaynab. The three of them shared a spiritual sportsmanship, as we would say now: so-and-so has a sporting spirit.

That is: he accepts defeat with a high spirit, without enmities or grudges. All of them submitted to the command of Allah with this spirit of faith.

As for those who take His saying, exalted is He, about His Messenger: ﴿and you feared the people, while Allah has more right that you fear Him...﴾ (37), and use it as a slur against the Messenger, they should know that fear is of two kinds: fear of something that you fear will harm you, and fear of modesty. The fear in ﴿and you feared the people...﴾ (37) is fear of modesty. It is sufficient that the Truthful, glorified is He, said concerning the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) (5): ﴿Indeed, that was troubling the Prophet, and he was shy of you, but Allah is not shy of the truth...﴾ (53)

So Allah, the Exalted, revealed: ﴿It is not for a believing man or a believing woman...﴾ (36) Ibn Kathir cited it in his tafsir (3/489), and al-Suyuti in "Asbab al-Nuzul" (p. 220).

Some people came, ate and left, then others came, ate and left, and three men remained talking and did not leave, while the Messenger of Allah wanted to be alone with Zaynab, his bride, while they were sitting. He went out, then returned, then went out again, until he was informed that the people had left. He was extremely shy. So the words of Allah, the Exalted, were revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, do not enter the houses of the Prophet unless you are permitted for a meal, without waiting for its preparation. But when you are invited, then enter; and when you have eaten, disperse without seeking to remain for conversation. Indeed, that was troubling the Prophet, and he was shy of you, but Allah is not shy of the truth...﴾ (53) See al-Wahidi's Asbab al-Nuzul (p. 205) and Ibn Kathir's tafsir (3/503).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 33, verse 37:

It seems that the Messenger of Allah wished to console her, or to lift her spirits, in return for what he had compelled her to do by marrying her to Zayd, and in return for her living with him reluctantly. When Zayd came, she said to him: "The Messenger of Allah has come and asked about you, and he said to me: 'Blessed is Allah, the best of creators.'" He said to her: "O Zaynab, I see that you should be for the Messenger of Allah, for you have fallen into his heart, and I see that I should divorce you so that the Messenger of Allah may marry you." Relief appeared on her, and she was amazed, as though she did not believe it: "If you divorce me, I will marry the Messenger of Allah?" This exchange was merely words.

By Allah, if this speech had been said in another situation, and to someone other than Zayd, the blood would have boiled in his veins and he would have done what he did. Consider instead the faith-based discipline with which Zayd was adorned.

He, may He be exalted, says regarding this matter:

﴿And [remember] when you said to him on whom Allah bestowed favor and you bestowed favor, "Keep your wife and fear Allah," while you concealed within yourself that which Allah is to disclose. And you feared the people, while Allah has more right that you fear Him. So when Zayd had no longer any need for her, We married her to you in order that there not be upon the believers any discomfort concerning the wives of their adopted sons when the adopted sons have no longer any need for them. And ever is the command of Allah accomplished.﴾ (33:37)

The meaning of ﴿And [remember] when you said...﴾ (33:37): Remember well and ponder the matter of Zayd in your mind. Remember when you said to him on whom Allah bestowed the favor of faith, and the intended one is Zayd: you bestowed favor upon him first by manumission, and you bestowed favor upon him through the law of humanity by making him your son, and you bestowed favor upon him by marrying him to a woman of Quraysh, who was your paternal aunt's daughter, while he was a slave. Then you bestowed favor upon him when you said to him, ﴿Keep your wife and fear Allah...﴾ (33:37).

But why did you say this word, O Muhammad? Was it out of fear of the people's speech, that they would say: "He married the wife of his adopted son"? How could that be, when this is intended by Allah, the Exalted: He wants to end the custom of adoption, and to end it at your hands. You concealed it out of fear of people's speech, but Allah disclosed it when He informed you of this matter, and that its end would be at your hands by your marrying the wife of your adopted son. ﴿And Allah has more right that you fear Him...﴾ (33:37). So leave the people alone.

Therefore He, glory be to Him, said in another place: ﴿Those who convey the messages of Allah and fear Him and fear none except Allah...﴾ (33:39).

We have previously explained that his fear, peace be upon him, was not fear of something that would harm him; rather it was the shyness of wishing that the Messenger of Allah repel suspicion from himself.

As for His saying, ﴿So when Zayd had no longer any need for her, We married her to you...﴾ (33:37): al-watar (وطر) is the things that suit a man's livelihood, so its meaning is aim or need. We have previously said that a man's need from his wife is that she be a source of tranquility (sakan); if not, then affection (mawaddah) that unites them; if not, then mutual mercy (rahmah).

Zayd lacked all these stages with his wife: he found with her neither tranquility, nor affection, nor mercy. So why then would he continue in the bond with her? Therefore he would go to the Messenger of Allah and complain to him of what he encountered from Zaynab, and the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, would say to him:

﴿Keep your wife and fear Allah...﴾ (33:37)

Consider here this faith-based discipline between our master the Messenger of Allah, Zayd, and Zaynab, may Allah be pleased with them: when Zayd divorced Zaynab, the Messenger left her to complete her waiting period (iddah). When her waiting period was complete, he said: "O Zayd, go to Zaynab and propose to her on my behalf."¹ What greatness is this! The Messenger of Allah sends the divorcer to propose on his behalf to the divorced woman. This indicates his trust in Zayd, and that he had completed his need from Zaynab and no longer had any want of her.

Zayd entered upon Zaynab and said to her: "Rejoice, O Zaynab, for the Messenger of Allah has sent me to propose to you for him." She said: "By Allah, I will not answer until I prostrate in thanks to Allah." Zaynab then stood and prostrated. At that, Zayd returned to the Messenger of Allah and informed him of what Zaynab had done. Then the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, came to her and entered upon her without seeking permission.²

Why did the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, enter upon her without seeking permission? They said: because she had by then become his wife, as He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿So when Zayd had no longer any need for her, We married her to you...﴾ (33:37), meaning: Allah married her to him from above the seven heavens.

Therefore, when Zaynab sat with the wives of the Prophet, peace be upon him, and this too is among the faith-based disciplines, she would say to them: "I take pride over all of you, that your guardians married you, while my Lord married me, so none of them dared to answer her."³

Not only this, but she also vouched for the Messenger of Allah. She said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, I vouch for you with three things." The Messenger of Allah smiled and said: "What is the first?" She said: "The first is that my grandfather and your grandfather are one. The second is that Allah married me from above the seven heavens. The third is that the one who acted as my emissary in the marriage was not Zayd, but Jibril."⁴

What greatness is this that we notice in this story, and what lofty faith-based discipline from the Messenger of Allah and his companions!

Thus: the Messenger of Allah did not marry Zaynab; rather, his Lord married her to him. Therefore we say to those who are eager to delve into this matter, and who reckon it a slur against the Messenger of Allah: understand the difference between zawwaja and tazawwaja. Tazawwaja means that he married by himself and by his own desire; zawwaja means that another married him off. The word ﴿zawwajnakaha...﴾ (33:37) contains the verb zawwaja, and the pronoun (nā) is the subject, referring to the Truthful One, glory be to Him; the kāf is for addressing the Messenger of Allah and is the first object; and the hā' refers to Lady Zaynab and is the second object of the verb zawwaja.

So the Messenger of Allah, in this matter and in all his wives, did not go against the command of Allah. So be fair, for the matter does not rest with Muhammad, but with the Lord of Muhammad. Read, if you wish: ﴿It may be that his Lord, if he divorces you, will substitute for him wives better than you, submissive, faithful, obedient, penitent, worshipful, who fast, previously married or virgins﴾ (66:5).

Then suppose that Muhammad did it: what is the fault in it, when plurality was already present? The Messenger of Allah did not initiate plurality. Plurality existed among the prophets and messengers, and among you and with you.

As for those who accuse the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, of having expanded for himself, marrying nine, while constricting his community to four, the answer is that Allah, the Exalted, ruled that the wives of the Messenger are the mothers of the believers. As long as they are mothers of the believers, no one may marry them after the Messenger. As for other believing women, if a man has seven, for example, he must part from three of them, and those three will find someone to marry. So the Messenger must keep all his wives, and other believers must part with whatever exceeds four.

Another point: you think that Allah granted His Messenger this matter, but in reality Allah constricted him when compared with the general body of believers. The believer may keep four wives; if one dies, he marries another, and if he divorces one, he marries a replacement. If all of them die or he divorces them, he may marry others until he completes four. Thus a believer may marry a large number of women.

As for the Messenger of Allah: yes, he married nine, but his Lord addressed him saying: ﴿Women are not lawful for you hereafter, nor to exchange them for other wives, even if their beauty pleases you...﴾ (33:52). So who was constricted, then? Muhammad, or his community?

Then, O people, notice the difference between the exception in the number and the exception in the thing counted. Did Allah make an exception for His Prophet in the number, from four to nine, or did He make an exception for him in a specific counted category? He made the exception in the counted category, not in the number, because if He had made it in the number, then whenever one of his wives died he could marry another. Rather, the matter was confined to a specific counted group, such that if all of them died, it would not be lawful for him, peace be upon him, to marry anyone after them.

After that, does the ruling against the Messenger remain as such? No. It was at the beginning of the matter; afterward, when affairs settled and Allah made His Messenger secure, He said to him: "Do what you wish, for you are trusted regarding your community."⁷

Then we say: suppose the Messenger of Allah had a choice in this matter, and it had not been previously determined. Did his action not lead to the abolition of the custom of adoption? And was the prophethood taken from the Messenger of Allah after he did what he did? Therefore the will of Allah and the will of His Messenger do not contradict.

Those who criticized our master the Messenger of Allah in this matter are like those who criticized our master Yusuf, peace be upon him, when Allah said of him: ﴿And she certainly desired him, and he would have desired her...﴾ (12:24). It is as though they are more jealous for Yusuf than his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic. Yes, Yusuf "desired her," meaning he considered her or something else. We will not tell you what is correct so that you may remain in your perplexity; but did Allah take the prophethood from him after he desired her? Therefore his desire for her did not contradict the prophethood, and what you say about this matter is idle meddling on your part.

Then comes the reason for this matter: ﴿So that there will not be upon the believers any discomfort concerning the wives of their adopted sons when the adopted sons have no longer any need for them.﴾ (33:37) Then the verse concludes with what leaves no room for doubt regarding the Messenger of Allah: ﴿And ever is the command of Allah accomplished.﴾ (33:37), meaning: it must occur, and it will not be left to any other person, lest the matter of abolishing the custom of adoption be spoiled. Therefore the Messenger of Allah's marriage to the wife of his adopted son was only to lift discomfort from all the believers, and now it is permissible for every adopter to marry the wife of his adopted son.

1 Ibn Sa'd related in al-Tabaqat al-Kubra (10/101) from the hadith of Anas, who said: "When the waiting period of Zaynab bint Jahsh had ended, the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, said to Zayd ibn Harithah: 'I find no one more trustworthy in my sight or more reliable in my soul than you. Go to Zaynab and propose to her on my behalf...' Zayd said: 'O Zaynab, rejoice, the Messenger of Allah mentions you.'" But Ibn Sa'd also related in al-Tabaqat (10/99) that after the end of Zaynab's waiting period, the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, was seized by a swoon, then came to himself smiling, and said: "Whoever goes to Zaynab to give her good news that Allah has married her to me from heaven." Aisha said: "Salma, the servant of the Messenger of Allah, went out running and told her, and she gave her an ornament she wore..."
2 Said by Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him: "Zaynab replied to Zayd: 'I will do nothing until I consult my Lord,' then she went to her place of prayer, and the Qur'an was revealed: ﴿So when Zayd had no longer any need for her, We married her to you...﴾ (33:37). He said: The Messenger of Allah came and entered upon her without permission." Related by Ibn Sa'd in al-Tabaqat al-Kubra (10/101), and Ibn al-Athir in Usd al-Ghaba (7/125).
3 Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (7420) from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik that Zaynab used to boast over the wives of the Prophet, peace be upon him, saying: "Your guardians married you off, but Allah married me from above the seven heavens."
4 Mentioned by Ibn Hajar al-'Asqalani in Fath al-Bari (13/412) with some of these wordings, from the mursal of al-Sha'bi: "Zaynab said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I am the one among your wives with the greatest right over you. I am the best of them in marriage, the most honored in emissary, and the closest of them in kinship. The Merciful married you to me from above His Throne, and Jibril was the emissary in that. I am the daughter of your paternal aunt, and none of your wives is a relative of yours except me.'" Related by al-Tabari and Abu al-Qasim al-Tahawi in his "Kitab al-Hujjah wa al-Tibyan."
5 Sa'ihat: that is, fasting women. This was said by Abu Hurayrah, Aisha, Ibn Abbas and many others. Ibn Kathir, in his tafsir (4/390), mentions thirteen other scholars who held this view. Then he said: Zayd ibn Aslam and the daughter of Abd al-Rahman said: sa'ihat means emigrating women. The first view is preferable, and Allah knows best.
6 Thayyib: a woman who has previously been married, whether divorced or widowed. Ibn Manzur said in Lisan al-Arab (article: th-y-b): "A thayyib among women is one who has married and separated from her husband in any manner after he had consummated with her."
7 This is His saying: ﴿You may put off whom you will of them and take to you whom you will...﴾ (33:51). However, al-Qurtubi weakened the view that this verse abrogates His saying: ﴿Women are not lawful for you hereafter...﴾ (33:52). Al-Qurtubi (8/5483) preferred that its meaning is an expansion for the Prophet, peace be upon him, in leaving off the turn-taking, so that it was not obligatory for him to divide equally among his wives. He said: "This view is the one that fits what has passed, and its meaning is established in the Sahih from Aisha, who said: I used to be jealous of those who gave themselves to the Messenger of Allah, and I would say: Does a woman give herself to a man? Then when Allah revealed ﴿You may put off whom you will of them...﴾ (33:51), Aisha said: By Allah, I see that your Lord only hastens to fulfill your desire."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 33, verse 38:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿There is no restriction upon the Prophet in what Allah has ordained for him.﴾ [al-Ahzab] That is, no sin or blame. ﴿In what Allah has ordained for him.﴾ [al-Ahzab] That is: how can you blame the Messenger of Allah for carrying out a command that Allah ordained for him? And consider the words ﴿ordained for him﴾ [al-Ahzab]. That is, for his benefit. He did not say "ordained upon him." Since it is Allah who ordained this, then take the matter up to Him, for His Messenger bears no fault in it.

This matter is exactly like the matter of the Isra' (the Night Journey). When the Messenger of Allah informed his people of the news of the Isra', they said: "O Muhammad, do you claim that you went to Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) in one night, when we travel to it on the backs of camels for a month?" (1) This was foolishness on their part, because Muhammad did not say "I traveled (saraytu)"; rather he said "I was taken on a journey (usri bi)." So the one who took him on the journey was his Lord, may He be mighty and majestic. Therefore the matter is not the act of Muhammad, but the act of Allah.

We have already given an illustrative example of this, and to Allah belongs the highest likeness. We said: suppose a man said to you, "I took my small son up to the summit of (Everest)." Would you say to him, "How did your son climb the summit of (Everest)?"

But now we have benefited from the saying of the deniers: "Do you claim, O Muhammad, that you went to Bayt al-Maqdis in one night, when we travel to it on the backs of camels for a month?" Because the foolishness of the denier leads him to the opposite of what he intended by his foolishness. We now take this saying as evidence in refuting those who say that the Isra' was a dream, or that it was in the spirit without the body.

For if the Messenger of Allah had said, "I saw in a dream that I went to Bayt al-Maqdis," they would not have made this statement. Thus the people understood that the Messenger of Allah went to Bayt al-Maqdis with his spirit and his body; otherwise they would not have compared their going with his going. Those who witnessed this event made this statement, so how can we come today and say: the Isra' was a dream, or was in the spirit without the body?

As for His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿The practice of Allah concerning those who passed away before, and the command of Allah is a decree determined.﴾ [al-Ahzab] That is: his brothers among the earlier Messengers, or what was practiced before Islam of plurality of wives. So the Messenger of Allah was not an innovator in this matter.

﴿And the command of Allah is a decree determined.﴾ [al-Ahzab] You will notice that the previous verse ended with His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And the command of Allah is ever accomplished.﴾ [al-Ahzab, 37] One might say: yes, accomplished at the time in which these events occurred. Therefore He says here: ﴿And the command of Allah is a decree determined﴾ [al-Ahzab, 38], meaning that what happened to the Messenger of Allah was determined from eternity, and nothing departs from the decree of Allah. It is authentically established that the pen has dried over what was written and what was decreed. (2)

(1) Ibn Hisham mentioned in al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah (2/4): When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) rose in the morning after the Isra' with him, he came to the Quraysh and informed them of the news. Most people said: "By Allah, this is a clear matter. By Allah, the caravan takes a month to travel from Mecca to Syria going and a month returning. Will Muhammad go there in a single night and return to Mecca?"

(2) Al-Bukhari recorded in his Sahih (5076) that Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "I am a young man, and I fear for myself the risk of sin, and I do not have what I need to marry women." He remained silent toward me. Then I said the same again, and he remained silent. Then I said the same to him again, and he remained silent. Then I said the same, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O Abu Hurayrah, the pen has dried over what you will encounter." It was also recorded by Ibn Abi Asim in al-Sunnah (1/50, 51), and al-Nasa'i in his Sunan (6/59).

Allah, glorified and exalted, was bringing us back to His words about His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: ﴿And you feared the people, while Allah has more right that you fear Him...﴾ [al-Ahzab: 37]. The messengers do not fear anything in conveying the message from Allah. It is as if He, exalted is He, negated for the Messenger ﷺ that his fear should be in conveying the message; rather, his fear was modesty, lest the tongues of his people should gossip about him. Otherwise, they do not possess for him anything that could harm him or frighten him.

We note here that ﴿Those who convey the messages of Allah and fear Him, and fear none except Allah...﴾ [al-Ahzab: 39] is a mubtada' (subject of a nominal sentence) of which no predicate (khabar) is stated, because His words, ﴿And Allah suffices as Reckoner﴾ [al-Ahzab: 39], are not the khabar of this mubtada'; rather, they are a comment upon it. So where is the khabar of this mubtada'? They said: its estimated form is "Those who convey the messages of Allah... cannot be accused of having feared people for the sake of conveying (the message)."

﴿And Allah suffices as Reckoner﴾ [al-Ahzab: 39], i.e., you will not hold them to account; rather, Allah will hold them to account. And the requirement of accountability with the Messenger of Allah, if he did something that was not proper for him, would have been that the message be withdrawn from him and that Allah bring another prophet, but none of this happened.

(1) It is permissible that His words, ﴿Those who convey the messages of Allah...﴾ [al-Ahzab: 39], be an adjectival description (sifah) of ﴿those who passed away before...﴾ [al-Ahzab: 38].

Then the context returns to another matter in the question of adoption, and He, glorified is He, says:

﴿Muhammad is not the father of any one of your men, but he is the Messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets. And Allah is ever, of all things, Knowing.﴾ (33:40)

He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Muhammad is not the father of any one of your men..﴾ Because dealing with the matter of adoption is more important than his (ﷺ) being the father of any of you. For him to be someone's father, that is, that he should be the father of one of you, would not benefit that person in anything. What benefits him is the conveyance of the message from Allah, and that his Lord's method, which makes him happy in his religion and his worldly life, be carried to him.

So, your joy in the Messenger of Allah as a Messenger takes precedence over your joy in him as a father. Otherwise, how many people have fathers and yet are wretched in life, of no worth!

His saying ﴿is not..﴾ The negation here conveys denial. He denies and rejects that he is the father of any one of your men. Consider the greatness of the Qur'anic expression in the phrase ﴿of your men..﴾. He did not say, for example, "the father of any one of you." Why? They said: because he (ﷺ) was the father of ʿAbd Allah, al-Qasim and Ibrahim, and they were all of them men, and he (ﷺ) was their father. So the phrase ﴿of your men..﴾ came to exclude these three, because they did not reach the level of manhood. Thus Muhammad was never the father of any [adult] man, even if he was the father of young children who had not reached the stage of manhood.

His saying ﴿but..﴾ means: more important than his being a father is that he is the Messenger of Allah. ﴿But the Messenger of Allah..﴾ This is not all; rather, also ﴿and the Seal of the Prophets..﴾, that is, the Messenger and Prophet who seals the messages, so that no new message may be added after him.

This is an issue on which the orientalists stopped, objecting. They say: the Qur'an states: ﴿And [mention] when Allah took the covenant of the prophets: "Whatever I give you of Scripture and wisdom and then there comes to you a Messenger confirming what is with you, you must believe in him and support him."﴾ (3:81)

Muhammad (ﷺ) is among the prophets from whom this covenant was taken, as evidenced by: ﴿And [mention] when We took from the prophets their covenant, and from you, and from Noah..﴾ (33:7).

So: Allah took the covenant from the prophets that, as part of their principles, they should inform their peoples of the coming of a new Messenger, and that if he came to them they must believe in him and support him, just as ʿIsa (peace be upon him) gave good news of the message of Muhammad (ﷺ), saying: ﴿And a messenger who will come after me, whose name is Ahmad..﴾ (61:6).

How then does Allah inform that Muhammad is the Seal of the Prophets while he is one of them? We say: yes, he is one of them, but if they were commanded to give good news and to inform their peoples of a Messenger who would come, then he (ﷺ) was commanded to inform his people that he is the Seal of the Prophets and Messengers.

For this reason it is related that a man claimed prophethood in the time of al-Ma'mun, so he ordered him placed in prison. After several months another man appeared claiming prophethood, and al-Ma'mun saw fit to confront each of them with the other. He brought the first claimant and said to him: "This man claims he is a prophet; what do you say about him?" He said: "He is a liar, because I have not sent anyone [claiming it] who has risen to the station of divinity, but merely that he is a prophet."

And the woman who also claimed prophethood in the time of al-Ma'mun, when he stood her before him, asked her, saying: "Did you not know that the Messenger of Allah said: 'There is no prophet after me'(1)?" She said: "Yes, but he did not say, 'There is no prophetess after me!'"

Then the Truth, glorified is He, concludes this matter with His saying: ﴿And Allah is ever, of all things, Knowing.﴾ (33:40). Since Allah, exalted is He, is Knowing of all things, no one has the right to object, for He, glorified is He, is the one who places the suitable Messenger in the suitable place and the suitable time, and He, glorified is He, knew that the message of Muhammad would encompass all time and all place.

1. Among what has been narrated as evidence that there is no prophet after the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is the hadith of Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) left ʿAli ibn Abi Talib behind during the expedition of Tabuk, and he said: 'O Messenger of Allah, you leave me behind with the women and the children.' He said: 'Are you not pleased to be to me in the position of Harun to Musa, except that there is no prophet after me?' Narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad (1/182)."

O you who have believed, remember Allah with much remembrance. (33:41)

Our Lord, glory be to Him, commanded us to remember Him with much remembrance, because remembrance (dhikr) is the foundation of acts of worship and the easiest of them for the believer. Therefore we find that our Lord commands us to it at the conclusion of acts of worship such as prayer, fasting and pilgrimage, and He made it greater, saying: ﴿And the remembrance of Allah is greater...﴾ (29:45).

Remembrance is the occupation of the memory (al-dhakira), which is a region in the brain. We have said that a person receives information at the focus of his consciousness (bu'rat al-shu'ur). If he wishes to retain it until the time he needs it, he stores it in the memory (al-hafiza), or in the margin of consciousness (hashiyat al-shu'ur). For example, you see a person and say: "I have not seen this man for twenty years, and the last time I saw him was in such-and-such a place."

So remembrance is of something that was present in the focus of consciousness. Remembrance means a matter that you have, with a reality that had its moment of existence, but a lapse of attention moved it to the margin of consciousness or to the memory. After that, we want you not to forget it in the margin or in a remote region such that recalling it requires effort; rather, I keep it always in a region close to you, so that recalling it is easy without hardship.

Likewise, your remembrance of Allah should be: He is the vital matter that should always remain in your remembrance, forever and ever. How could you forget the remembrance of your Lord, when He took the covenant from you while you were in the world of the atoms (ʿālam al-dharr), and took from you the acknowledgment that He, glory be to Him, is your Lord? The Real, glory be to Him, created the intellect to receive information through the means of perception, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And Allah brought you out from the wombs of your mothers, knowing nothing, and He made for you hearing, sight and hearts, that you may give thanks.﴾ (16:78)
