Thus hearing and sight are the foundation of the senses, and by them we know what we did not know when we came out from the wombs of our mothers. When we receive information, some people think that people differ in it by intelligence and dullness: one picks up the information at once, and another needs it repeated several times.

The reality is that the intellect is like a photographic camera (al-fotoghrafiya), which captures information in a single instance, on condition that it is empty and prepared to receive it, not occupied with other things, because the focus of consciousness cannot hold or contain more than one idea. This matter we addressed in His saying: ﴿Allah has not made for any man two hearts within his chest...﴾ (33:4).

The intelligent person is the one who does not occupy his mind with two matters at one time, and does not think of one thing while he is engaged with another. When the focus of consciousness is empty, people are all equal in capturing information.

Therefore, the successful teacher is the one who can draw the students' attention and does not give them the opportunity to occupy themselves with other than the lesson. This is achieved only by being gentle with them and involving them in the lesson with questions from time to time, so that the student remains expecting to be asked and does not become preoccupied. For this reason we have seen that the dialogue method is the most successful method of teaching; as for the method of merely reciting information, it makes the teacher in one valley and the students in another valley, each of them thinking about something that occupies him.

We have said before that when a student knows the importance of a lesson, he reviews it on his way to the examination, and while climbing the stairs, if this lesson comes to him he answers it word for word. Why? Because he remembered it at the critical time, when the opportunity is narrow and does not tolerate preoccupation or negligence, so the intellect captures every word and records it; if he wishes to recall it, it comes just as it was. Why? Because it met an intellect that was empty and not occupied.

Consider the greatness of the Creator, glory be to Him, in the matter of recollection: the memory is a small part of the brain. How then can a small child, not exceeding eight years old, memorize the entire Qur'an and recite it back to you at any time, while we marvel at the recording tape that preserves for us one or two circles of study?

The Qur'an is not mere memorization; it is companionship. The letters of the Qur'an are angels, every letter of it has an angel, and the angel loves the one who loves him. If you keep in contact with the Qur'an and recite it frequently, it is as if you love the angels; when you want to recall what you have memorized, the angels gather for you and the Qur'an flows on your tongue. But if you abandon it, it abandons you, and it slips away from your memory. For this reason the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) warned us against abandoning the Qur'an, saying: "Keep up your recitation of the Qur'an, for by Him in whose hand is my soul, it escapes more swiftly than camels from their tethers." (2)

We have said before that remembrance is the only act of worship that costs you nothing, does not disable any of your limbs, does not require time or effort from you, and has no specific time. Whoever remembers Allah standing, sitting, or lying on his side is counted among those who remember, and this is in relation to your posture. Whoever remembers Allah in the morning and evening, or at dawn and dusk, is counted among those who remember; this is in relation to time.

Whoever says "Glory be to Allah, praise be to Allah, there is no god but Allah, Allah is greatest, and there is no power nor strength except with Allah, the Most High, the Mighty" thirty times a day is recorded among those who remember. Whoever wakes at night and wakes his family and prays two rak'ahs is among those who remember.

So the remembrance of Allah is an easy matter: you can remember Allah while you are working with the axe or writing with the pen, you can remember Allah while you are eating or drinking, etc. Thus the remembrance of Allah, though it is greatest, is easy and light for the believer.

(1) Tafassi (تفصي) from a thing means to be freed from it, to escape. The Prophet's (ﷺ) saying about the Qur'an, "it is more prone to escape than the hearts of men from their camels in their tethers," means: more prone to slipping away and getting out. [Lisan al-'Arab, root f-s-y]
(2) Recorded by Ahmad in his Musnad (1/423) from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud, and by Muslim in his Sahih (791), Book of the Prayer of Travellers, from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 33, verse 42:

And His saying, may He be exalted:

﴿And glorify Him morning and evening.﴾ [al-Ahzab]

Tasbih (glorification, declaring God free of imperfection) is taqdis (sanctification), and taqdis is tanzih (transcendence). So what do we declare God transcendent of? They said: We declare God transcendent in His essence, in His acts, and in His attributes. God has existence, you have existence, the river and the mountain have existence, but His existence, may He be exalted, is not like the existence of anything other than Him. His existence, may He be exalted, is existence not preceded by non-existence, whereas the existence of everything else is existence after non-existence. This is regarding the essence.

As for the acts, God has an act just as you have an act, but declare your Lord transcendent so that His act is not like your act. We have said this in the event of the Isra' and Mi'raj, and in the difference between sara (he travelled) and asra bihi (he was made to travel by Him). If the act belongs to God, then do not look to time, because it is not your act but God's act, and God's act requires no treatment; He says to a thing "Be," and it is.

We have also said that even in human capacities we find that an act takes time in proportion to the strength of the doer. A small child carries what an adult carries in a minute in an hour. So if you measure God's act by His power, you find the act without time.

Likewise we declare God transcendent in His attributes: God has a hearing that is transcendent of being like your hearing, and He has a face that is transcendent of being like your face, and so on, all within the framework of ﴿There is nothing like Him﴾ [al-Shura].

When you survey the verses of tasbih in the Qur'an you find them numerous, but tasbih has a special character when it comes at the openings of surahs. At the beginning of al-Isra': ﴿Glory be to the One who took His servant by night﴾ [al-Isra'].

So the surah began with the glorification of God because of the wondrous and strange events it contains; therefore He said at the outset ﴿Glory be to the One who took His servant by night﴾ [al-Isra']. For God's being glorified and sanctified is established before He acts, and "Glory be to God" existed before the glorifier existed, just as He is a Creator before anything created exists. He is a Creator in His very nature first, before creation. As we said about the poet: you say "So-and-so is a poet." Is that because you heard a poem from him, or is he a poet before he composes it? He is a poet before he composes it, and were he not a poet he would not have composed.

Whoever follows the wording of tasbih in the Qur'an finds that it is established for God before He created the glorifiers, in His saying ﴿Glory be to the One who took His servant by night﴾ [al-Isra'], and then after God created creation: ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies God﴾ [al-Hashr].

Creation continues to glorify in the present: ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies God﴾ [al-Jumu'ah]. So the glorification of God was and continues until the Hour arrives. Therefore the Truthful, glorified is He, commands His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his community with him, not to depart from this system that glorifies, and He says to him:

﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾ [al-A'la].

The command to mention God comes after the command to glorify Him, as if He were saying to you: whenever you mention Him, declare Him transcendent in His essence, attributes and acts. It is in your interest in the journey of life that God has no likeness, no equal, no peer, and no rival, because all will be under His justice, glorified is He. So God's transcendence is for your benefit, O you who glorify.

We have previously mentioned in this regard the saying of the villagers (the one who has no big one, let him buy himself a big one). The existence of a great one above everyone protects you from anyone being arrogant towards you. So His greatness and His majesty are among the greatest blessings upon us. When you glorify Him and declare Him transcendent, praise God, for He is transcendent; praise God that He has no partner, and that people are all equal before Him; praise God because His word and command take effect over everyone; praise God that He has not taken a consort or a son, and that there is no kinship between Him and any of His creatures.

And how could we not mention God, glorify Him and praise Him, when He is the One who created creation, and before He created them He ordained their ends for them? Creation is bringing into being according to a measure for an end. Indeed, He prepared for them what serves them. Man came to a universe prepared to receive him; before He created him, He created for him.

Then He did not charge you directly with His method; rather He left you to flourish in His blessings from your birth until the age of puberty without obligation. The meaning of puberty is that you reach the age of discernment, so that you turn to God with intellect and thought. Religion is not imitation; it is conviction and persuasion.

We have previously likened the maturing of a human to the ripening of a fruit. A fruit is not sweet except when its seed ripens, and becomes fit to germinate if planted. This is from the greatness of the Creator, glorified is He. Were the fruit to become sweet and ready before its seed ripens, we would eat the fruits once and never benefit from them after us. We gave the example of the watermelon seed: if you find it black and firm, know that its fruit has become ripe, sweet, and fit to eat. The Creator, glorified is He, made this matter for the preservation of the species.

Another matter: after you have reached the age of obligation, did obligation come to you encompassing every movement of your life? Did it come as a fetter upon you? When you reflect on the matters of obligation you find them within a limited scope, in which God commanded you "do this and do not do that." This zone does not occupy more than five percent of the movement of your life, and He left you the remaining ninety-five percent, in which you are free: you may act or not act. What greatness this is! And what mercy our Lord, mighty and majestic, treats us with! If this indicates anything, it indicates the love of the Creator, glorified is He, for His creatures and His handiwork. Does this not require of us that we not neglect His remembrance, and that we increase in glorifying and thanking Him, morning and evening?

Greater than all of this, He, glorified and exalted is He, made your remembrance of Him and your glorification of Him for your own benefit, and in your scale of deeds. Therefore He said in the verse that follows:

﴿It is He who sends blessings upon you, and His angels, that He may bring you out of darkness into light. And He is ever Merciful to the believers.﴾ [al-Ahzab 43]

The meaning of ﴿He who sends blessings upon you..﴾ [al-Ahzab] (43). Salah (ṣalāh, here meaning blessing or invocation) is du'a, and du'a is only the seeking of good for the one who makes it. One only makes du'a to someone able to grant that good. How, then, are we to understand this? Does our Lord, may He be blessed and exalted, make du'a for Himself? They said: if the purpose of salah is the seeking of good, and that good is obtained when it is sought, then the Truth, glory be to Him, is the one who makes the du'a, and He is the one who possesses the keys to all good. So He is the one who sends blessings upon you, He is the one who gives to you, and He is the one who has mercy on you.

Also, the angels send blessings upon you. ﴿And His angels..﴾ [al-Ahzab] (43). He, glory be to Him, has told us about them that they are ﴿honoured servants, who do not precede Him in speech and act by His command﴾ [al-Anbiya] (26-27), and He said: ﴿They do not disobey Allah in what He commands them, and they do what they are commanded﴾ [al-Tahrim] (6).

The angels are of several kinds. Some are charged with serving us and with our benefits on earth. Some protect us from the calamities that may suddenly strike us, by the power Allah has given them over these. Some are the recording angels, the honourable scribes. These angels attached to us are the ones who were commanded to prostrate to Adam, peace be upon him, in His saying: ﴿So when I have proportioned him and breathed into him of My spirit, fall down in prostration to him﴾ [al-Hijr] (29).

This is evidence that they will be in his service.

It is as if Allah, the Exalted, said to Iblis: I commanded you to prostrate to Adam, and I commanded the angels, and you were with them. If you are one of the angels, then you ought to comply. And if you are not one of the angels, but I gathered you into their company because of your obedience, then it was obligatory upon you to obey, because the one above you prostrated.

We have clarified this matter with an example, and to Allah belongs the highest example. We said:

If it is announced in one of the government offices that the President will visit this office on such a day, and the ministers must line up to greet him, does this command not include the deputy ministers all the more?

So when Allah said to the angels: Prostrate to Adam, and Iblis was with them although he was lower than them, it was incumbent upon him to prostrate. Then, O Iblis, if you had attained a rank higher than the angels through obedience, your obedience to Allah must be at this rank. You are blameworthy in any case. However, he was of the jinn, and the jinn have free will, so he transgressed the command of his Lord.

There is another kind of angel that has no connection with the human being or his worldly affairs. These are the exalted or dominant angels (al-'Aliyun or al-Muhaymin), and they are the ones about whom Allah spoke when Iblis refused to prostrate. His Lord said to him: ﴿Have you become arrogant, or have you been among the exalted?﴾ [Sad] (75).

These exalted angels were not included in the command to prostrate, because they know nothing of Adam and have no relation to him. Foremost among them are the bearers of the Throne, and they are the most honoured of the angels. These are the ones who send blessings upon you after Allah has sent blessings upon you. Therefore, the Truth, glory be to Him, shows us these angels, their role in blessing us and seeking forgiveness for us. So He, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Those who bear the Throne and those around it glorify their Lord with His praise and believe in Him, and they ask forgiveness for those who believe..﴾ [Ghafir] (7).

These are the most distinguished and most honoured of the angels. They glorify their Lord with His praise and believe in Him. But what is the benefit of ("and believe in Him") after they have glorified Him? They said: because glorification may come from fear and dread, whereas the glorification of these angels comes from love and from faith, and from the knowledge that He, glory be to Him and exalted, deserves to be glorified. Among the duties of these angels is also that they seek forgiveness for those who believe. Although they have no connection with people and are not in their service, they still send blessings upon them and ask forgiveness for them.

So we say: the salah from one who owns the du'a and is able to answer it is mercy, compassion and tenderness, while the salah from one below Him is du'a to the Able, the Owner of good. So they make du'a to Allah for the believers and ask Allah to forgive them. Indeed, they go to great lengths in du'a and express tenderness in it: ﴿Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge, so forgive those who repent and follow Your way, and protect them from the punishment of the Blazing Fire﴾ [Ghafir] (7).

Moreover, they do not stop at seeking deliverance for the believers from the Fire. Rather, they ask for them Paradise: ﴿Our Lord, admit them to the Gardens of Eden which You have promised them, along with those righteous among their fathers, their spouses and their offspring. Indeed, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise﴾ [Ghafir] (8).

Then they add to that: ﴿And protect them from evil deeds. And whomever You protect from evil deeds that Day, You will have had mercy upon him. And that is the great success﴾ [Ghafir] (9).

By Allah, if the believer wished to make du'a for himself, he would find no more general or comprehensive du'a than the du'a of the angels for him. After they ask forgiveness for him and deliverance from the Fire, they do not leave him in that state among the people of al-A'raf, neither in Paradise nor in the Fire. Rather, they ask Allah to grant him Paradise, in accordance with His saying: ﴿So whoever is drawn away from the Fire and admitted into Paradise has attained success﴾ [Al 'Imran] (185).

This matter is one of those which the orientalists (al-Mustashriqun) stopped at. They said: it contradicts the Prophetic hadith: "There is no day on which the sun rises but two angels call out, one of them saying: 'O Allah, give the one who spends a replacement,' and the other saying: 'O Allah, give the one who withholds destruction.'" (1). So how can you say that the angels make du'a for people's good while they make du'a against them for evil?

They are excused in their objection, because their faculties cannot grasp the meanings in the noble hadith. The contradiction, in their view, lies in the words of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: "and the other says: 'O Allah, give the one who withholds destruction.'" The first is clear and has no contradiction, because it is a supplication for good. The second, however, is a supplication for harm: "O Allah, give the one who withholds destruction."

If they had reflected on the text of this phrase, they would have found the answer in it. Does destruction (talaf) give or take? It is supposed to take. So when the Messenger of Allah says: "O Allah, give the one who withholds destruction," know that it is a giving and not a taking, even though on the surface it is destruction. The meaning is that something has preoccupied you and tempted you, so that a calamity strikes you in it which frees you from it, and you return to your Lord. Therefore, it is a taking in appearance but a giving in reality.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, explains to us the reason for the blessing of Allah and the blessing of the angels upon the believers. He says: ﴿to bring you out from darknesses into light﴾ [al-Ahzab] (43). So it is as if the way of Allah, "do and do not do," is the first of Allah's blessings upon us, because it is the means that brings us out of darknesses into light. Here He used something tangible so that we may measure the intangible by it. In light you see your path and are guided to your goal without ruin, whereas in darkness your steps stumble and you lose the way. You walk without guidance and without insight, so the weaker among you is crushed and the stronger among you crushes you.

The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, directs us, when we sleep at night, to extinguish the lamps. He says: "Extinguish the lamps when you go to sleep." (2) Science has also established that lights left on during sleep have a harmful effect on human health, and that a person does not rest in full comfort in the light, because of the radiation of light that affects him during sleep. They have also warned us against exposure to television lights, for example.

So light has a function, and darkness has a function. This is in the realm of the tangible.

Likewise, the way of Allah, "do and do not do," is the spiritual light that protects you from ruin and grants you the illuminations by which you are guided along the paths of life. Therefore He, the Exalted, said after it: ﴿And He is ever Merciful to the believers﴾ [al-Ahzab] (43).

But if He, glory be to Him, is merciful to the believers, what about the disbelievers? They said: He, glory be to Him, is Raḥmān (Most Gracious) toward the disbelievers. Allah is Raḥmān of this world and Raḥīm (Most Merciful) of the Hereafter, because Raḥmān of this world means that His goodness encompasses all, believer and disbeliever, obedient and disobedient. In the Hereafter, however, the attribute of Raḥīm is manifested, because His mercy in the Hereafter is specific to the believers alone.

As for the saying of the Truth, glory be to Him: ﴿Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth..﴾ [al-Nur] (35), it does not mean that this is an attribute of His essence, but rather that He is the Light of the heavens and the earth, meaning, the one who gives them light, just as we say: the lamp is the light of the mosque.

We have previously clarified this matter with the words of Abu Tammam in praise of al-Mu'tasim:

The advance of 'Amr in the generosity of Hatim,
In the forbearance of al-Ahnaf, in the intelligence of Iyas.

'Amr is the proverbial example among the Arabs for courage, Hatim for generosity, al-Ahnaf ibn Qays for forbearance, and Iyas ibn Mu'awiya for intelligence.

One of those present, who harboured resentment against him, stood up and said: "The Commander of the Believers is above what you say. Do you liken him to the coarse Arabs?" And he recited:

The panegyrists likened him in valour and generosity
To one who, if he saw him, would be the least of servants.
In his army are fifty thousand like 'Antar,
And in his treasury are a thousand Hatims.

At that, Abu Tammam lowered his head for a moment, then said:

Do not deny my striking for Him a parable
Rare in generosity and valour, beyond him.
For Allah struck the lesser for His light
A parable of the niche and the lamp.

So the spiritual light protects you from spiritual ruin, just as the tangible light saves you from tangible ruin. Therefore He, glory be to Him, said of His light: ﴿Light upon light﴾ [al-Nur] (35). That is: a tangible light that protects you from tangible dangers, and a spiritual light that protects you from spiritual dangers. ﴿Allah guides to His light whom He wills﴾ [al-Nur] (35). The light here means the spiritual light by which the believer is guided and walks, whereas the disbeliever knows only the tangible light.

If you ask: where do we find this light, O Lord? Your Lord answers you: ﴿In houses which Allah has permitted to be raised and in which His name is mentioned; glorifying Him therein morning and evening, are men whom neither commerce nor sale distracts from the remembrance of Allah..﴾ [al-Nur] (36-37).

If you want the true light, it is in your solitude with your Lord, and in His house, where its illuminations are manifested upon you and His light overwhelms you.

Before we leave the matter of Allah's blessing and the angels' blessing upon the believers, we mention our own salah upon the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, in accordance with His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet. O you who have believed, send blessings upon him and greet him with the greeting of peace﴾ [al-Ahzab] (56).

The salah from Allah, the Exalted, means tenderness, mercy and compassion. The salah from the angels means du'a and request addressed to the One who possesses. As for our salah upon our master, the Messenger of Allah, some think it is du'a from us for the Messenger of Allah, but it is not so. Because when you say in the salah upon the Messenger of Allah: "O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad," you are not blessing him, peace and blessings be upon him. Rather, you are asking Allah, the Exalted, to bless him. But how do you ask Allah to bless His Messenger? They said: because every good that the Messenger receives is scattered upon his ummah.

The Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, did not leave Muhammad to have blessings sent upon him by everyone who believes in him without the Messenger of Allah returning this greeting with a similar blessing. So He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And pray for them; indeed, your prayer is a comfort for them﴾ [al-Tawba] (103). It is as if this is a return of the greeting and of the believers' blessing upon the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him.

1 Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih (1010) from the hadith of Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him.
2 Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (3280) from the hadith of Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: "When the night has come on, or when the darkness of the night has fallen, restrain your children, for the devils then spread out. When an hour of the night has passed, release them, close your door and mention the name of Allah, extinguish your lamp and mention the name of Allah, tie up your waterskin and mention the name of Allah, and cover your vessel and mention the name of Allah, even if you cover it with something."

Then Allah, glorified is He, says:

﴿Their greeting on the Day they meet Him will be "Peace," and He has prepared for them a generous reward.﴾ (33:44)

The discussion here concerns the Hereafter. This greeting and this peace do not come from us; they come from Allah, as He said elsewhere: ﴿Peace, a word from a Lord, Most Merciful.﴾ (36:58)

The mercy we receive from Allah in this world, along with His tenderness and compassion toward us, means: soundness in the course of life, uprightness in conduct, ease of mind, and tranquility of the soul. Yet even so, this world is not free of troubles and events that strike you. But Allah's mercy in the Hereafter is complete peace, which nothing disturbs. A person also enjoys Allah's blessings in this world, but the fear of losing them spoils them for him.

In the Hereafter, however, he enjoys them with pure delight, undisturbed by anything. The blessing is lasting and enduring; it neither escapes him nor does he escape it. In this world he was in the realm of causes (ʿālam al-asbāb, the world of causes), but now in the Hereafter he is with the Causer, glorified is He, who says: ﴿To whom belongs dominion this Day? To Allah, the One, the Subduer.﴾ (40:16)

But: what is meant by His saying, ﴿the Day they meet Him…﴾ (33:44)? Is it the Day of Resurrection for reward, or the day they meet Him by death and the ending of life, as we say, for example, of someone who died, "So-and-so has met his Lord"? Some said: the believer is not approached by the Angel of Death except that he first greets him with peace before taking his soul. If he greets him with peace, this means he is among the people of peace, and this is the first of its ranks. It may also be that what is meant is the complete peace that the believer meets on the Day of Resurrection, where he finds a peace that no disturbances follow.

Therefore, we find that our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), while suffering the agonies of death, Fatimah said to him when she saw what he was going through: "Oh, my distress! Oh, my father!" He said to her: "There is no distress upon your father after today." (1) So what distress could there be upon the Messenger of Allah after he passes to the presence of his Lord, to the final peace after which there is no fear.

Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿and He has prepared for them a generous reward.﴾ (33:44) He described the reward itself as generous, while it is the Generous One who prepared the reward. Describing the reward as generous means that the generosity passed from the Lord, glorified is He, who prepared it, to the reward itself, until it too became generous.

An example of this is His saying: ﴿And We have prepared for her a generous provision.﴾ (33:31) Thus generosity passed from the Provider to the provision, because provision in this world has causes in the hands of creatures, but provision in the Hereafter comes to you without causes, and no one has any share in it. And why should it not be described as generous, when it comes to you without effort on your part, and merely by the thought you summon it and see it before you?

1 Ibn Majah narrated it in this wording in his Sunan (1629) from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik that the Messenger of Allah said to Fatimah when he heard her words: "There is no distress upon your father after today. Indeed there has come upon your father what will leave no one of him behind; the meeting is on the Day of Resurrection." Its origin is in al-Bukhari (4462), where he said: "There is no distress upon your father after today."

Then the Almighty says:

﴿O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness, a bringer of good news, and a warner.﴾ (33:45)

Ash-shahid (the witness): he is the one who confirms and establishes the truth for its owner. For this reason, a judge requests the testimony of witnesses so that his ruling in a case comes from verification, clear proof and evidence. Accordingly, they say that a judge does not rule on the basis of his own knowledge, but on the basis of evidence, even if he knows something from his general life, and then it comes before him in a case; he leaves it and withdraws from it to another judge who rules on it, so that he does not build his ruling on his own knowledge.

When you reflect on this matter, you find that God Most High wishes to distribute the responsibility of judgment among several bodies, so that when the ruling is issued, it is issued after scrutiny, examination and refinement to ensure the truth.

For example, if an incident occurs, we go to the police station to make a report (mahdar) about the incident. The report is referred by the police officer to the public prosecution, which refers it to the judge to rule on it, and then it is returned once more to the executive authority to be carried out. This whole cycle is intended to seek out the truth and place it in its proper position.

So what about when the Almighty is the One who bears witness, the One who judges, and the One who executes the judgment? Undoubtedly, justice here will be absolute justice. If you say: then for what does the Messenger of God bear witness?

They said: The Messenger of God bears witness that he conveyed to his community, just as all the messengers bear witness that they conveyed to their peoples, as He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness, and We bring you as a witness against these?﴾ (4:41) [an-Nisa'].

Therefore: every messenger is a witness over his community, and you are a witness over this community that you have conveyed to it. But your distinction over those before you from among your brother messengers is that you are their seal, so there is no prophet after you. For this reason, I will make from your community those who will succeed the prophets who come after the messengers in their mission.

Therefore, a noble hadith has come: the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The scholars of my community are like the prophets of the Children of Israel" (1).

Thus, the Almighty guaranteed within the community of Muhammad that there would be among them those who perform the task of the prophets in conveying the message, and this is the meaning of ﴿that you may be witnesses over mankind...﴾ (2:143) [al-Baqarah].

The word "mankind" here is general, encompassing Adam, peace be upon him, and his descendants until the Hour arises. If you ask how: we say they bear witness over mankind by the testimony of the Qur'an that the messengers conveyed to their nations. This concerns those who passed; as for those who will come, you are obligated to bear witness over them that you have conveyed to them, just as the Messenger of God bears witness over you that he has conveyed to you.

Therefore: the community of Muhammad has taken a share of prophethood, namely that it will be summoned and will bear witness over people.

For this reason, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) prepares his community for this task, saying: "May God make radiant a man who hears my saying, memorizes it, then conveys it to one who has not heard it, for many a bearer of knowledge conveys it to one who understands it better than he who heard it" (2).

Also read in this regard the saying of God Most High: ﴿And thus We have made you a middle nation...﴾ (2:143) [al-Baqarah]. Why? ﴿That you may be witnesses over mankind, and the Messenger may be a witness over you﴾ (2:143) [al-Baqarah]. This community is in the middle, such that there is neither excess nor deficiency, and it is like the scale that does not tilt one pan over the other except by what is placed in it; it is like the just balance that does not lean here or there.

And His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿and a bringer of good news...﴾ (33:45) [al-Ahzab] means to those who respond to you with the reward of God, and bisharah (good news) is informing of good before its time. ﴿and a warner...﴾ (33:45) [al-Ahzab], i.e., a warner to those who do not believe you of the punishment of God, and indhar (warning) is frightening with an evil that has not yet come in its time.

(1) Al-Shawkani said in "al-Fawa'id al-Majmu'ah" (p. 286): "Ibn Hajar and al-Zarkashi said: it has no basis." Likewise al-Suyuti said in "al-Durar al-Muntathirah" (p. 309). Al-'Ajluni said in "Kashf al-Khafa'" (1744): "Some have added: and it is not known in any reliable book... al-Taftazani, Fath al-Din al-Shahid, Abu Bakr al-Mawsili and al-Suyuti in al-Khasa'is indicated acting upon its meaning."

(2) Narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad (1/437), al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan (2657, 2658), Ibn Majah in his Sunan (232), and al-Humaydi (1/47), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 33, verse 46:

"By His leave" (bi-idhnihi): by a command from Him, not on your own initiative. A leader or reformer may come with a method or ideas of his own and spread them among his people.

So His words ﴿by His leave﴾ [al-Ahzab 33:46] show the difference between the Messenger and a human reformer. What Muhammad brought is from Allah, and he conveyed it to you only by Allah's command.

Whoever calls to a method of goodness must meet three conditions.

The first: he must not benefit from anything he calls to. This is never found in any human being. We have seen that when the capitalists legislated, they wronged the workers, and when the socialists legislated, they wronged the capitalists, and so on.

This is because people have different and numerous desires, and each wants to legislate according to his own desire and in a way that serves his interests. He wants to make others serve his desire. After a period that may be long, experience exposes them and reality discloses them, and the evils of what they legislated appear to them, so that they rebel against their own laws, revolt against themselves, and return to amending these laws.

The second condition: he must have knowledge of the events that may occur after he legislates, and no detail of the matter may escape him, so that he does not need to amend the law or make an addition to it.

Third: whoever legislates must be wise in what he legislates, placing each matter in its proper place, so that he does not favour one group at the expense of another, and so that everyone stands equal before him.

When you reflect on these three conditions, you will find that they are found only in Allah, glory be to Him. Therefore, none should legislate for mankind except the Lord of mankind. We have previously clarified this matter with an example from the tangible. People in darkness need some light to guide them to the fulfilment of their needs at night. Each of us lights his night with whatever lighting suits him: one lights a candle, another a lamp (number five), another a lamp (number ten). After we began using electricity, we saw the ordinary bulb, the fluorescent, the neon and the crystal, and so on.

So: you light your darkness according to your capacities. But when the sun of morning rises, do you keep these lights on? No, rather everyone extinguishes their lights, because the light of the sun comes according to the capacity of its Creator, glory and majesty be to Him. Therefore we say: extinguish your lamps, for the sun of Allah has risen. If this is the case with physical light, it is also, and all the more so, the case with spiritual light. When the light of legislation and the light of method come to you from Allah, extinguish whatever other legislations and methods there are.

As for His words ﴿and as a illuminating lamp﴾ [al-Ahzab 33:46], Allah, glory be to Him, likened His Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, to a lamp (siraj). This description is not to be taken in its literal sense regarding the Messenger of Allah. The meaning of "lamp" is not like a lamp that lights a room for you, for example; rather it is like the lamp of which He said: ﴿and We made a blazing lamp﴾ [al-Naba' 78:13], and what is meant there is the sun.

If you ask: why was the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, not described as a sun, since He said of it: ﴿It is He who made the sun a radiance﴾ [Yunus 10:5], and the sun is stronger than a lamp?

They said: the speech here is the speech of the Lord, and the expression is precise and inimitable. It is true that the sun illuminates the whole world, but the community of Muhammad is charged with carrying out his call after him. So the Messenger was a lamp, and from a lamp one takes light without its light diminishing, whereas one cannot take from the sun.

When the lights of guidance shone through the tongue of the Messenger Muhammad, the earlier laws no longer had any place to intervene, as the panegyrist said:

You are as the sun, and the kings are as stars;
when it rises, no star appears among them.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 33, verse 47:

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿And give good tidings to the believers that they will have from Allah a great bounty.﴾ (47)

We say in supplication: "O Allah, deal with us by bounty, not by justice." For justice is that you receive a recompense equal to your deed, or that you take your due right; whereas bounty is that you take beyond your right and in addition to it. Among this is the words of the Exalted: ﴿Say, "In the bounty of Allah and His mercy, in that let them rejoice."﴾ (58) [Yunus].

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "None of you will enter Paradise by his deeds." They said: "Not even you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Not even I, unless Allah covers me with His mercy." This is because when I reckon my deed against what my Lord has given me of blessings, before I was created, and until I reached maturity and became responsible, I find that if I spent my whole life in obedience to my Lord, I would not have fulfilled His right upon me.

Then, from another side, you find that worship and obedience benefit you yourself, and Allah, exalted is He, gains nothing from them. So if the benefit of obedience and worship returns to you, then the reward for it is a bounty from Allah.

We give an example of this, and to Allah belongs the highest comparison: your son, whom you encourage to study, and whose supplies you prepare, and whom you support throughout the year. When he succeeds at the end of the year, you give him a gift or a reward; this gift is by way of bounty.

Therefore, if you wish to reconcile between disputants, or to bring them together, say to them: "Would you like me to judge between you by justice or by bounty?" They will say to you: "There is nothing better than justice." Then you may say: "Rather, bounty is better than justice; for justice is that you take your right from your opponent, while bounty is that you leave your right to your opponent, to take it from the hand of your Lord, mighty and majestic."

This is what we have seen practised in the story of the slander (al-ifk) between our master Abu Bakr, when he pardoned Mistah (2), after the revelation of the words of the Exalted: ﴿And let not those of virtue and wealth among you swear not to give to the near of kin and the needy and the emigrants in the way of Allah; let them pardon and overlook. Do you not like that Allah should forgive you? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ (22) [al-Nur].

So whoever wishes that Allah forgive him his sins, let him forgive his brother his slip and his offence.

(1) Ibn Atiyyah said: My father, may Allah be pleased with him, said to us: "This is the verse I hope for most in the Book of Allah, the Exalted; for Allah, mighty and majestic, has commanded His Prophet to give good tidings to the believers that they have with Him a great bounty, and Allah, exalted is He, has explained that great bounty in His words: {And those who believed and did righteous deeds, in the gardens of Paradise they will have whatever they wish with their Lord. That is the great bounty} (22) [al-Shura]." [Quoted by al-Qurtubi in his tafsir, 8/5470.]

(2) He is Mistah ibn Uthathah ibn Abbad ibn al-Muttalib. His name was Awf, while Mistah was his epithet; his mother was a maternal cousin of Abu Bakr. Abu Bakr used to support him because of his kinship to him. When he joined those who spoke of the slander concerning Aisha, Abu Bakr swore that he would not spend on him, and then the verse was revealed: {And let not those of virtue and wealth among you swear not to give to the near of kin...} (22) [al-Nur], so Abu Bakr returned to supporting him. Mistah died in the year 34 AH during the caliphate of Uthman; it is also said he died in 37 AH, and that he witnessed Siffin with Ali. [al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah (7929)].

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and disregard their harm, and rely upon Allah. And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs.﴾

At the beginning of the surah, the Truth, glorified is He, addressed His Prophet ﷺ with His saying: ﴿O Prophet, fear Allah and do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites...﴾ [al-Ahzab]. Here, his Lord addressed him with His saying: ﴿And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and disregard their harm, and rely upon Allah. And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs.﴾ [al-Ahzab]. The first was at the beginning of the call, when the disbelievers had begun plotting against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. So what of it now, when the call has grown strong and its roots have firmed? The scheming of the disbelievers against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ must surely have multiplied.

Therefore He repeats to him the matter of ﴿And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and disregard their harm...﴾ [al-Ahzab]. This does not mean that He will abandon you; rather, I am your Disposer of affairs (wakil) ﴿and rely upon Allah. And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs.﴾ [al-Ahzab].

If you say: how can this be, since the wakil (agent, trustee) is less than the asil (principal)? We say: no. The principal does not appoint another except because he is unable to act himself, so he chooses the stronger to act on his behalf.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 33, verse 49:

Then the Almighty says:

﴿O you who have believed, when you marry believing women and then divorce them before you have touched them, then you have no waiting period for them to count. So provide for them and release them in a fair manner.﴾ (49)

The verse speaks of a social matter that concerns the preservation of the species, and the preservation of the human species can only be achieved through marriage, which is the means of procreation. The first stage of marriage is the stage of betrothal (khitba), and many people do not understand the meaning of betrothal or its limits for both man and woman. Betrothal is simply that the suitor goes to the girl's guardian (wali) and says to him: "If I come forward to ask for your daughter's hand, will I be found acceptable?"

Her guardian says: "Welcome to you. This is called betrothal, and perhaps he will not come forward. If he does come forward for her, he may see her once, in the presence of her mahrams, because the Prophet (ﷺ) said to a young man who wanted to propose: 'Look at her, for it is more likely to create affection between you both'" (1).

It is strange that people confuse betrothal with the marriage contract, giving betrothal the status of a contract. So when the guardian accepts the suitor, they agree on the dowry (mahr) or the engagement gifts (shabka) and every detail of the marriage, and he is permitted to sit with his daughter, to speak with her, and perhaps to be alone with her. Would that they had made it a contract, so they could spare themselves this embarrassment.

If the suitor backs out of the betrothal, all they need do is go to the girl's guardian and say to him: "I asked for your daughter's hand, but I am free of this matter." As for the contract, it is not dissolved before consummation except by divorce. So do not make the form of betrothal and the substance of a contract the same thing.

And the Almighty, exalted is He, explains to us in this noble verse the rulings regarding divorce if it occurs before consummation with the wife: ﴿O you who have believed, when you marry believing women and then divorce them before you have touched them, then you have no waiting period for them to count..﴾ [al-Ahzab] (49).

Here "nikah" is intended to mean only the contract, for otherwise, if the other meaning were intended, He would not have said ﴿before you have touched them..﴾ [al-Ahzab] (49). "Touch" (massa) is a euphemism for intercourse, and it is an act that the Qur'an always veils with words that do not signify it directly.

The ruling here is ﴿then you have no waiting period for them to count..﴾ [al-Ahzab] (49). So the husband has no waiting period over his wife if he divorces her (2) before he has consummated the marriage with her, because the waiting period was prescribed for a wisdom. In the case of a revocable divorce, the waiting period gives the husband the opportunity to take back his wife and restore her to his marriage by himself. The waiting period is for ascertaining the womb and confirming that it is free of pregnancy. Or the waiting period may be for neither of these, but because he has died and she is left behind (3).

So the waiting period before consummation has one ruling, and after consummation it has another ruling. This difference is also clear in the matter of the dowry: before consummation the wife receives half her dowry, as He, glorified is He, said: ﴿then half of what you have specified..﴾ [al-Baqarah] (237). And here He said: ﴿So provide for them and release them in a fair manner (49).﴾ If the dowry was specified between the two parties, she receives half of it; if it was not specified, she receives half the customary dowry (mahr al-mithl).

As for the waiting period after consummation, it has details, varying from one case to another according to what suits the situation in which the waiting period begins. And the waiting period, as we have said, indicates that it is something counted. If the woman is one who menstruates, it is three menstrual cycles, so that the cleansing of the womb may be confirmed during them. But the womb is cleansed by a single instance, so why did God make it three menstrual cycles?

They said: the purpose of that is to give the husband an opportunity; he may reconsider himself and calm down, and take back his wife during this period. So the Shari'a here takes into account the building of the family. Do you not see that the Almighty prescribed the joining of husband and wife with the words: "I have married you to her and her to you"? As for the case of divorce and separation between the spouses, He made it in three stages, because God, exalted is He, wants not to allow a passing anger a path to breaking the word of God in marriage.

I recall that they used to pose to us a question as if it were a riddle: Does a man observe a waiting period? Or: Does a woman have no waiting period with respect to a man? They said: Yes, a man observes a waiting period in one case: if he marries a woman and then divorces her and wishes to marry her sister, he must complete the waiting period so that marriage to her sister becomes lawful for him.

As for a woman who has ceased menstruating, her waiting period is three months; the waiting period of a pregnant woman is until she gives birth to her child. As for the waiting period of a widow, it is four months and ten days. But what is the ruling if a woman is subject to both the death of her husband and something else; how does she observe her waiting period? They said: in this case she observes the longer of the two terms: pregnancy, or the four months and ten days.

And you may ask: Why was the waiting period of a divorced woman three months, while the waiting period of a widow is four months and ten days? They said: because there is a difference between divorce and death with regard to the husband's relationship with his wife. Its cause is that the One who created male and female placed a word that unites them, and this word is: "I have married you" and "I have married her to you", on condition that it be public, before witnesses. Do not take this word lightly, for you do not know what this word does in the particles of human formation, but you know it by its effects.

And we have said: suppose you were approached by a young man who keeps pestering your daughter, for example. What would you do? Without doubt you would be enraged, your blood would boil, jealousy would seize you, and perhaps you would harm him. But if he came through the door and asked you for her hand, you would welcome him, be happy, and everyone would rejoice. So what has changed? And what is the difference between the two situations? The one that provoked you was that he spied on her without the permission of her Creator. Therefore the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Fear God regarding women, for you have taken them under the trust of God, and you have made their private parts lawful by the word of God" (4).

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to a man who was known for being jealous over his daughters, and who had come to invite the Messenger of God (ﷺ) to marry one of his daughters, so the Messenger of God laughed and said: "Lawfulness has cut off the nose of jealousy."

So the contract that unites the spouses in the word of God makes between the spouses a lawful flow (sayyal) belonging to each of them, and these two flows meet in what is lawful and under the canopy of the Shari'a that joined them.

Divorce is usually accompanied by hatred from one or both parties, or the aversion of one toward the other. Therefore the waiting period between them is three months or until the child is delivered, because the aversion that has arisen between them kills the cells of union between the tissues, and hastens the ending of the flow between them and obliterates it.

As for the death of the husband, the marriage has been severed by divine decree from God. Usually the wife loves her husband and grieves at his loss, and the calamity of death comes and increases her love for him. In this case it is not easy for the flow between them to end; therefore the Creator, glorified is He, wills to prolong the waiting period until this flow that joined them ends, so that no new flow enters upon the man's flow and a conflict arises between the two flows. This is why the waiting period of a widow is longer than that of a divorced woman.

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿then you divorced them before you had touched them..﴾ [al-Ahzab] (49) means: divorce before touching and consummation existed just as it exists now, and we see both parties, or one of them, rushing into the contract even though he is not prepared for the expenses of marriage, but rushes into it for a benefit that will return to him from this bond.

History has recorded that many families, especially noble Arab families, used to do this, but they would not allow the husband in this case to be alone with the wife, even though he had contracted her, and some of our young women have honorable stories in this matter.

Among what has been related on this subject is the story of Bahitha bint Aws ibn Haritha al-Ta'i and al-Harith ibn Awf, who was a chief of the chiefs of the Banu Murra. Al-Harith ibn Awf had a friend named Ibn Sinan, and one night al-Harith sat conversing with his friend Ibn Sinan, and he said to him: "Do you think, if I proposed to one of the Arabs for his daughter, he would reject me?" He said it while proud of himself and boastful of his lordship over his people.

When his companion saw him in this state, he said to him: "Yes, there is someone who would reject you." He said: "Who?" He said: "Aws ibn Haritha al-Ta'i." Al-Harith called to his servant and said: "Bring the mounts, and let us go to Aws ibn Haritha al-Ta'i." They went to him, and found him sitting in the courtyard of his house. When Aws saw him, he said: "Welcome to you, O Harith." Al-Harith approached him and said: "Woe to you, O Aws, what has brought you?" and left him on his mount. He said: "I have come to you as a suitor for your daughter." He said to him: "You are not there," meaning you are not worthy of her. Al-Harith turned the reins of his mount and departed, while Ibn Sinan showed relief, because his words had proved true about his companion.

When Aws entered upon his wife, she asked him: "Which man stood with you without staying long or dismounting?" He said: "It was al-Harith ibn Awf, a chief of the chiefs of the Banu Murra." She said: "And why did you not host him?" He said: "He has acted foolishly," meaning: he has committed a folly. She said: "How so?" He said: "He came proposing for my daughter." She said: "How strange! Or do you not wish to marry off your daughters?" He said: "Yes." She said: "If you will not marry them to the chiefs of the Arabs, to whom will you marry them? O Aws, go and make up for the matter." He said: "How, when what has happened has happened?" She said: "Go after him, and say to him: 'You came to me while I was angry about a matter that has nothing to do with you, and when I reflected on myself I came to you apologizing, asking you to return, and you will have from me what you love.'"

The man went, but did not find the caravan. He urged on his mount until he came up with them in the caravan. Ibn Sinan turned and said: "O Ibn Awf, here is Aws catching up with us." He said: "What shall I do with him? Go on." Aws called out: "O Harith, wait (irba') for me a while," meaning: wait for me, and you will have from me what you love. Al-Harith rejoiced and returned with him.

Aws returned to his house and said to his wife: "Call your eldest daughter." She came, and he said: "O daughter, al-Harith ibn Awf, chief of the Banu Murra, has come to propose to you." She said: "Do not do it, father." He said: "Why?" She said: "I am a woman with an aversion in my face," meaning ugliness that repels whoever sees me, "and in my character there is a fault," meaning a defect, "and he is not a cousin of mine who would respect my kinship, nor a neighbour of yours in your country who would feel shame before you, and I fear he may dislike something in me and divorce me, and then there will be upon me what you know." He said to her: "Go, may God bless you."

Then he said to his wife: "Call your middle daughter," and she came, and he said to her what he had said to her sister. She said: "Do not do it, father." He said: "Why?" She said: "I am a clumsy woman," meaning: I do not do work well, and I have no craft, "and I fear he may see in me what he dislikes and divorce me, and there will be in me what there will be." He said to her: "Go, may God bless you. Call your youngest sister." She was Bahitha, the one whose example is struck in this situation.

When her father put the matter to her, she said: "Do what you see fit, father." He said: "My daughter, I have presented it to your two sisters, and they refused." She said: "But I am beautiful of face, skilled of hand, and noble of character. If he divorces me, may God not compensate him with anything." He said: "May God bless you." Then he rose to al-Harith and said: "Be blessed, O Harith, for I have married my daughter Bahitha to you. May God bless you both." He said: "I have accepted her marriage."

Then he said to his wife: "Prepare your daughter, and make for her a tent in the courtyard of the house." When the tent was made, Bahitha was brought to it, and al-Harith entered upon her, but he did not remain long before he came out. Ibn Sinan asked him: "Have you finished your affair?" He said: "No, by God, O Ibn Sinan." He said: "Why?" He said: "I came to approach her." She said: "In the presence of my father and brothers? By God, that will never happen," and she came out.

He said: "Since she is not content while she is with her father and brothers, come, let us depart." He ordered the departure, and the caravan travelled with them for a long time. Then he said: "O Ibn Sinan, go ahead," meaning: give us the opportunity. Ibn Sinan went ahead with the caravan, and al-Harith withdrew with his wife to one side of the road and pitched his tent. Then he entered upon her, and she said to him: "What God wills! Will you treat me as one treats a captive taken as booty, or a bondwoman dragged away? By God, no..."

(1) On the authority of al-Mughira ibn Shu'ba, who said: I proposed to a woman, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to me: "Did you look at her?" I said: "No." He said: "Then look at her, for it is more likely to create affection between you both." Related by Ahmad in his Musnad (4/245, 246), al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan (1087), and Ibn Majah in his Sunan (1865). Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id: "Its chain is sound and its narrators are trustworthy."

(2) This refers to divorcing her before consummation. But if the husband dies before he has consummated the marriage, she must observe a waiting period, and the waiting period of a widow is the same as if he had consummated it, based on the saying of God, the Exalted: ﴿Those of you who die and leave wives behind, they shall wait by themselves for four months and ten days (234)﴾ [al-Baqarah], and the waiting period was made obligatory upon her even if he had not consummated with her out of fidelity to the deceased husband and consideration of his right." [Fiqh al-Sunna 2/342]. Ibn Qudama said in al-Mughni (9/78): "Every woman whose husband has died, and who is not pregnant, whether before or after consummation, free or slave, her waiting period is in months."

(3) The waiting period (iddah): derived from "adad" (counting and enumeration), meaning what a woman counts and reckons of days and menstrual cycles. It is the name of the period in which a woman waits and refrains from remarriage after her husband's death or his separation from her. [Fiqh al-Sunna, Shaykh Sayyid Sabiq 2/241].

(4) Related by Muslim in his Sahih (1218), Book of Hajj, and Ibn Majah in his Sunan (3074), and Abu Dawud in his Sunan (1905), from the hadith of Jabir ibn Abd Allah, in a long hadith about the Hajj of the Prophet (ﷺ), which was the Farewell Pilgrimage.

(5) Irba' 'ala nafsika: be restrained and gentle. Its meaning is also: wait. So it carries the sense of pausing and waiting. [Lisan al-Arab, root: r-b-'].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 33, verse 50:

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful to you your wives whose bridal payments you have given, and those whom your right hand possesses from what Allah has given you as spoils of war, and the daughters of your paternal uncles and the daughters of your paternal aunts, and the daughters of your maternal uncles and the daughters of your maternal aunts who emigrated with you, and a believing woman if she gives herself to the Prophet and the Prophet wishes to marry her, exclusively for you, apart from the believers. We have certainly known what We have enjoined upon them concerning their wives and those whom their right hands possess, so that there will be no difficulty for you. And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ (50)

The Truth, blessed and exalted is He, never addressed His Prophet Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, by his proper name, as He addressed other prophets, saying: "O Noah," "O Jesus," "O Moses," "O Abraham," and so on. As for the Messenger of Allah, his Lord addressed him saying ﴿O Prophet…﴾ (50) [al-Ahzab] and {O Messenger…} (41); [al-Ma'idah].

Calling a person by his proper name is evidence that he has no distinguishing attribute. If he possesses a distinguishing attribute, he is called by it, as you say: "O brave one," "O poet," and so on. Now, everyone shares the proper name, so calling the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, with "O Prophet" and "O Messenger" is an honouring of him, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

As for His saying ﴿Indeed We have made lawful to you your wives…﴾ (50) [al-Ahzab], what is the meaning of ﴿made lawful﴾ (50) [al-Ahzab] here, since the discussion concerns his wives, may Allah bless him and grant him peace? They said: its meaning is that they were in a forbidden status and then Allah made them lawful for him, i.e., made them permissible. This meaning is made clear by His saying after it ﴿whose bridal payments you have given﴾ (50) [al-Ahzab], as if the Messenger of Allah had first taken the permissible course, as is evident from his having given the reward, that is, the dower.

The scholars paused at the naming of the dower as "ajr" (reward). They said: how is the dower called a reward, when the meaning of ajr in the language is: a payment placed upon a time-limited benefit which the hired person renders to the employer, whereas marriage is not time-limited, rather among its conditions is the intention of permanence and continuity?

In answer to this question we say: verses must not be taken separately from one another; rather, the verses that come in the same subject should be gathered side by side, so that their understanding comes out complete and whole.

The Truth, glorified is He, says in another place, addressing His Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, regarding his wives: ﴿You may postpone whom you will of them﴾ (51) [al-Ahzab], i.e., you delay your enjoyment of her, ﴿and you may take to you whom you will﴾ (51) [al-Ahzab], i.e., you bring her to you.

So: since you have the right to postpone some of the wives and withhold them from the turn-taking, and then take others, the benefit here is time-limited, so it fits that the dower be called a reward.

The Truth, glorified is He, grants His Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in every stage of his biography the purest, most virtuous and noblest positions. His saying ﴿whose bridal payments you have given﴾ (50) [al-Ahzab] is evidence that he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, did not benefit from them except after he had paid their dower, whereas a person may name the dower, enter upon his wife without paying any of the dower, and the whole dower or part of it may be deferred. But deferring the dower gives the woman the right to refuse to lie with him; if she allows him, that is a favour from her. So the Messenger of Allah chose the most perfect thing.

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came to explain to people what was sent down to them, and his Lord made him a behavioural exemplar in matters which are hard for people to receive, so the Messenger of Allah implemented them in himself first, as we said in the matter of adoption.

Likewise in the matter of plurality of wives: the Messenger was sent while plurality existed among the Arabs and existed even among the earlier prophets, but Allah willed to limit this plurality with a limitation that restrains the excess of women, and not make it permissible in every number. So He commanded His Messenger to say to his community: whoever has more than four, let him keep four of them and part with whatever exceeds them, whereas the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had nine wives.

Had the ruling included him, so that he kept four and released five, great harm would have befallen them, and they would have been left suspended, because they are the wives of the Messenger of Allah and the Mothers of the Believers, and no one may marry any of them after the Messenger of Allah.

So: the ruling differs for the Messenger of Allah, and his number is restricted, with respect to him, to these nine in their persons, such that if one of them dies or is divorced, he is not permitted to marry another, because Allah addressed him saying: ﴿Women are not lawful to you after this, nor that you exchange them for other wives, even though their beauty should please you﴾ (52) [al-Ahzab].

We have explained to the orientalists who delved into this matter that the Messenger was not exempted in the number, but was exempted in the counted: he was restricted to these nine in their persons, and it is not permitted for him to marry another. As for others of his community, they may marry twice or many times this number, on condition that they do not exceed four at one time.

The word ﴿We have made lawful to you your wives﴾ (50) [al-Ahzab] came before ﴿Women are not lawful to you after this﴾ (52) [al-Ahzab]. It has been reported from Sayyida 'Aishah that she said: The Messenger of Allah did not die until he was permitted to marry whatever he wished. How is that?

They said: because Allah, the Exalted, willed to give His Messenger the distinction of fidelity to his wives. Although Allah permitted him to marry others, he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, did not do so, out of fidelity to them. The Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, did this because when he was greeted with a greeting, he would return it with one better than it or return it with its like. He, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had seen from his wives a prior good when he gave them the choice and they chose him and preferred living with him over the adornment and enjoyments of this world; so it is as if he returned this greeting to them with something better.

The coming of ﴿We have made lawful to you your wives﴾ (50) [al-Ahzab] before ﴿Women are not lawful to you after this﴾ (52) [al-Ahzab] is evidence of the honouring of the Messenger and of his being treated with a special treatment: Allah made lawful to him before forbidding to him. An example of this honouring is His saying: ﴿Allah has pardoned you. Why did you give them permission?﴾ (43) [al-Tawbah]. Thus the pardon preceded the reproach.

We note in His saying ﴿Indeed We have made lawful to you your wives﴾ (50) [al-Ahzab] that "azwaj" (wives) came in the masculine form and He did not say "zawjatuka" (your wives), because "zawj" applies to the man and to the woman. Linguistically, "zawj" means the single one who has with him another of his kind, and "zawj" does not mean "two," as some believe. Similarly the word "tawam" (twin): it means one who has another with him, so each of them is called a twin. From this is His saying: ﴿eight pairs of the sheep, two and two of the goats﴾ (143) [al-An'am].

Then He says: ﴿and those whom your right hand possesses from what Allah has given you as spoils﴾ (50) [al-Ahzab]. We know that "what the right hand possesses" refers to the enslaved woman. The saying ﴿from what Allah has given you as spoils﴾ (50) [al-Ahzab] came as a precaution, for the possession by the right hand with respect to the Messenger of Allah came by a lawful way, from the spoils, meaning the captives of war.

The Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, personally undertook the taking of captives, because among the slave-women there were free women who were seized by force or were stolen, and some were sold in the slave market as slave-women, and this we indeed saw in the story of our master Zayd ibn Harithah. So the saying ﴿from what Allah has given you as spoils﴾ (50) [al-Ahzab] means: that you possessed her, and you were fully certain that she was a slave and a spoil which Allah made lawful to you.

﴿and the daughters of your paternal uncles, and the daughters of your paternal aunts, and the daughters of your maternal uncles, and the daughters of your maternal aunts﴾ (50) [al-Ahzab].

Likewise Allah made lawful to His Prophet that he marry from the daughters of his paternal uncles, or the daughters of his paternal aunts, or the daughters of his maternal uncles, or the daughters of his maternal aunts. "Al-'Umumah" (paternal kinship): his relatives on his father's side, and "al-Khu'ulah" (maternal kinship): his relatives on his mother's side. We note that the Messenger of Allah did not marry from the daughters of his paternal uncles, nor from the daughters of his paternal aunts, nor from the daughters of his maternal uncles, nor from the daughters of his maternal aunts.

The meaning is that Allah, the Exalted, made lawful to him to marry from these whenever he found them, because his kin would be trustworthy to him and helpers to him in his affair.

When you reflect on this verse, you find that "uncle" (al-'amm) and "maternal uncle" (al-khal) came in the singular, whereas "paternal aunts" and "maternal aunts" came in the plural. Why? They said: because "uncle" and "maternal uncle" are nouns of genus, and a noun of genus applies to the singular and the plural. Evidence of this is that in the Qur'an a noun of genus is excepted with the plural, as in ﴿By time, indeed mankind is in loss, except those who have believed and done righteous deeds and advised each other to truth and advised each other to patience﴾ (1-3) [al-'Asr].

"Mankind" (al-insan) is a singular noun of genus, and excepted from it are "those who believed," which is plural. As for "paternal aunts" and "maternal aunts," they are not nouns of genus, so they came in the feminine plural form.

Also, because the paternal uncle is the twin of the father (sinw al-ab), on the supposition that they are many uncles, they hold the status of the father. Read in this regard His saying: ﴿Or were you witnesses when death approached Ya'qub, when he said to his sons, "What will you worship after me?" They said, "We will worship your God and the God of your fathers, Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac"﴾ (133) [al-Baqarah]. So the paternal uncle (Ishmael) entered into the general term "fathers."

Likewise He called the paternal uncle a father in His saying: ﴿And when Abraham said to his father, Azar﴾ (74) [al-An'am], and it is known that he was his uncle.

In another place "'amm" (uncle) came in the plural form, namely His saying: ﴿There is no blame upon the blind, nor upon the lame, nor upon the sick, nor upon yourselves that you eat from your houses, or the houses of your fathers, or the houses of your mothers, or the houses of your brothers, or the houses of your sisters, or the houses of your paternal uncles, or the houses of your paternal aunts, or the houses of your maternal uncles, or the houses of your maternal aunts﴾ (61) [al-Nur].

Here "uncles" and "maternal uncles" came in the plural form. Why? They said: because the discussion here concerns the houses from which you are permitted to eat, and "houses" came in the plural form, and an uncle has one house; so since it says "houses," it must be that "your paternal uncles" and "your maternal uncles" come in the plural form.

Then He says: ﴿and a believing woman if she gives herself to the Prophet﴾ (50) [al-Ahzab]. "Hiba" (gift): the transfer of ownership without consideration. We say: so-and-so gave you such-and-such, meaning he gave it to you without consideration; it is not a sale, nor an exchange, for example.

Therefore, when this verse was revealed, Sayyida 'Aishah said: I am amazed at a woman who debases herself and gives herself to a man like this, for free, without consideration. Then the text was revealed: ﴿and a believing woman if she gives herself to the Prophet﴾ (50) [al-Ahzab]. Thereupon Sayyida 'Aishah said to our master the Messenger of Allah: O Messenger of Allah, I see that Allah hastens to your desire. He, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to her: "And you, O 'Aishah, if you were to fear Allah, He would hasten to your desire."

The meaning: Allah hastens to my desire, because I hastened to His desire; He asked of me and I fulfilled, so He grants me what I want before I ask Him.

He said ﴿and a believing woman﴾ (50) [al-Ahzab] because this gift here is specific to the believing woman; if she were a Christian, it would not be valid for her to give herself to—

Notes:
1. Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir (3/499): "This verse is a middle course between excess and deficiency. The Christians do not marry a woman unless there are seven forefathers or more between the man and her, while among the Jews one marries his brother's daughter and his sister's daughter. This complete, pure law came to demolish the excess of the Christians by permitting the daughter of the paternal uncle and paternal aunt, and the daughter of the maternal uncle and maternal aunt, and to forbid what the Jews went too far in permitting, namely the daughter of the brother and the sister."
2. Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir (8/5475): "It is known that none of his wives were from the daughters of his paternal uncles, nor from the daughters of his paternal aunts, nor from the daughters of his maternal uncles, nor from the daughters of his maternal aunts, so it is established that He made lawful to him marriage with these from the outset.
3. Related by al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan (3216), and al-Nasa'i in his Sunan (6/56), as a saying of 'Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her. Al-Tirmidhi said: this is a good (hasan) hadith.
4. The word "the Prophet" here is evidence that this matter is specific to the Messenger of Allah: none of his community may marry a woman by way of gift, by her giving herself to him, and this is among the matters specific to the Messenger of Allah, so Allah said: ﴿exclusively for you, apart from the believers﴾ (50) [al-Ahzab].
5. Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (4788, 5113), and likewise Muslim in his Sahih (1464), Kitab al-Radâ', and Ahmad in his Musnad (6/134, 158, 261), from the hadith of 'Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her.

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says:

﴿You may postpone whom you will of them, and you may take to you whom you will. And whomever you seek of those you have set aside, there is no blame upon you. That is more suitable that their eyes be comforted and they not grieve, and that they all be pleased with what you give them. And Allah knows what is in your hearts, and ever is Allah Knowing and Forbearing.﴾ (33:51)

His saying, ﴿You may postpone whom you will of them...﴾ (33:51): that is, you may delay whichever of your wives you will from her night; ﴿and you may take to you whom you will﴾ (33:51): that is, you may bring her to you and lie with whichever of them you will; ﴿and whomever you seek of those you have set aside﴾ (33:51): whomever of your wives you desire and bring near after having put her aside; ﴿there is no blame upon you﴾ (33:51): that is, there is no sin and no fault.

﴿That is more suitable that their eyes be comforted and they not grieve, and that they all be pleased with what you give them﴾ (33:51): that is, they will all be made happy, both she whom you take to you and she whom you postpone and delay, and they will be content with that, because they know that your choice in this is by the command of Allah. She whom the Messenger of Allah takes to himself rejoices in the love of the Messenger of Allah and in his meeting; and she who is delayed rejoices too, because the Messenger of Allah spared her, then returned to her again and took her to himself and brought her near. This shows that she has a role and a station. Also, when this is by the legislation of the Lord of Muhammad for Muhammad, it does not mean that he disliked her or renounced her. If you do this, O Muhammad, although it involves hardship, you do it only in obedience to a command from whom? To the command of Allah, and so you receive Allah's reward for it.

When we reflect on the word ﴿taqarra﴾ (33:51), we find that, like the general words of the Qur'an, it is like a diamond: every atomic particle in it has a special sparkle and radiance. This is why they say of it: "da bilali" (a native expression of praise). Despite the abundance of its sparkle, one ray does not obscure another ray within it; likewise the words of the Qur'an.

(qarra) occurs often in the Qur'an, as in ﴿a comfort of the eye for me and for you﴾ (28:9).

The word qarra means to settle, to be still. We say: qarra bi-l-makan, meaning he settled in the place and became still. Al-qarr is cold, and "comfort of the eye" carries both meanings: the eye becomes still at something, and does not move on to another. If it is beautiful and captivates it, it does not part from it. They say: so-and-so is "qayd al-nazar" (one whose gaze is fixed).

On the other hand, they say: so-and-so has a roving eye, meaning it does not rest on anything; or "his eye is dashi'a" (greedy) among our brothers who pronounce the jim as a dal, like "dardah," meaning Jurja; and al-'ayn al-jash'a (the greedy eye) has the same meaning. In the political sense they say: so-and-so has aspirations, meaning that whenever he reaches a position, he looks to the one above it.

As for qarr in the sense of coldness, the "comfort of the eye" means its coolness, and it is a metaphor for its joy, because the eye does not become hot except in grief and pain. This is why it has recently been established that the eyeball is a precise "thermometer" for the state of the whole body, and a gauge of its health or sickness.

Because of the importance of the eye, we say, for emphasis: "So-and-so came to me with his own eye." We have previously discussed the phenomenon of thermal regulation in the human body and said: among the marvels of the creation of man is that thermal regulation in his body takes place by a special system, such that every organ in the body retains a temperature suited to it. If the general and ideal body temperature is 37°, and it is strangely the same among the people of the North Pole and likewise among the people of the equator, then the temperature of the liver, for example, is not less than 40° Celsius; as for the eye, if its temperature rises more than ten degrees, it bursts.

So then: the comfort of the eyes of the Prophet's wives and their joy lie in his will, whereby he brings near whom he brings near, or postpones whom he postpones, because his will springs from Allah's command to him.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿and that they all be pleased with what you give them﴾ (33:51): that is, in whatever circumstances.
