Then His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿And Allah knows what is in your hearts, and ever is Allah Knowing and Forbearing﴾ (33:51), comes to indicate that the contentment here is not the contentment of outward forms; rather what is meant is the heart's contentment in carrying out Allah's commands, without there being in the souls any inner reservations or objection.

So Allah, Glorified is He, ﴿was Knowing﴾ (33:51), He knows what is in the hearts, ﴿Forbearing﴾ (33:51), He does not requite you for what He knows of your hearts; and if He were to requite you according to the measure of what He knows, that would exhaust you.

Reflect on Allah's forbearance toward us and His mercy to us in the matter of beginning with "In the name of Allah." The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, teaches us that every deed not begun with "In the name of Allah" is abtar, that is, cut off from blessing. When a person begins an action, he does not do it by his own power over it, but by the subjugation of Him who created it for him. So when you say, "In the name of Allah, I do such-and-such," you act by the name of the One who subjected this thing to you.

This is why the Truthful, the Exalted, says: ﴿And He who created all the pairs and made for you of the ships and the cattle that which you ride, that you may sit upon their backs and then remember the favor of your Lord when you are seated upon them and say, "Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us, and we were not capable of that. And indeed, to our Lord we will return"﴾ (43:12–14).

So you must begin with "In the name of Allah," even if you are disobedient to Allah. Beware of thinking that you are not worthy of this word, for your Lord is Forbearing, and Merciful, Compassionate.

1 al-jash'/ the worst greed. It is said: it is the most intense greed for food and other things. It is said: it is to take your share and covet the share of others. [Lisan al-Arab, entry: jash']

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 33, verse 52:

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says:

﴿It is not lawful for you [to take] women after this, nor to exchange them for other wives, even if their beauty impresses you, except what your right hand possesses. And Allah is ever, over all things, Watchful.﴾

We have already discussed the interpretation of this verse within the context of the preceding verses, and we summarize it here: the Truthful, glorified is He, first began with His Messenger by making lawful for him, in His saying: ﴿O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful for you your wives...﴾ [al-Ahzab] and then He restricted this permission here, saying:

﴿It is not lawful for you [to take] women after this, nor to exchange them for other wives, even if their beauty impresses you...﴾ [al-Ahzab]. So the Truthful, glorified is He, brings the lighter ruling in some matters and then the heavier one, so that the people may know that Allah, exalted is He, began His Messenger with kindness, mercy and tenderness, and to show His favour upon him, just as He said to him, ﴿Allah has pardoned you...﴾ [al-Tawbah] before He reproached him by saying: ﴿Why did you grant them permission...?﴾ [al-Tawbah].

And this verse, ﴿It is not lawful for you [to take] women after this, nor to exchange them for other wives, even if their beauty impresses you...﴾ [al-Ahzab], makes clear that what was prescribed for the Messenger of Allah regarding the plurality of wives is different from what was prescribed for his community. The Messenger of Allah was exempted by Allah, exalted is He, in the counted (al-ma'dud) and not in the number (al-'adad). The difference between an exemption in the number and an exemption in the counted is that the number applies to multiple things: if He had permitted him a number of nine and they then died, he would have been allowed to marry nine others, and if one of them died he would have been allowed to marry one in her place.

But the exemption was not for the Messenger of Allah in the number as it was for his community; rather it was in the counted, such that it is restricted to these women specifically. The wisdom in this is that a woman whom her husband divorces, among the general women of the believers, may marry another, unlike the wives of the Messenger of Allah, for they are the mothers of the believers, so it is not lawful for them to marry after the Messenger of Allah.

Then we explained that the matter of what the right hand possesses is not a stain upon the brow of Islam; rather it is one of its distinctive features. God owned the neck in order to protect it from being killed, and the comparison here is not between slavery and freedom, but between slavery and killing, as we have explained. Whoever reflects on the condition of the male or female slave under the shade of Islam cannot but acknowledge the wisdom of the Sharia in this matter.

1 Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir (3/501): "Several scholars, such as Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, al-Dahhak, Qatadah, Ibn Zayd, Ibn Jarir and others, mentioned that this verse was revealed as a recompense to the wives of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and as a pleasure with them for the goodness of their conduct in choosing Allah and His Messenger and the Last Abode when the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, gave them the choice, as has passed in the verse. So when they chose the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, their reward was that Allah, exalted is He, restricted him to them and forbade him to marry others than them or to exchange them for other wives, even if he was impressed by their beauty, except for the female slaves and concubines, for there is no blame upon him concerning them. Then He, exalted is He, lifted the burden from him in this matter and abrogated the ruling of this verse, and permitted him to marry; but he did not marry after that, so that the favour would be to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, over them."

2 Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir (8/5491): "The scholars differed concerning the permissibility for the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, of a disbelieving slave-woman, according to two opinions:
The first: she is lawful, by the generality of His saying, ﴿except what your right hand possesses﴾ [al-Ahzab]; this was said by Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Ata' and al-Hakam.
The second: she is not lawful, out of exalting his station above intimacy with a disbeliever, and Allah, exalted is He, has said, ﴿And do not hold on to the ties of disbelieving women﴾ [al-Mumtahanah]. So how then with him, peace and blessings be upon him?"

Then the Almighty says:

﴿O you who believe! Do not enter the houses of the Prophet unless permission is given to you for a meal, without waiting for its timing. But when you are invited, enter, and when you have eaten, disperse, without lingering for conversation. Indeed, that would cause annoyance to the Prophet, and he would be shy of [asking] you to leave, but Allah is not shy of the truth. And when you ask his wives for something, ask them from behind a screen. That is purer for your hearts and their hearts. And it is not for you to annoy the Messenger of Allah, nor to marry his wives after him, ever. Indeed, that would be an enormity in the sight of Allah.﴾ [53]

The Almighty has distributed the matter between the Messenger of Allah and his community. Just as He said to the Messenger at the beginning of the surah, ﴿O Prophet, fear Allah...﴾ [al-Ahzab: 1], He commanded his community to remember Him and obey Him. And just as He spoke of a matter concerning the Messenger of Allah, He likewise spoke of a matter concerning his community in His words ﴿O you who believe! When you marry believing women and then divorce them...﴾ [al-Ahzab: 49].

After that He said to the Messenger of Allah: ﴿O Prophet! Indeed We have sent you as a witness, a bearer of good news, and a warner﴾ [al-Ahzab: 45], to show the comprehensiveness of his benefit to his community. So He recompensed him on behalf of the community by their sending blessings upon him, and by their being courteous when they enter his house, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Thus He said here: ﴿O you who believe! Do not enter the houses of the Prophet unless permission is given to you...﴾ [al-Ahzab: 53], because the obligation must be directed at those who have believed in Allah. We have said that Allah the Almighty is Lord and God. The meaning of "Lord" (rabb) is that He created, nurtured, bestowed blessings and showed favour; and creating, nurturing, bestowing blessings and showing favour are not exclusive to believers, but extend to everyone whom Allah has brought into existence, whether believers or disbelievers.

The sun shines on everyone, the rain waters the land of the believer and the disbeliever, and the earth responds to all. Whoever skilfully takes the means provided by Allah from the gift of lordship obtains the result and receives his share, limited by the extent of his [pursuit of] lordly provision in this world: ﴿Whoever desires the tilth of the Hereafter, We will increase him in his tilth; and whoever desires the tilth of this world, We will give him of it, but he will have no share in the Hereafter﴾ [ash-Shura: 20]. And Allah does not waste the reward of one who does good deeds.

The believer who does not take hold of the outstretched hand of Allah through the means, and neglects them, lives backward, a dependent on others, living as a beggar seeking his sustenance even from the disbeliever. When the field is left to the disbeliever, and he takes up the means and gives them their due, he takes the gift of the Lord; and it was more fitting for the believer not to leave his Lord's gift to be taken by one who does not believe in Allah, and then himself lag behind the caravan of civilisation, even if the civilisation that the disbelievers have reached today is a civilisation only in material things.

As for values and morals, they have declined in these societies, as evidenced by the fact that when you go to these countries and stay in a hotel, as we did, you find written on the door of the room: "If thieves enter upon you, do not resist, for your life is more precious than what you have with you. If you go out onto the street, carry no money beyond your necessities." So: they have advanced in some things and declined in others.

If the manifestation of their advancement is in the economic sphere, look at the highest individual income in the world: you will find it in Sweden, and yet psychological and nervous illnesses, suicide, madness, deviance and other social diseases are widespread among them.

These countries have become civilised in a material way, because they have taken up its means: each one perfects his work and gives working time to work. Between eight and twelve you will not find a person in the street, nor will you find anyone sitting in a café, for example, or wasting working hours. During the break everyone goes to the restaurant to eat a ready-made sandwich, then returns to his work.

This is how the material society lives: whoever does not work in it dies of hunger. Praise be to Allah that our youth have become aware of the importance of work and have abandoned the childhood in which they lived until the age of thirty, dependent on their parents.

Here the Almighty teaches us courtesy towards the Messenger of Allah and makes him an example for us. He, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, lived a life of sufficiency in food, clothing and dwelling; he had only a few rooms, one room for each of his wives, and there was no sitting-room or reception room. Therefore the community must learn the manners of entering and visiting in such a situation, especially with the Messenger of Allah in his houses.

So the Almighty said: ﴿O you who believe! Do not enter the houses of the Prophet unless permission is given to you...﴾ [al-Ahzab: 53]. The word "houses" (buyut) is the plural of "bayt", which is that which is prepared for spending the night (al-baytutah), i.e., for lodging in it; and night is mostly for resting, so it is a place of stillness and lodging, whereas daytime is a place of movement. After fatigue and exertion a person must retire at night to a place where he rests and returns. For this reason the house was named "sakan" (a place of tranquillity), and likewise the wife was named "sakan" for the same reason.

The house is a dwelling for sheltering the body and its ease, and the woman is a dwelling for sheltering the heart and the repose of the soul; both should be a source of rest.

"Bayt" is pluralised as "buyut" if we mean a dwelling, and as "abyat" if we mean a line of poetry. Among the Arabs, a people of eloquence and expression, poetry was called "bayt", because meanings take shelter in it, just as we take shelter in our houses and dwell in them; likewise meanings dwell in the line of poetry, so the line itself becomes wisdom.

Therefore Ahmad Shawqi, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "Poetry remains 'aqil" — that is, it has no adornment, from their saying "the woman 'aqil", meaning one who has no adornment — unless wisdom adorns it, for without it it is nonsense of no benefit.

Wisdom remains wandering until a line of poetry shelters it, which is memorised and passed down through the ages, just as we now cite the verses of al-Mutanabbi, al-Ma'arri and Shawqi, and so on.

Lodging is according to its nature in everything: those who work by day lodge at night, and those who work by night lodge by day, although the original sense of lodging is at night. Beware of occupying a person during his time of lodging, whether it is night or day, for the time of work is for work and the time of dwelling is for dwelling.

Therefore, our wise people among the peasants say: "Whoever guards [at night] does not plough [by day]," meaning that a person who is busy during his time of rest does not excel at his work or perfect it.

Setting aside whether the time of rest is at night or by day: if you contemplate, for example, lands where the sun shines for three or six months and sets for three or six months, do we imagine that their people work for the whole three months and sleep for three months? No; rather they divide this period into night and day, into periods: a period for work and a period for rest.

Therefore you find, from the greatness of the Qur'an, that it takes precaution regarding such matters, and the Almighty says: ﴿And among His signs is your sleep by night and by day, and your seeking of His bounty﴾ [ar-Rum: 23]. Sleep occurs at night, and it also occurs by day for one whose nature of work requires him to work by night.

A house is according to the means of its owner. What matters is that a person has a place to shelter in and rest, however small, even if it is a narrow place just enough for a person to lay his side on the ground. If there is space, so much the better; and the visitor at the door must consider the extent of the lodging of the one he knocks upon.

Just as people differ in their houses, so they differ in the luxury of life and the means of comfort in the home according to their resources. And since comfort is according to resources, each person should adorn himself with contentment, and link his work and his income to the luxury of his life. Before you impose a luxurious life on yourself, first impose on yourself a work of the same level of luxury, so that from it the means of that luxury are secured.

As the proverb says: "Stretch your legs according to the size of your quilt." If your means provide you only with sufficiency, then be content with it; and if you rebel and seek more, then let your first rebellion be against yourself, and do the work that secures what you aspire to.

The affliction of people in their economics is that they first fix the standard of living, then force their income and means to that standard, so deficiency occurs and resources do not meet requirements. The obligation is rather that I fix my standard of living in light of my income and means; by this a person lives happy and at ease, and nothing burdens him. And while we speak of income and resources, we must not overlook observing what is lawful in earning and in spending.

If houses and the means of comfort in them are according to the means of their owners, then their psychological states should likewise be according to their means, so that the heart of the poor is not filled with resentment towards the possessor of blessings.

So: we must adorn ourselves with contentment, and be satisfied with what is in our hands. Who knows, perhaps this possessor of blessing inherited it: if he did not toil for it himself, his forefathers and grandfathers toiled for it. We have previously said that whoever sweats for ten years of his life rests for the rest of his life, whoever sweats for twenty years gives rest to his children, and whoever sweats for thirty gives rest to his grandchildren. And who is it that has sweated and striven and not found the fruit of his sweat?

Whoever wishes to live honoured and respected in his old age, let him work in his youth and while he has strength, and let him sweat before there comes a day in which he does not have this strength. For this reason our master, the Messenger of Allah, observed this meaning in his saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Give the hired worker his wage before his sweat dries." [3]

As for those who loiter in the streets or in cafés, they are not fit for this honourable life in their old age; likewise the worker who does not give his work its due, or does not perfect it, or sits watching the employer waiting for an opportunity to waste time. It is well known that a penny acquired by its owner without right becomes a burden upon him and a corruption of his state, because he did not sweat for it.

And read, if you wish, the saying of our master, the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "Whoever acquires wealth from *mahawish*, Allah will cause it to vanish in *nahabir*." [4] The *mahawish* are the unlawful ways of gathering wealth, which is the same meaning we intend when we say, for example, "So-and-so gathered this wealth from *al-habsh*" or "*al-natsh*"; and the *nahabir* are the doors through which this wealth is spent on what has no benefit. We often see some people whose income and salaries are large, yet they live the life of the poor; no trace of this blessing is seen on them or on their children.

People differ in their view of blessings in the hands of others. The one whose faith is strong, when he sees a blessing in another's hand, does not envy him for it, but sees it as Allah's grace upon His servants, and you see him praying for the possessor of the blessing to be blessed, and saying: "By Allah, he deserves this blessing and more, for he strove and laboured."

The believer says: "What Allah wills," "There is no power except by Allah," "O Allah, bless him and give me of Your blessings." The believer sees in the blessings of this world a miniature model of the blessings of the Hereafter, and says: "This is what humans prepare for themselves, so how much more what Allah has prepared for His creatures?" Then the bliss of Paradise appears to him, and he turns towards it with a heart filled with faith and certainty. This way of regarding others' blessings is called *ghibta* (wholesome desire for the like of what another has).

As for one who is not a believer, may Allah protect us, he resents the possessor of blessing, regards him as undeserving, wishes its removal from him, and envies him for it; all of this is evidence of weak faith and objection to Allah's decrees concerning His creation.

We call the mosques "houses of Allah," and the mosque is called "the house of Allah," because it was made especially so that we may meet Allah therein when we hear...

1 Hammad ibn Zayd said: this verse was revealed concerning those who linger. The majority of exegetes hold that its occasion was that when the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, married Zaynab bint Jahsh, the wife of Zayd, he gave a wedding feast for her and invited the people. When they had eaten, groups of them sat talking in the house of the Messenger of Allah while his wife turned her face to the wall, and they burdened the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Anas said: "I do not know whether I informed the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, that the people had left, or he informed me." Anas said: "The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, set off until he entered the house, and I tried to enter with him, but he drew the curtain between me and him, and the veil was revealed." He said: "He admonished the people with what they were admonished with, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed this verse." Recorded by al-Qurtubi in his tafsir (8/5492).

2 Ibn Manzur said in Lisan al-Arab (root: '-q-l): "The tooth, the finger, the wound and the like are not carried [as blood-money]." And *al-awdah* are silver dirham ornaments.

3 Recorded by Ibn Majah in his Sunan (2443) from the hadith of Ibn Umar. Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id: "Its isnad is weak; in it are two weak narrators." It is also recorded with this wording by al-Tabarani in his al-Mu'jam al-Saghir (1/20) from the hadith of Jabir, and by Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilya (7/142) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah. By the totality of these routes and narrations it rises to the rank of *hasan*, and it has a basis in Sahih al-Bukhari from Abu Hurayrah, in the Book of Sales.

4 Cited by al-Ajluni in Kashf al-Khafa' (2/313), who attributed it to al-Qada'i from Abu Salamah al-Himsi, marfu'. Abu Salamah is weak and has no companionship. Taqi al-Din al-Subki said: "It is not authentic." *Al-mahawish* are gains of evil: every wealth obtained from something not lawful, whose source is not known, such as usurpation, theft and the like [Lisan al-Arab, root: h-w-sh]. *Al-nahabir*: ruin, i.e., He causes it to vanish into ruin and scattered affairs [Lisan al-Arab, root: n-h-b-r].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 33, verse 54:

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿If you disclose a thing or conceal it, indeed Allah is ever Knowing of all things.﴾ (54)

So in the verse there is an indication of warning: beware lest your passing thoughts (khawatir) carry you away in this matter, for your Lord, nothing is hidden from Him, and nothing escapes His knowledge. Although passing thoughts and whisperings (hawajis) are not something a person is held to account for, they are nonetheless forbidden and prohibited when they concern the Messenger of Allah.

There has come in this noble hadith: "Whoever intends an evil deed but does not do it, a good deed is recorded for him" (1). This applies to general matters, but if the matter concerns the Messenger of Allah, then it is not so, because the intention of the Truth, glorified is He, is to preserve the Messenger of Allah's energy for the mission he was sent with, and that nothing preoccupy him from it. And what mission is greater than the mission of guiding the whole world, not only in his time, ﷺ, but from his mission until the Hour is established?

As for His saying, ﴿If you disclose a thing..﴾ (54) [al-Ahzab], i.e., any thing whatsoever, ﴿or conceal it, indeed Allah is ever Knowing of all things﴾ (54) (al-Ahzab). "Knowing" (ʿalim) is an intensive form (ṣīghat mubalagha) in knowledge, because Allah's knowledge is eternal (azali), not renewed with the renewal of events. So Allah knows before the act, during the act, and after it.

Therefore we have said: time, for us, is past, present and future, but with respect to the Truth, glorified is He, there is no past, present or future. Hence He, glorified is He, speaks of the future as if it were past.

Read, for example: ﴿The command of Allah has come, so do not seek to hasten it..﴾ (1) (al-Nahl). "Has come" (atā) is a past verb, and yet after it He says ﴿so do not seek to hasten it﴾ (1) (al-Nahl), and seeking to hasten occurs only for a thing whose time has not come. So "has come" means, with respect to you, that it will come; but with respect to the Truth, glorified is He, it has come in actuality, because all time is equal in Allah's knowledge.

And the meaning of ﴿indeed Allah is ever Knowing of all things﴾ (54) (al-Ahzab) is: He was and still is Knowing, because since He, glorified is He, was Knowing, and knowledge does not undergo change in Him, He is Knowing regarding what has passed and still continues, because He does not change. So "was" (kāna) here does not mean that His knowledge is a result of your event, the event you have brought about; rather He, glorified is He, is Knowing before it occurs from you.

This verse is among those at which the orientalists have stopped, seeking, as they suppose, to find fault in the words of Allah, because they constantly accuse us of regarding the Qur'an with sanctity, that it is the speech of Allah, so we do not employ our minds in it, and that when they scrutinize the Qur'an and dare to investigate it, they find in it objections, by their claim.

The direction of their objection regarding His saying ﴿If you disclose a thing or conceal it, indeed Allah is ever Knowing of all things﴾ (54) (al-Ahzab), and similarly: ﴿And Allah knows what you disclose and what you conceal﴾ (29) [al-Nur].

They say: if Allah boasts of knowing what we conceal, what is the distinction and what is the greatness in knowing what we disclose?

We say: beware, when you read the speech of Allah, of judging it with your mind before you believe that it proceeds from Allah, the Exalted, and that this is His speech, glorified is He. Then, at that point, consider the matter with your mind and investigate it until you reach its wisdom and its aspect of inimitability (i'jaz).

So His saying ﴿If you disclose..﴾ (54) [al-Ahzab]: Allah does not address an individual; rather He addresses the mass of people, and in the case of disclosure by a multitude, you cannot determine the source of the act in it, such that you could trace every voice and every movement to its owner.

We have previously illustrated this with a demonstration, for example, in which voices mingle and chants rise, and we heard, for instance, someone calling for the downfall of so-and-so. Can we in this case identify the owner of this chant? No, we cannot, because of the confusion and overlapping of voices, even though it was a loud proclamation made by its owner at the top of his voice and displayed before the crowd, and yet you cannot identify him.

As for the Truth, glorified is He, He knows the voice, knows its owner, knows its effect and result, and returns every word, and indeed every soul, to its owner. So those who try to conceal themselves and hide among the mass of people should beware: if they create confusion among creation and hide from them, they will not hide from Allah, for Allah is not confused by languages, and voices are not mixed up for Him.

1. On the authority of Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever intends a good deed but does not do it, a good deed is recorded for him; and whoever intends a good deed and does it, ten to seven hundred times its reward is recorded for him; and whoever intends an evil deed but does not do it, nothing is recorded against him, and if he does it, it is recorded." Related by Muslim in his Sahih (130), Kitab al-Iman.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 33, verse 55:

Then the Almighty says:

﴿There is no blame upon them concerning their fathers, nor their sons, nor their brothers, nor the sons of their brothers, nor the sons of their sisters, nor their women, nor what their right hands possess. And fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is ever, over all things, Witness.﴾ (55)

After the verse of hijab was revealed: ﴿And when you ask them for something, ask them from behind a screen...﴾ (53) [al-Ahzab], the relatives of the Mothers of the Believers complained and said: "What about us too, O Messenger of Allah?" So Allah revealed this verse: ﴿There is no blame upon them concerning their fathers...﴾ (55) [al-Ahzab].

The meaning of ﴿There is no blame upon them...﴾ (55) [al-Ahzab] is: there is no sin or wrongdoing in these mentioned persons entering upon them, because their status with respect to the woman is known, and there is no fear from their entering upon her. They are: the father, the son, the brother, the brother's son, and the sister's son.

As for the phrase ﴿nor their women...﴾ (55) [al-Ahzab], it is a construct phrase (mudaf and mudaf ilayhi), and the idafah (annexation, genitive construction) in the Arabic language comes with three meanings: in the sense of "min" (from), like "ardabb sha'ir" meaning "an ardabb of barley," i.e., from barley; in the sense of "fi" (in), like "makr al-layl" (the plotting of the night), meaning "in the night"; and it comes in the sense of "al-lam" (for), like "mal Zayd" (Zayd's wealth), meaning "belonging to Zayd." Here the lam is for ownership or for specialization. So "mal Zayd" means: property belonging to Zayd. And you say "lijam al-faras" (the bridle of the horse): the bridle is not owned by the horse, rather it is specific to it.

So the word ﴿women﴾ (nisa'ihinna) here may carry the sense of "min" and the sense of "li," meaning: women belonging to them, or women from among them. It does not carry the sense of "fi" here. Thus the intended meaning is women from among them, i.e., from their kin, or their women, i.e., those who follow them such as servants, on the condition that they be believers, because the believing woman is the trustee over the believing woman. As for a People of the Book woman or a disbelieving woman, it is not valid for her to serve the believing woman, because she may describe her to her people.

Therefore we observe the precision of expression here in not mentioning the paternal uncles and maternal uncles, because the paternal or maternal uncle, although he is in the station of a father, may describe the girl to his son. If the paternal or maternal uncle has no son, the cause is absent, and it is permissible to be lenient with them, then, in entering upon the woman and displaying adornment before them.

As for His saying: ﴿nor what their right hands possess...﴾ (55) [al-Ahzab], we have said that ownership by the right hand comes from captives in a legitimate war, which you have personally taken captive, meaning that he was not free; then he was taken and sold as a slave. After capture, one may acquire what the right hand possesses by buying him, or taking him as an inheritance, or taking him as a gift. What the right hand possesses may be women, and so they enter under "their women," or it may be boys who have not reached the level of men.

As He, glorified is He, said elsewhere: ﴿or the children who have not yet attained knowledge of the private parts of women...﴾ (31) [al-Nur].

Included in this also are the followers who work in the house, such as doormen, drivers, cooks, etc. The Sharia is lenient with these, because social custom refuses that a relationship should arise between them and the people of the house. These followers work in the houses, and in them are women and beautiful daughters, yet how many of these have dared to look at their mistress? That is because the social position has placed a barrier between them.

Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿And fear Allah...﴾ (55) [al-Ahzab]. It is as if the Almighty is saying: I have clarified to you the ruling on entering upon women, and I have clarified the categories in whose entering there is no blame upon you. The guard over you in this is your taqwa (God-consciousness) of Allah, for the fear of Allah is what moves you to obey Him and prevents you from departing from it. It suffices, after the command to taqwa, that you know ﴿Indeed, Allah is...﴾ (55) [al-Ahzab]. And there remains ﴿over all things Witness﴾ (55) [al-Ahzab].

1 Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir (8/5499): "The paternal uncle and maternal uncle were not mentioned because they take the course of the parents, and the paternal uncle may be called 'father,' as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿We will worship your God and the God of your fathers, Abraham and Ishmael...﴾ (133) [al-Baqarah]..

Then the Truthful (al-Haqq) says, glory be to Him:

﴿Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet. O you who have believed, send blessings upon him and greet him with sincere greetings (56).﴾

The Prophet (ﷺ) came with good for his nation, bringing glad tidings to the believers and a warning to the disbelievers. The Prophet (ﷺ) was eager for the guidance of his people, as the Exalted said: ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves; grievous to him is your suffering; he is anxious over you; for the believers, he is kind and merciful (128).﴾ [at-Tawbah]

The Prophet (ﷺ) would feel pain and sorrow if anyone slipped from his hand and left the sphere of faith, and he would burden himself in the matter of the call beyond what he could bear and beyond what was asked of him, until his Lord addressed him saying: ﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief over their traces, if they do not believe in this message (6).﴾ [al-Kahf]

It is known that our master, the Messenger of Allah, was asked only to convey (the message); as for guidance, it is from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for He, the Exalted, said: ﴿If We willed, We could send down upon them a sign from the heaven, so that their necks would remain humbled before it (4).﴾ [ash-Shu'ara']

Because of the intensity of his eagerness for the guidance of his people, his Lord rebuked him, for it weighed upon his soul; so the rebuke here is for his own benefit (ﷺ), as in the saying of the Exalted: ﴿O Prophet, why do you forbid what Allah has made lawful for you, seeking the approval of your wives...? (1)﴾ [at-Tahrim]

This rebuke is like your rebuke to your son who exhausted himself in studying, so that you pitied him; you do not blame him for negligence, but for overexertion in a task his strength cannot bear.

The peak of his eagerness for his nation (ﷺ) appeared when Allah revealed: ﴿By the morning brightness (1), and by the night when it is still (2), your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested (you) (3). And the Hereafter is better for you than the first (life) (4). And your Lord is going to give you, and you will be satisfied (5).﴾ [ad-Duha]

So the Messenger of Allah took it from his Lord and made it for his nation, and he said: "Then I will not be satisfied while one of my nation is in the Fire." (2)

So if the Messenger of Allah is so eager for you in this manner, he deserves from you that you send blessings upon him; for every good he attains reaches you and returns to you. Therefore the Glorified said: ﴿Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet. O you who have believed, send blessings upon him and greet him with sincere greetings (56).﴾ [al-Ahzab]

You notice that the predicate ﴿send blessings...(56)﴾ [al-Ahzab] is a statement about Allah and the angels; the Truthful combined His blessing with the blessing of His angels. The Prophet (ﷺ) once heard a man giving a sermon, who said: "Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger is rightly guided, and whoever disobeys them, Allah will punish him." The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "Wretched is the orator of the people you are." (3) Why?

They said: Because he combined Allah the Exalted and His Messenger in: "and whoever disobeys them" (ومن يعصمها), whereas he should have said: "whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger." Allah alone is the One who may join with Himself whomever He wills. He, the Glorified, said: ﴿And they found fault with nothing except that Allah and His Messenger had enriched them from His bounty...(74)﴾ [at-Tawbah]

As for us, it is never permissible for us to use a form of association between Allah the Exalted and any of His creatures.

And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet...(56)﴾ [al-Ahzab] — thus Allah has spoken, and He joined with Himself whomever He willed of His creation. You may not make such a joining unless you recite it as Qur'an. If you wish to compose words of your own, you must say: "Allah sends blessings upon the Prophet, and the angels send blessings upon the Prophet."

Therefore the scholars of tafsir were cautious regarding this matter and said that "yusallūn" (يصلون) is not a predicate for both together; rather, the implied predicate is that Allah sends blessings upon the Prophet, and the angels send blessings upon the Prophet.

If Allah sends blessings upon the Prophet and the angels send blessings upon the Prophet, then what about you? You too must send blessings upon the Prophet: ﴿O you who have believed, send blessings upon him and greet him with sincere greetings (56).﴾ [al-Ahzab]

We have already explained that blessing (ṣalāh) from Allah has a meaning, from the angels has a meaning, and from the believers who are commanded to it has a meaning; each according to its own level. Originally, ṣalāh means supplication (du'a'), and supplication requires a supplicant, one for whom it is made, and one who is supplicated. For example, when I ask Allah to forgive so-and-so, I am the supplicant, Allah the Exalted is the one supplicated, and so-and-so is the one for whom it is made. So if the one who blesses and supplicates is Allah the Mighty and Majestic, then who would supplicate? Thus the meaning of supplication does not apply to Allah the Exalted.

Hence we said: if you look at events, you will find that your friend, if he says to you, "I promise to give you such-and-such tomorrow," this is a promise from him, and he possesses none of the means to fulfil it. But if he says, "I ask Allah to give you such-and-such," attributing the giving to Allah the Exalted, this is more likely to be realized, because it is ascribed to Allah; if the supplication is accepted, the request is fulfilled, and if Allah Himself commands this gift, then you will surely receive it without doubt.

Therefore: the blessing from Allah is not in the sense of supplication; rather, it is direct execution, and a comprehensive and general mercy. It is enough of His mercy toward His Prophet (ﷺ) that He made him the Seal of the Prophets, so that no one may surpass him. It is enough of His mercy, bounty and praise toward him that He linked his name with His own name; therefore He addressed him saying: ﴿And We raised high your remembrance (4).﴾ [ash-Sharh]

It is enough of Allah's honouring him that he will be the one whose intercession is received on the Day of Resurrection, not only for his nation but for all creation. It is enough that Allah, the Exalted, addressed all His messengers by their personal names, while He addressed him with the honourable description in: ﴿O Prophet...(12)﴾ [al-Mumtahanah] and ﴿O Messenger...(41)﴾ [al-Ma'idah].

As for the blessing of the angels, it is supplication. Read: ﴿Those who bear the Throne and those around it glorify their Lord with His praise and believe in Him, and ask forgiveness for those who believe: "Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge, so forgive those who repent and follow Your way, and protect them from the punishment of the Blaze (7). Our Lord, and admit them to the Gardens of Eden which You have promised them, along with the righteous among their fathers, their spouses and their descendants. Indeed, You are the Almighty, the Wise (8). And protect them from evil deeds; and whoever You protect from evil deeds on that Day, You have truly had mercy on him. And that is the great triumph (9)."﴾ [Ghafir]

So if all creation is the object of the angels' blessing, their asking forgiveness and their supplication, including those among them who sinned and then repented, then how much more so the Messenger of Allah, who is the guide of all people?

As for the blessing of the believers, it is seeking forgiveness. Their seeking forgiveness is not for the Messenger of Allah; rather, it is for themselves, because the Messenger of Allah came as a mercy to them. And since he came as a mercy to them, it was obligatory that his reverence never leave their minds. If they seek forgiveness, it is forgiveness for their heedlessness of him (ﷺ), or for the fact that his name has not preceded them, so that they send blessings upon him.

When the believer sends blessings upon the Messenger of Allah, what does he possess of giving to offer the Messenger of Allah? What is in our hands? So reflect on the wording of your blessing upon the Messenger of Allah: you do not say "I bless" (usalli), but you say: "O Allah, bless Muhammad," or "May Allah bless Muhammad," thereby asking One who is higher than you to bless the Messenger of Allah, because you have no gift to offer the Messenger of Allah.

Therefore: the blessing from Allah is the general and absolute mercy, the blessing from the angels is supplication, and the blessing from the believers is seeking forgiveness.

Accordingly, the Messenger of Allah was asked: "O Messenger of Allah, that is the blessing of Allah and that is the blessing of the angels; so what is the blessing upon you?" meaning, how is it? He (ﷺ) said: "Say: O Allah, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim; and bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim, in the worlds; indeed, You are Praiseworthy, Glorious." (5)

A companion entered upon him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have never seen you before today with such radiance and cheerfulness." He (ﷺ) said: "Jibril came to me and informed me that whoever sends one blessing upon me, Allah sends ten blessings upon him, writes for him ten good deeds, and erases ten bad deeds from him." (6)

And ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: A man entered upon the Messenger of Allah and asked: "What is the blessing upon you, O Messenger of Allah?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "That is from the hidden knowledge; had you not asked me, I would not have told you. Allah has appointed two angels over me; when one of His servants blesses me, the two angels say: 'May Allah forgive you.' And Allah says: 'Amin,' and the angels say: 'Amin.'" (7)

Glory be to Allah: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, Himself says "Amin" to the supplication of the two angels.

They also said: sending blessings upon the Messenger of Allah is an obligation upon the believer, like the Hajj once in a lifetime; yet it is obligatory upon him at every mention of the Messenger of Allah. Therefore it is stated in the hadith: "The most miserly of people is the one in whose presence I am mentioned and he does not send blessings upon me." (8)

As for His saying after this: ﴿and greet him with sincere greetings (56)﴾ [al-Ahzab] — you may notice at the beginning of the verse: ﴿Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet...(56)﴾ [al-Ahzab], and the Glorified did not say "and they greet." When He commanded the believers, He said: ﴿send blessings upon him and greet him with sincere greetings (56)﴾ [al-Ahzab], adding: "and greet him with sincere greetings."

The scholars said: because blessing upon the Messenger of Allah is not complete except with submission to him, meaning obedience to him and yielding to his command, and surrendering your reins to him in every small and great matter. Otherwise, how could you bless him while you disobey his commands? The Exalted said: ﴿But no, by your Lord, they will not [truly] believe until they make you judge concerning that over which they dispute among themselves, and then find within themselves no discomfort from what you have decided and submit completely (65).﴾ [an-Nisa']

Among the meanings of greeting is that we say: "As-salamu 'alayka ayyuha al-Nabi" (Peace be upon you, O Prophet), as we say in the tashahhud. And "al-Salam" is one of the names of Allah; the meaning of "As-salamu 'alayka ya Rasulallah" is: Allah has made for you a protection, so that no one may harm you.

1 Bakha'a nafsahu: he killed it with rage or grief. Al-Farra' said regarding the meaning of the verse: that is, the one who exits your soul and kills your soul. [Lisan al-'Arab, root: b-kh-'-]..
2 Al-Khatib narrated in "Talkhis al-Mutashabih" from Ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) that he said: "Muhammad will not be pleased while one of his nation is in the Fire." Al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman also narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas that he said: "His pleasure is that his entire nation enter Paradise."..
3 From ʿAdi ibn Hatim: a man gave a sermon before the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger has been rightly guided, and whoever disobeys them has gone astray." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Wretched is the orator you are. Say: 'and whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger has gone astray.'" Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih (870), Ahmad in his Musnad (4/379, 256), and Abu Dawud in his Sunan (1099)..
4 Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir (8/5500): "The scholars differed regarding the pronoun in His saying 'yusallun': one group said the pronoun refers to Allah and the angels, and this is a statement from Allah which honoured His angels. They said: because no one is permitted to join the mention of Allah with another in a single pronoun, and Allah may do in that what He wills. Another group said: there is an ellipsis in the speech, its implied meaning being: Indeed Allah sends blessings, and His angels send blessings, and there is no joining of pronouns in the verse, and that is permissible for humans to do..
5 Al-Bukhari narrated in his Sahih (4797) from the hadith of Ka'b ibn 'Ujrah: It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, as for greeting you, we know it; so how is the blessing upon you?" He said: Say: "O Allah, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed the family of Ibrahim; You are Praiseworthy, Glorious. O Allah, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed the family of Ibrahim; You are Praiseworthy, Glorious."..
6 Cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/650) and attributed to al-Bukhari in al-Adab al-Mufrad from Anas and Malik ibn Aws ibn al-Hadathan that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Jibril (peace be upon him) came to me and said: Whoever sends one blessing upon you, Allah sends ten blessings upon him, and raises him ten degrees."..
7 Mentioned by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/652) from the hadith of al-Hasan ibn 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), and attributed to al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn al-Najjar, its wording being: "Al-Hasan said: They said: O Messenger of Allah, what do you think of the saying of Allah, 'Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet (56)' [al-Ahzab]? He said: 'This is indeed from the concealed knowledge, and had you not asked me about it I would not have told you. Allah has appointed two angels over me; whenever a Muslim servant mentions me and blesses me, those two angels say: May Allah forgive you, and Allah and His angels say in reply to those two angels: Amin. And whenever a Muslim servant mentions me and does not bless me, those two angels say: May Allah not forgive you, and Allah and His angels say to those two angels: Amin.'" Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir (3/515) regarding this hadith: "Very strange, and its chain contains severe weakness."..
8 Narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad (1/201), and Ibn Hibban in his Sahih (2388 – Mawarid al-Zam'an) from the hadith of al-Husayn ibn 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with them both) that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The miser is the one in whose presence I am mentioned and he does not send blessings upon me."..

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 33, verse 57:

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Indeed, those who annoy Allah and His Messenger – Allah has cursed them in this world and the Hereafter, and has prepared for them a humiliating punishment.﴾ (33:57)

Al- Idha' (annoyance): inflicting pain by the one who annoys upon the one annoyed, whether the annoyance is by speech or by deed, and annoyance in this sense is not befitting to the Truth, glory be to Him. So what is the meaning of: "those who annoy Allah"?

They said: Allah, exalted is He, is not harmed by deed, because they are not able to do that; it is an impossible matter. But speech is possible, and annoyance here means angering Allah, exalted is He, by speech that is not fitting for Him, such as their saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is poor and we are rich...﴾ (3:181), and some of them denied the existence of Allah.

And their saying: ﴿The hand of Allah is chained up...﴾ (5:64).

And their saying: ﴿Ezra is the son of Allah...﴾ (9:30).

And some of them revile time (al-dahr), and Allah says in the hadith qudsi: "My servant annoys Me, for he has no right to annoy Me; he reviles time, and I am Time; in My hand is the affair; I turn the night and the day." (1)

Does time bear any blame for the events that cause you pain? Time is merely the container of the event, while the doer is Allah, mighty and majestic. So: do not revile time, for time is Allah. And they themselves said: ﴿It is nothing but our life of this world; we die and we live, and nothing destroys us but time...﴾ (45:24).

All of this is annoyance by speech, but we must examine it: is it a lie and slander, or a true statement supported by evidence? A person may annoy you with a word, yet you are not harmed by it; in that case he bears its sin, and you are safe from its evil and from its pain... So these sayings of theirs do in reality contain annoyance, but not to Allah, the Exalted; rather it is annoyance to them. How?

When the Truth, glory be to Him, appointed man as vicegerent on earth, He created for him the cosmos before creating him. Man arrived in a cosmos prepared to receive him, containing the foundations of the continuation of life and the foundations of the continuation of the species. Then He also prepared for him a law of his preservation, so that if he suffered a defect he could repair it. This law is His method, glory be to Him, preserved in His Book. Read the words of the Truth, glory be to Him: ﴿The Most Merciful (1) taught the Qur'an (2) created man (3) taught him the bayan (4)﴾ (55:1-4).

The law of preservation is in the Qur'an, existing before man was created, because man is the creation of Allah, and His handiwork, which Allah created in the best stature and in the finest form, and He wills that he remain so, sound in every aspect of his formation. So when this vicegerent created by Allah departs from the law of his preservation, he will undoubtedly anger Allah, because Allah wants His handiwork to remain beautiful, as He originated it, glory be to Him.

Therefore, those who deny the existence of Allah, or those who associate partners with Him, and those who say: "Indeed Allah is poor and we are rich," or who say: "The angels are daughters of Allah," etc. — these sayings entail the anger of the Truth, glory be to Him, because he (man) as His vicegerent on earth did not perform what was required of him according to the method of Allah.

And we say to these people: beware lest you think that by your disbelief you have escaped the grip of the Truth, glory be to Him; rather you are in His grip and under His will. Had He willed, He would have compelled you to obey Him, or created you in the state of righteousness so that disobedience would not come from you, as He created the angels. Rather He made you free in what He charged you with: whoever wills, let him believe, and whoever wills, let him disbelieve, so that He may know who turns to Him in love, not by compulsion.

The proof of this is that you are created in two states: a state in which you have choice, which is the obligations (al-taklif), and a state in which you are held in the grip of the Truth, glory be to Him, which is the decree (al-qada'). Since you have grown accustomed to rebelling against the obligations, why do you not rebel against the decrees of Allah concerning you, such as sickness and death, for example?

Moreover, since you have chosen disbelief, and I am the Lord, and it is required of me to help you attain what you love, I will seal your heart, so that faith does not enter it and the disbelief you love does not leave it. Thus I have come to your desire, which shows that your disbelief in Me does not harm Me or annoy Me.

It has come in the hadith qudsi: "O My servants, you will never reach My benefit so as to benefit Me, and you will never reach My harm so as to harm Me." (2)

And if you have a domain of choice in this world, which is the matter of the obligations, there will come a Day of Resurrection when all choice ceases, and no one has choice in anything on the day when the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Whose is the dominion today?﴾ (40:16), and no one answers, neither owner nor owned, so the Truth, glory be to Him, answers Himself: ﴿To Allah, the One, the Subduer.﴾ (40:16)

This concerns the meaning regarding Allah, exalted is He. As for the annoyance regarding our master the Messenger of Allah, the Messenger of Allah is a human being, and he can be afflicted with annoyance by deed and by speech. Just as they said "Allah is poor and we are rich," they said of the Messenger of Allah: "a soothsayer, a sorcerer, a madman, a poet." Then the annoyance exceeded into deed, which afflicted the Messenger of Allah and pained him by action.

Was he not struck with stones until his feet bled at Ta'if? (3) Did they not place on his noble back the afterbirth of a camel in Makkah (4), that is, the camel's afterbirth fell? Was his front tooth not broken on the day of Uhud, and was his face not cut and his blood not flowing, may Allah bless him and grant him peace? (5)

So the Messenger of Allah was touched, along with his Lord, mighty and majestic, by annoyance in speech, then he was touched by another annoyance in deed, a human annoyance that involves pain. The peak of annoyance by deed is when his sacred prohibitions and his wives, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, are violated.

Therefore Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And it is not for you to annoy the Messenger of Allah...﴾ (33:53), that is: by opposing what he brought, or by accusing him of what is not in him, or by subjecting him to physical pain. Then He specified among the kinds of annoyance only the matter of the wives, saying: ﴿Nor to marry his wives after him, ever.﴾ (33:53). He mentioned this matter specifically and openly, out of regard for the nature of the human soul. We have said that a man may show generosity to his companions or loved ones with the most precious of what he owns, but he will never accept that anyone look at his wife; he protects her and is jealous of her even from a mere glance.

Therefore, our master Hudhayfah, who loved his wife, said to her: "Do you not wish to be with me in Paradise?" She said: "Yes." He said: "Then, if I die, do not marry after me," for he was jealous over her even after his death, because I heard the Messenger of Allah say: "A woman belongs to her last husband." (6)

However, this hadith was countered by another hadith: when the Messenger of Allah was asked: "Which of a man's wives will be with him in Paradise?" He said: "The one with the best character toward him." (7)

Some saw a contradiction between these two hadiths, but in reality there is no contradiction between them, because "last" here does not mean last in time, but last in transition, as when you enjoyed a beautiful journey with one of your friends twenty years ago, and when you remind him of it he says: "That was the last pleasure," even though you enjoyed other journeys after it.

The meaning is: she belongs to her last husband in enjoyment, even though he was earlier in good character. So the two meanings agree; there is no contradiction between them.

The matter of a man's jealousy over a woman has roots in our history and Arab literature, such as the saying of the poet (8):

I am infatuated with Da'd as long as I live, and if I die,
Alas, who will be infatuated with her after me?

He is occupied with her even after he dies, but it is held against him that he was occupied with the one who will replace him in his passion for his beloved. So more eloquent than him is the saying of another (9):

I am infatuated with Da'd as long as I live, and if I die,
May Da'd never be good for a lover after me!

Thus this jealousy has levels and degrees.

History tells us that one of the Abbasid caliphs, I think it was al-Hadi, loved a slave-girl named Ghadir, and out of his intense love for her they said he married her. In one of their intimate moments of passion and love he said to her, since his health was not good: "Promise me that if I die you will not marry after me." She indeed gave him this pledge. When al-Hadi died, she soon forgot her love for al-Hadi and forgot her grief over him, and this is one of Allah's mercies upon us: everything begins small and then grows, except calamities, which begin great and then diminish.

After that, Ghadir married the brother of al-Hadi. One day she awoke frightened and screaming, until those in the palace gathered around her and asked her: "What is wrong with you?" She said: "al-Hadi came to me in a dream and said to me:

You broke my pledge after you dwelt with the dwellers of graves,
And you married Ghadirah, the brother of him who named you Ghadir,
May the new companionship not bring you happiness, nor may the circles return to you,
And you joined me since morning, and wherever you went you became a follower."

She had hardly finished her saying when her last breaths departed, and she died.

Therefore, the Truth, glory be to Him, takes into account these human instincts and this nature. Do you not see that the waiting period of a woman whose husband has died was one full year, as in His saying: ﴿And those who die among you and leave wives behind – a bequest for their wives: provision for a year without eviction.﴾ (2:240)

Then the waiting period of a widow was made four months and ten days, out of respect for this instinct in women.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, explains the just recompense for those who annoy Allah and annoy His Messenger, saying, glory be to Him: ﴿Allah has cursed them...﴾ (33:57), that is, He has expelled them from His mercy ﴿in this world and the Hereafter, and has prepared for them a humiliating punishment.﴾ (33:57)

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, gives us a sign that this just recompense which He has prepared for those who annoy Allah and His Messenger is not zealotry for Allah, nor zealotry for the Messenger of Allah, as evidenced by the fact that whoever annoys a believing man or woman must be recompensed for that annoyance. He equated the believing man and woman in the intent to annoy with annoying Allah and annoying His Messenger, saying, glory be to Him:

﴿And those who annoy believing men and believing women without their having earned it have certainly borne a slander and a manifest sin.﴾ (33:58)
