Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 33, verse 58:

When the Truthful, Glorified One spoke of harming the believing men and believing women, He specified this harm by His saying ﴿without their having earned it﴾ [al-Ahzab] because there is a lawful harm that Allah has made obligatory for those who transgress His limits. The prescribed penalty (hadd) for fornication (zina), for slander (qadhf), for drinking wine (shurb al-khamr), and so on, all of these involve harm to the believing man and the believing woman, but it is lawful harm, and whoever carries it out is not punished, just as with the harm done to Allah and His Messenger.

Therefore the Exalted says concerning the two who commit indecency: ﴿And those two who commit it among you, then harm them﴾ [al-Nisa].

When the Truthful, Glorified One prescribed these penalties and this harm, He prescribed it only as a punishment for whoever oversteps the limits of Allah, and as a purification for him from his sin, and then as a deterrent for others. When Sayyidina Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) recited this verse: ﴿And those who harm believing men and believing women...﴾ [al-Ahzab], he wept. His companion said to him: "What makes you weep, O Commander of the Faithful?" He said: "Because I have harmed the believing men and believing women." He said: "O Commander of the Faithful, you harm in order to teach and to correct, and Allah the Exalted has commanded us to stone and to cut off hands." So Umar laughed and was delighted.(1)

Moreover, in the matter of the prescribed penalties, the Truthful, Glorified One commands us even more than this: ﴿And let not pity for them detain you in the religion of Allah﴾ [al-Nur].

For compassion toward the penalties of Allah is a foolish mercy, and we are not more merciful to creation than the Creator, Glorified is He. When Allah magnifies the punishment and emphasizes it, He only wants us not to dare against His limits, and not to expose ourselves to these punishments. And you may ask when you read His saying: ﴿And for you in retribution there is life﴾ [al-Baqarah].

How can there be life in killing? Yes, in retribution (qisas) there is life, because when you know that if you kill you will be killed, you will never proceed to killing, and thus Allah has protected both the killer and the killed. Would this be considered harm?

The meaning of ﴿without their having earned it﴾ [al-Ahzab] is: without a crime that deserves harm. As for the word ﴿earned﴾ [iktasabu] in the verse, we have said: there is a difference between fa'ala and if'tala. Fa'ala is the natural act that contains neither exaggeration nor affectation, whereas if'tala contains affectation and exaggeration. Likewise kasaba and iktasaba: kasaba means that you take hold of a thing beyond what you were given, as if you bought for five and sold for seven, for example, so this is kasb; but iktasaba contains additional effort and contrivance.

Therefore you find in general linguistic usage that kasaba is used for good and iktasaba is used for evil, like His saying: ﴿For it is what it has earned, and against it is what it has earned﴾ [al-Baqarah]. "For it is what it has earned" indicates ownership, and "against it is what it has earned" indicates debt.

This is because lawful matters come naturally and spontaneously, whereas the unlawful requires attempt, contrivance and caution. When you look, for example, at your wife, you are natural and make no effort; but when you look at a beautiful woman in the street, you steal glances, and you sneak, fearing that someone will see your deed. This is the difference between the lawful and the unlawful.

In one verse of the Book of Allah the verb kasaba is used for evil, and that is His saying: ﴿Yes, whoever earns an evil deed and his sin surrounds him, those are the companions of the Fire﴾ [al-Baqarah].

Why? They said: because the verse concerns one who has become accustomed to evil deeds, whose sins have surrounded him until they became a habit, and became easy for him until they were for him like the lawful, which he does without effort; rather he openly flaunts them and boasts of them. This is the one who openly commits sin, concerning whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "All my community will be forgiven except the openly sinful," and in it: "Allah has covered him, and he rises up exposing himself."

And this one who rejoices in sin and boasts of it has reached such mastery that he can conceal the movements of his emotion in the unlawful as if they were the lawful itself. Therefore the verb kasaba comes here, as if the evil deed had become a settled disposition.

I recall, in connection with contrivance and affectation in the unlawful, a man from our town named Sheikh Mustafa, who went to the market to buy a cow and put the money in his pocket. Out of his caution he placed his hand over his pocket for fear of thieves. When they saw him in the market holding his pocket with his hand, they knew he was their target. How did they trick him into being robbed? One of them smeared his shoulder with animal dung, then rubbed against Sheikh Mustafa until his clothes were soiled, so he became angry and began cleaning his clothes of the dung, forgetting the matter of the money in his pocket, and they robbed him.

Just as the unlawful comes with affectation, so too its punishment is affected and exaggerated in proportion to the affectation of the act. Therefore the Exalted says concerning the punishment of those who harm the believing men and believing women without their having earned it: ﴿Then they have borne a slander﴾ [al-Ahzab]. He did not say "hamalu" (they carried); and there is a difference between hamala and ihtamala. Hamala is said of what is within your capacity to carry, whereas ihtamala means beyond capacity; and if you carry it, you carry it with hardship. So the recompense here is of the same kind as the deed: just as you engaged in effort and affectation in disobedience, so the recompense for it will be.

﴿Then they have borne a slander and a manifest sin﴾ [al-Ahzab]. Buhtan (slander) is saying about another what is not in him; so buhtan is a lie. As for ithm (sin), it is that you commit a wrong against him by harming him with an attribute that is actually in him, but which he dislikes you to ascribe to him, as when you say to a blind man, for example: "O blind one!"

Therefore it is reported in a hadith that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked: "Do you see, if there is in my brother what I say?" He said: "If there is in him what you say, you have backbitten him, and if there is not in him what you say, you have slandered him."(3) That is: you have lied and fabricated against him.

The Truthful, Glorified One described the sin here as manifest ﴿and a manifest sin﴾ [al-Ahzab], meaning clear and evident, because the evidence of sin is either that you yourself acknowledge it and confess your wrong, or that there is proof. If we asked you: "Did you say to this man, 'O blind one!'? Would you like to be described with an attribute you dislike?" you must say: "I do not like it." So the sin here is evident, and your acknowledgment of it suffices.

And you should treat people as you wish them to treat you, as the Messenger of Allah taught us. Just as it does not please you that people steal from you, so you should not steal from them; and just as sin harms you, so it harms them.

1. Cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/657), attributing it to Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim from Qatadah concerning the verse, who said: "Beware of harming the believers, for Allah protects them and is angered on their behalf. It is claimed that Umar ibn al-Khattab recited it one day, and it alarmed him so much that he went to Ubayy ibn Ka'b (may Allah be pleased with him), entered upon him and said: 'O Abu al-Mundhir, I recited a verse of the Book of Allah and it struck me with every impact: ﴿And those who harm believing men and believing women...﴾ [al-Ahzab]. By Allah, I punish them and strike them.' He said to him: 'You are not one of them; you are only a teacher.'" See also the Tafsir of al-Qurtubi (8/5509): "You are only a teacher and corrector."
2. A hadith agreed upon (Muttafaqun alayh). Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (6069), and likewise Muslim in his Sahih (2990), from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "All my community will be forgiven except the openly sinful. Among openness is that a man does a deed at night, then in the morning, though Allah has covered it for him, he says: 'O so-and-so, I did such-and-such last night,' and he spent the night while his Lord covered him, and he rises up uncovering the cover of Allah from himself."
3. Related by Muslim in his Sahih (2589), Kitab al-Birr wa al-Silah, and likewise Ahmad in his Musnad (2/230, 384, 386), from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do you know what backbiting is?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "Your mention of your brother with what he dislikes." It was said: "Do you see, if there is in my brother what I say?" He said: "If there is in him what you say, you have backbitten him, and if there is not in him, you have slandered him."

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, takes us to another etiquette of the household, saying:

﴿O Prophet, say to your wives and your daughters and the women of the believers: they should draw their outer garments over themselves. That is more suitable that they will be known and not be harmed. And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ (33:59)

We note that the command was first addressed to the wives of the Prophet, then to his daughters, peace and blessings be upon him. This means that the Messenger of Allah does not order his community to do something he himself exempts himself from; rather, he orders them to do something he begins with his own household. This is more conducive to the acceptance and implementation of the command: before I command you, I have commanded myself, so I have not set myself apart from you in anything.

Thus it is related in the biography of the Muslim commander "Tariq ibn Ziyad" (1) that when he went to conquer al-Andalus, he stood with his soldiers on the shore of the sea, while his enemies were on the other shore. Then he said to the soldiers: "O people, I will not order you to do a thing from which I myself am exempt. When the two groups meet, I will be ahead of you. I will confront the leader of the people. If I kill him, you will have been spared his affair; and if he kills me, you will not lack a leader after me."

That is: I will be ahead of you in fighting, and I will not send you out while I sit watching and observing what happens. In other words: I do not set myself apart from you in anything.

By this same equality, too, ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) governed the people and led the world while he wore his patched garment in Madinah. Therefore, when a man saw him sleeping under a tree like the common people, he said: "You judged justly, so you were just, and so you were secure, and so you slept, O ʿUmar."

When he (may Allah be pleased with him) wished to make a decision regarding a matter of his subjects' affairs, he knew that corruption comes first from the entourage, the relatives, the followers, and the centres of power that surround a ruler. Therefore he would gather his kinsmen and warn them: "I have resolved to issue a decision regarding such and such. By Him in whose hand is my soul, whoever of you opposes me in any part of it, I will make him an example for the Muslims. O people, beware lest there enter upon you one who claims kinship with me, so that you give him what is not his right; by Allah, if you do, I will make you an example for the Muslims."

The Qur'anic text's wording ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives...﴾ (33:59) is evidence that our master the Messenger of Allah was transmitting the text that came to him, in the very form in which Allah spoke, without changing anything in it. Otherwise he could have conveyed the command to his wives by saying: "O Prophet's wives and daughters, draw your outer garments over yourselves." Rather, he conveyed the Qur'anic text as it was revealed to him, so that everyone would know that the command is from Allah, and that Muhammad is only a conveyor from Allah; so whoever wishes to dispute the matter, let him dispute with its Author.

When this verse was revealed, the wives of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, numbered nine. Allah honoured them and gave them the choice, and they chose the Messenger of Allah. Five of them were from Quraysh: ʿĀʾishah, Ḥafṣah, Umm Ḥabībah, Umm Salamah, and Sawdah bint Zamʿah. Three were from the rest of the Arabs: Maymūnah bint al-Ḥārith, Zaynab bint Jaḥsh, and Juwayriyah bint al-Ḥārith from the Banū al-Muṣṭaliq. And one was from the lineage of Hārūn, brother of Mūsā, peace be upon them both: the lady Ṣafiyyah bint Ḥuyayy ibn Akhṭab.

As for the daughters of the Messenger of Allah: the Messenger of Allah had sons and daughters. The sons all died in childhood, while Allah preserved the daughters until they were all married: Zaynab, Ruqayyah, and Umm Kulthum. The youngest of them was Fāṭimah, and she was the only one who remained after the death of our master the Messenger of Allah; as for Zaynab, Ruqayyah, and Umm Kulthum, they died during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah.

Fāṭimah has a story of laughter and weeping. Therefore some of the knowers used to say, concerning the Almighty's words ﴿And that it is He who makes laugh and makes weep﴾ (53:43), that when Fāṭimah was asked, "What made you weep, and what made you laugh?" she said: "When I entered upon my father while he was ill, he said to me, 'This is the illness of death, O Fāṭimah,' so I wept. Then I left, and he signalled to me and said, 'O Fāṭimah, you will be the first of my household to join me,' so I laughed." Therefore Fāṭimah did not remain after the Messenger of Allah except for six months.

The scholars have derived from this hadith that the meeting of the dead takes place immediately upon death; for if the meeting were at the Resurrection and the Last Day, those who died first and those who died last would be equal in that respect. The words "you will be the first of my household to join me" indicate that his meeting with her, peace and blessings be upon him, will occur as soon as she dies.

The point in this story is that one of them, I think it was Imam ʿAlī, said to Fāṭimah: "Allah says ﴿And that it is He who makes laugh and makes weep﴾ (53:43); but the Messenger of Allah made you weep first and then made you laugh, so that the 'makes laugh and makes weep' is not a grief for him."

As for Lady Zaynab (3), she was married to al-ʿĀṣ ibn al-Rabīʿ (4) before marriage to polytheists was forbidden. Al-ʿĀṣ was taken captive at the Battle of Badr, so Zaynab went to ransom him and sent a necklace she had with her. When the Messenger of Allah saw it, he recognised that it was the necklace of Khadījah, may Allah be pleased with her, which she had given to her daughter. He said: "If you think fit to return her necklace to her and release her captive, then do so." So the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, left the matter to those who would benefit from it, and they relinquished the necklace (5).

As for Ruqayyah and Umm Kulthum, they had incidents, some of them regrettable and some joyful. The regrettable: ʿUtbah ibn Abī Lahab had contracted marriage with Ruqayyah, and his brother ʿUtaybah had contracted marriage with Umm Kulthum, and this was before the Messenger of Allah's mission. When the Messenger of Allah was commissioned and what happened between him and Abū Lahab occurred, Allah revealed: ﴿Perish the hands of Abū Lahab, and perish he. His wealth and what he earned will not benefit him﴾ (111:1–2).

He said to his son ʿUtbah: "My head and yours are forbidden to one another until you divorce Ruqayyah." So he divorced her. After that, ʿUtbah passed by the Messenger of Allah and did an act containing mockery of the Messenger of Allah, and he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "May a dog of Allah's dogs devour you" (6).

ʿUtbah informed his father of the Prophet's supplication against him. Abū Lahab knew the truthfulness of the Messenger of Allah and that his supplication is answered and not rejected, so he feared for his son, took precautions for him, and entrusted him to his companions on his trading journeys. Strangely, despite all this, he did not believe.

Indeed, ʿUtbah used to sleep in the midst of the caravan while they surrounded him on every side. But one night a lion came to him, seized him from among the people, and nothing of him remained except what he could be recognised by.

One of the ill-disposed commented on this incident, saying: "The Messenger of Allah said, 'May a dog devour you,' and this is a lion." One of the knowers replied to him: "When the dog is attributed to Allah, it must be a lion. The Messenger of Allah did not say 'a dog of your dogs', but 'a dog of Allah's dogs' (7)." This was the matter of ʿUtbah. As for ʿUtaybah, he divorced Umm Kulthum, but he did not confront the Messenger of Allah with harm; rather, they said he was too shy to face the Messenger of Allah, so the Messenger of Allah did not invoke against him.

As for the joyful incident in the lives of Ruqayyah and Umm Kulthum: Allah replaced them with better than ʿUtbah and ʿUtaybah. Ruqayyah married our master ʿUthmān, and when she died he married Umm Kulthum after her. Therefore he, may Allah be pleased with him, was given the title Dhū al-Nūrayn (Possessor of the Two Lights). The women used to sing when ʿUthmān married Ruqayyah:

"The best two persons a man has seen are Ruqayyah and her husband ʿUthmān (8)."

Consider the greatness of this recompense: that Allah replaced them with ʿUtbah and ʿUtaybah — and who? ʿUthmān! Indeed, what a recompense. Recompense in such matters comes through accepting the decree in its like. If a person is afflicted, submits, and entrusts the matter to Allah, saying as the Messenger of Allah taught us: "Indeed we belong to Allah and to Him we return. O Allah, reward me in my affliction, whatever the affliction is, and replace it for me with something better" (9).

When he says that and knows that Allah has wisdom in every decree He decrees, Allah will surely replace it for him with something better. I think the story of Lady Umm Salamah is famous in this context. When her husband Abū Salamah died, she grieved over him intensely. When the women came to console her over her husband, one of them said: "O Umm Salamah, say as the Messenger of Allah said: 'Indeed we belong to Allah and to Him we return. O Allah, reward me in my affliction and replace it for me with something better than it.'" She said: "Is there anything better than Abū Salamah?" meaning: in her view he was the best and most excellent of people.

Yet despite this, she accepted Allah's decree. She had not finished her waiting period when someone knocked on her door, saying: "O Umm Salamah, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, is proposing to you for himself." She laughed, because Allah had replaced her with one better than Abū Salamah (10).

After the Truthful, glorified is He, had first commanded the wives and daughters of the Prophet with this etiquette, He extended it to the women of the believers, saying: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives and your daughters and the women of the believers: they should draw their outer garments over themselves...﴾ (33:59), because the family of the Messenger of Allah is not only his wives and daughters, but the whole world. The word "nisā'" (women) is a plural with no singular from its own form: the singular of "azwāj" is "zawj," and the singular of "banāt" is "bint," but the singular of "nisā'" is from its meaning, not its form, so you say "imra'ah." The plural of "imra'ah" as "imra'āt" was deemed too heavy, so they said "nisā'," and its origin in the language is from "nasi'," they said, because woman's creation came later after man's creation. In the language, "nasi'" means postponement and deferral, so they said "nisā'."

Then He mentions the command addressed to the wives of the Prophet, his daughters, and all the women of the believers: ﴿they should draw their outer garments over themselves...﴾ (33:59). The verb ﴿yudnīna﴾ is in the jussive as the answer to the imperative "qul" (say), like: "be silent and you will be safe; study and you will succeed." In the verse there is an implied condition: "If you say to them, 'Draw them,' they will draw them." As in ﴿And proclaim to the people the pilgrimage; they will come to you on foot﴾ (22:27). The address here is to the believing women, headed by the wives and daughters of the Prophet; and if these do not comply with the command, then the condition of faith has been violated in them.

The meaning of "idnā'" (drawing near) is bringing one thing close to another. From this is His saying, describing the fruits of Paradise, ﴿its clusters hanging low﴾ (69:23), meaning easy to reach and easy to pick. The intended meaning is: they draw their outer garments (jalābīb) down from above, to cover the body. His words ﴿over themselves﴾ indicate that it covers the whole body, wrapped around it and let down to the ground.

The word ﴿jalābībihinna﴾ has the singular "jilbāb," and they differed in defining it. They said: it is the garment worn over the inner garment; so if the inner clothing is, for example, a vest or a shirt and trousers, the jilbāb is worn over it. The inner clothing may be short, but the jilbāb must be ample, long, and near the ground (11).

They also said: the jilbāb is the head-covering (khimār) that covers the head and is drawn over the neck-opening (juyūb), i.e., the opening of the collar. But this is not sufficient; it must be let down to the ground to cover the woman entirely, because a woman's body is ʿawrah (private), and some garments reveal, some describe, and some attract attention.

It is a condition in the lawful dress of a woman that it not be revealing, nor descriptive, nor attention-attracting. For some women wear a long, ample jilbāb that reveals nothing of their body, yet it is tight, describing the chest and the buttocks and displaying the contours, so that she appears as if she were naked (12).

Therefore, among the literary expressions on this matter is the saying of one of them, and he is right: "A woman's excessive display of adornment is an insistent offering of herself to a man." That is: she wants to attract his gaze, wants to alert the heedless, as if she were saying: "We are here." If we are lenient about this with an unmarried girl, there may be an excuse for her; but what excuse is there for the married one?

Then the Blessed and Exalted Truth explains the wisdom of this etiquette in the matter of dress, saying: ﴿That is...﴾ (33:59), that is: lowering the jilbāb to the ground, covering the body, and not displaying adornment. ﴿...more suitable...﴾ (33:59), that is: closer; ﴿that they will be known and not be harmed﴾ (33:59).

The Muslim woman is recognised by her dress and modesty, so no one dares to approach her with evil or to molest her. Her clothing and dignity tell you that she is not of that cheap kind who awaits a signal from you, nor one who presents herself in an arousing, enticing, attention-seeking manner.

As for His saying, after that...

She said: "He told me of his death, so I wept; then he told me that I would be the first of his family to follow him, so I laughed."

The hadith...

11. This is what al-Qurṭubī held in his Tafsīr (8/5511). He said: "The jalābīb is the plural of jilbāb, which is a garment larger than the khimār. It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn Masʿūd that it is the rida' (wrapper). It has also been said that it is the qināʿ (veil), but the correct view is that it is the garment that covers the whole body."

12 Al-Hakim narrated in his Mustadrak (4/187) from the hadith of Dihya ibn Khalifa al-Kalbi that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent him to Heraclius, and he returned, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave him a qibti (Egyptian cloth). He said: "Cut it in half (its half) into a shirt, and give your companion (your wife) the other half to cover her head with." When he turned to leave, he said: "Tell her to put something beneath it so that it does not reveal the shape of her body (lest it describe her)." Al-Hakim said: "This is a hadith with a sound chain of narration, but the two (Shaykhs) did not record it." Al-Dhahabi said: "In it there is a break in the chain (inqita')."

Then Allah, glorified is He, says:

{If the hypocrites, those in whose hearts is a disease, and the agitators in al-Madinah do not desist, We will surely incite you against them; then they will not remain your neighbours there except briefly.} (60)

One who follows the procession of the messages finds that the Messengers, in spreading their message, faced three kinds of people: a group that believed, a group that disbelieved, and a group that stood wavering between disbelief and belief, and these are the hypocrites (munafiqun).

That is because a Messenger is sent only to change a social condition that has reached a degree of corruption people cannot bear. Whoever suffers from this condition awaits this new Messenger, and as soon as he is sent, they hasten to believe in him, because he has brought new principles, free of injustice, oppression, tyranny, bribery and corruption.

Thus, whoever has been afflicted by these events and suffered from this corruption hastens to belief. Likewise the people of Egypt believed, and as soon as Islam entered it they hastened towards it. Why? Because they had suffered before it under Roman rule. Likewise the Persians believed as soon as they heard of Islam, and they saw the good example in the Muslims after the corruption of the non-Muslims had afflicted them.

Whenever people suffer from corrupt conditions, they look forward to a savior, and if one comes to them, they follow him, especially if he is one of them and has an honourable past in which they never found him to be a liar or a deceiver.

This is what we saw, for example, in the story of the conversion of Sayyidina Abu Bakr. As soon as Muhammad announced that he was the Messenger of Allah, he hastened to believe in him without asking him about anything. Why? Because he knew his truthfulness, knew his trustworthiness, and was certain of that.

Similar was the belief of Sayyidah Khadijah, may Allah be pleased with her. When the Messenger of Allah came to her agitated by what he had encountered of the descent of the angel upon him, she embraced him, calmed his fear, and did him justice. She took him to Waraqa ibn Nawfal to confirm for him that he was upon the truth, and that Allah, the Exalted, would never abandon him or forsake him.

Among what she said was: "By Allah, you surely honour the guest, bear the burdens of others, earn for the destitute, and help them in the calamities of time..."

Therefore the scholars said: Sayyidah Khadijah was the first female jurist (faqihah) in Islam, before Islam was revealed.

It is natural that the people of corruption, and those who profit from it, stand in opposition. They benefit from corruption and tyranny, and they want their lordship and status to endure, and the people to remain their slaves, consuming their good things and humiliating them.

Those who have enslaved people and made themselves masters, even gods, and who know that the Messenger came only to end their lordship and their false divinity, must inevitably confront the call. They must disbelieve in it and fight it, to preserve their lordship and their temporal authority.

It is strange to see some of the common people who have become accustomed to this servitude, accepted this humiliation, and been content to live under the protection of these masters whatever the consequences. These and their like are the ones who said: ﴿They say, "Why was this Qur'an not sent down to a great man from one of the two towns?"﴾ [Az-Zukhruf] (31)

So after the savior Messenger came to them, they continued to look forward to a great man who would enslave them.

Each of these two groups (the believer and the disbeliever) was consistent with himself. The believer believed with his heart and spoke with his tongue, and the disbeliever disbelieved with his heart and disbelieved with his tongue, because he did not utter the word of monotheism. A human being is heart and form, and in faith the form must agree with what is in the heart.

As for the third category, the hypocrite, he is not consistent with himself, because he believed with his tongue but did not believe with his heart. He is a coward who shows you love and conceals hatred. Therefore Allah placed them in the lowest level of the Fire.

So when the Messenger of Allah asked the Arabs to say, "There is no god but Allah," in order to nullify the authority of the leaders of disbelief, they refused to say it. Why? Because they knew it was not merely a word spoken, but that it carries consequences and entails responsibilities they could not bear. Had it been merely a word spoken, they would have said it, and the enmity between them and the Messenger of Allah would have ended.

So the meaning of "There is no god but Allah" is: no servitude except to Allah, no submission except to Allah, no legislation except from Allah, no benefit except from Allah... etc. And how can these meanings agree with one who has become accustomed to servitude and submission to other than Allah?

When the Exalted spoke here about the hypocrites, He singled out al-Madinah, saying: ﴿If the hypocrites, and those in whose hearts is a disease, and the agitators in al-Madinah...﴾ [Al-Ahzab] (60). Hypocrisy did not appear in Makkah, the stronghold of disbelief and idols, but appeared in al-Madinah, which sheltered the emigrants of the Messenger of Allah. Most of its people were from the People of the Book (ahl al-Kitab), who were closer to belief than the disbelievers. So why this phenomenon?

It has been said: because Islam was weak in Makkah and became strong in al-Madinah. Hypocrisy is a healthy sign for Islam, because had it not been strong, the hypocrites would not have feigned it. The appearance of hypocrisy in al-Madinah is evidence of the strength of Islam there, and that it had gained power and dominance. Therefore the weak in faith became hypocrites in order to take the good of Islam and to seek shelter under its protection. Otherwise, the weak do not feign.

Yes, hypocrisy appeared in al-Madinah, about whose people Allah said: ﴿And those who had already settled the abode and faith before them love those who emigrate to them, and do not find in their breasts any need for what they have been given, and they prefer them over themselves, even though they themselves are in need.﴾ [Al-Hashr] (9)

And the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said of it: "Faith surely retreats to al-Madinah as a snake retreats into its hole."

Also the Qur'an itself said about the people of al-Madinah: ﴿And among the people of al-Madinah are those who have become hardened in hypocrisy...﴾ [At-Tawbah] (101). This is not a belittling of al-Madinah, but a demonstration of the strength of Islam there, such that it had acquired a power and might that hypocrisy had to feign towards.

Here is His saying: ﴿If the hypocrites do not desist...﴾ (60). When you hear ﴿If they do not desist...﴾ (60), know that Allah has sworn by something, and this statement is the answer to the oath. The Exalted does not swear except by a great thing. We humans swear to confirm our words, as you say: "By Allah, what so-and-so did was such and such, and I will do such and such."

As for the Exalted, His speech is truthful and effective without an oath, so what of when He swears? Therefore some of the knowers (ʿarifun) say: when Allah, the Exalted, is heard swearing, who has angered the Generous until He was compelled to swear?

The word ﴿the hypocrites...﴾ (60) has as its singular munafiq, derived from nafiqa' al-yarbu'. The yarbu' (jerboa) is a small animal resembling a mouse, known to the people of the desert. It lives in burrows, and hunters watch for it to catch it when it comes out of its burrow. But this small animal has cunning and craftiness: what does it do? It makes two entrances to its burrow, one known and the other concealed by something. When it senses the hunter at the known entrance, it goes to the other entrance. Therefore the hypocrite is exactly like one who has a disbelieving heart and a believing tongue.

You notice that Allah described the hypocrites here with three attributes: ﴿the hypocrites, those in whose hearts is a disease, and the agitators in al-Madinah...﴾ (60). The conjunction here does not necessarily imply difference, but rather the coordination of different attributes of one thing. These attributes came separately because they had become so manifest in them that they were almost a distinct type of its own.

The Qur'an has described the hypocrites elsewhere as having a disease in their hearts, saying: ﴿And among the people are those who say, "We believe in Allah and the Last Day," but they are not believers. They deceive Allah and those who believe, but they deceive only themselves, and they do not perceive. In their hearts is a disease, so Allah increased their disease, and for them is a painful punishment because they used to lie.﴾ (8-10)

In this is evidence that the conjunction here conveys the coordination of one attribute upon another, not of one group upon another. Similarly is the conjunction in His saying: ﴿And those who had already settled the abode and faith...﴾ (9) [Al-Hashr]. Here "the abode" means al-Madinah, and likewise "the faith" is also meant to refer to al-Madinah.

The meaning of ﴿al-Murjifun﴾ (60) [Al-Ahzab] is from irjaf, which is a violent tremor that shakes. From it is His saying: ﴿On the Day when the Quaking will quake, followed by the Following.﴾ [An-Nazi'at] (6-7). So the agitators are those who try to shake what is firm and undermine what is stable. Likewise, whenever the hypocrites saw strength in Islam, they tried to shake and disturb it in order to weaken it and destroy it.

These are the ones we call in modern political language "the fifth column" (at-tabur al-khamis), the group that spreads rumours and broadcasts falsehoods that weaken the general current and threaten its stability.

The hypocrites often sat saying: "The tribe of so-and-so and the tribe of so-and-so have gathered to attack al-Madinah and to destroy Muhammad and his message." Their aim in these rumours was to weaken and defeat the morale of the new Muslims and the weak among them.

Even at the level of individuals, they would go to someone who was thinking about Islam, or whom they saw was inclined towards it, and say to him: "Did you not know that so-and-so's tribe seized him, or his master took him and tortured him to death because he followed Muhammad?" All this to turn people away from the religion of Allah.

So the agitator (al-murjif) means the one who walks about spreading sedition and falsehoods in order to turn the people of truth away from their truth through the slander and falsehoods he disseminates.

Therefore Allah, the Exalted, threatens them: "If these hypocrites do not desist from agitating in al-Madinah and misleading the people, then We will surely have a different affair with them." This was a time of truce and covenant between the Muslims and the Jews and their hypocrite associates. It is as if Allah, the Exalted, is saying: "We have been silent about their crimes until the strength of Islam grew. Now that Islam has become strong, if they break their covenant with us, we will confront them."

And it is strange that these agitators should think that Allah does not know their falsehoods, nor does His Messenger. Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Or do those in whose hearts is a disease think that Allah will not bring forth their malice? And had We willed, We would have shown them to you, and you would have recognized them by their marks; and you will surely know them by the tone of their speech. And Allah knows your deeds.﴾ [Muhammad] (29-30)

The meaning of "the tone of speech" (lahn al-qawl) is that they turn words away from their meaning. Among this is their saying to the greeting of the Messenger of Allah: "as-sam ʿalaykum" (death be upon you), where as-sam means death. Likewise they twisted their tongues with the word "ra'ina" (our shepherd, or "pay attention to us"), saying "ra'una," intending foolishness (ruʿuna).

More strange than that is what the Qur'an related of them: ﴿And they say to themselves, "Why does Allah not punish us for what we say?"﴾ [Al-Mujadilah] (8).

This statement of theirs is evidence of their stupidity. First: because they wish for punishment. Second: because they said it to themselves and did not say it to people, nor even to one another, for "they say" is plural and "to themselves" is plural, as if each of them was saying it to himself.

So: did none of them ask himself: "Who informed the Messenger of Allah of what is in my soul?" Does this not show that Muhammad is connected to his Lord, and that He will surely expose them and reveal what their breasts conceal? So this is their stupidity.

And whoever examines the history of the Jews and the hypocrites in al-Madinah finds that Islam did not seize them unawares. Rather, it gave them a covenant, granted them security, and widened for them in dwelling and livelihood as long as they did not harm the Muslims. But it reached the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, that they were conspiring in sin and aggression, so he sent for them and forbade them from secret conspiring in sin and aggression. But they returned once again, as

The accursed (al-mal'un): one expelled from the mercy of God; or, they were expelled from Medina after God exposed the inner depths of their wicked souls. For this reason the Messenger of God expelled them from the mosque, because in their wickedness and baseness they used to enter the mosque, and even pray in the first row, thinking that this would conceal their hypocrisy.

But the Messenger of God used to expel them by name: "O so-and-so, O so-and-so." (1) He, may God's blessings and peace be upon him, knew them. And why would he not, when God had said to him: ﴿And if We willed, We would have shown them to you, and you would have recognized them by their marks...﴾ (Muhammad: 30).

The meaning of ﴿wherever they are found﴾ (al-Ahzab: 61) is: wherever they are found. ﴿They are seized﴾ (al-Ahzab: 61) means: they are captured. ﴿And killed with [repeated] killing﴾ (al-Ahzab: 61). Note the intensification in ﴿killed﴾ (al-Ahzab: 61) and the emphasis in ﴿killing﴾ (al-Ahzab: 61), meaning: kill them violently, and let no mercy towards them take hold of you, as a recompense for what they committed against Islam and the Muslims.

Because the hypocrite who has been stamped with hypocrisy, his nature becomes poisoned and polluted and never becomes pure. Hypocrisy is in his blood and accompanies him wherever he goes, and his affair must inevitably end in expulsion from whatever place he settles in.

Therefore, although God Almighty has scattered them across the earth as nations, each fragment of them in some land has a cohesion among themselves, such that they do not dissolve into other societies, so that they remain with special places known by them. In every country there is known a "Jewish quarter." But people must inevitably discover their scandals, and their affair ends with their expulsion and annihilation. The most recent expulsion of them, for example, was what happened in Germany.

And God spoke truly when He said about them: ﴿And [recall] when your Lord declared that He would surely send against them until the Day of Resurrection those who would afflict them with a terrible punishment﴾ (al-A'raf: 167).

1. Al-Qurtubi cited in his tafsir (8/5515) that when Surat "Bara'ah" was revealed, they were gathered, and the Prophet, may God's blessings and peace be upon him, said: "O so-and-so, stand up and go out, for you are a hypocrite, and O so-and-so, stand up." So their Muslim brothers stood up and took charge of expelling them from the mosque. See also (Zad al-Masir) by Ibn al-Jawzi (3/492).

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿The way of Allah concerning those who passed away before, and you will not find any change in the way of Allah.﴾ (33:62)

After Allah, the Truth, glory be to Him, had shown the end of His enemies by slaying them and the victory of His Messenger ﷺ, He clarified that this is nothing new in the procession of the messages. Rather, it is an established and recurring custom (sunnah). Have you seen, in the procession of the messages, a messenger whom Allah sent and then abandoned or forsook, and whose affair ended with his enemies being victorious over him?

As-sunnah (the custom, way): it is the natural, innate method that recurs and never fails. Thus, if a matter happens once or twice, it is not called a sunnah; the sunnah, then, has regularity and continuity.

Therefore, what is meant by sunnah here is the triumph of the truth over falsehood. ﴿Concerning those who passed away…﴾ (33:62), that is, those who went on from the earlier nations. The sunnah of Allah in granting victory to the truth remains in force and will continue until the Hour arrives, because it is a sunnah.

﴿And you will not find any change in the way of Allah.﴾ (33:62) Indeed, it does not change or alter, because it is the sunnah of whom? The sunnah of Allah. Allah, glory be to Him, has no equal, and no partner who could alter it or add to His judgment with anything.

After that, the Truth, glory be to Him, wished to inform us that the method which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ brought from his Lord, containing His commands, His prohibitions, and the ways of deliverance from adversaries, must be respected, because it will bring all people to another life in which they will be received, a reception in which nothing will benefit them except their deeds.

It is another life in which they live with the Causer (al-Musabbib), glory be to Him, not with the causes (al-asbab). So beware lest you think that Allah created you, provided for you, and bestowed His blessings upon you in this world, and the matter ended, and that whoever departed from His method escaped His punishment. Nay, remember always that you will return to Him, and you will not escape from His hand.

The Messenger of Allah was asked often about the Hour. Questioning is a healthy phenomenon when it concerns matters of legal obligation (taklif), because asking about the religious obligations is evidence that the questioner believed in the Messenger of Allah and loved to be bound by obligations, so he wished to build the movement of his life on Islamic foundations from the start.

Suppose that Islam came upon things that had been inherited from the Jahiliyyah (the pre-Islamic period) and that Islam confirmed them; then someone comes to ask what Islam's view of them is, out of eagerness to preserve the soundness of his religion and the movement of his life.

But Allah the Exalted wanted to make matters easy for people, so He said:

﴿O you who believe, do not ask about things which, if they were disclosed to you, would trouble you...﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 101].

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Leave me as I have left you, for those before you were destroyed by their much questioning and their disputing with their prophets" (1).

So the questioning that is required is questioning about the legal matters that concern the Muslim, even if they are from the affairs of the Jahiliyyah, and Islam has confirmed many of them. Thus the diyah (blood-money), for instance, came into Islam from roots that existed among the people of the Jahiliyyah, and Islam confirmed it. Allah the Exalted commanded the Muslim to ask about such matters in His saying:

﴿So ask the people of the reminder, if you do not know﴾ [An-Nahl: 43].

As for asking about the Hour: the Hour is an unseen matter that no one knows except Allah, so it is a question with no benefit. Therefore, when the Messenger of Allah was asked, "When is the Hour?", he said to the questioner: "What have you prepared for it?" (2), directing him to what he should ask about and be concerned with.

This noble verse ﴿They ask you about the Hour...﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 63] came after the battle of harm against Allah, and harm against His Messenger and the believers in him. This harm came from those who do not believe in the heavens, do not believe in Allah, and do not believe in the conveying of the message from Allah through His Messenger.

Their harm to Allah is, in reality, harm to themselves, because it does not reach Allah, and Allah wants good for them, since they are His servants and His creation. When they depart from His method, they only harm themselves. As for their harm to the Messenger of Allah, they harmed him (ﷺ) in his family and in his person. They confronted him (ﷺ) with what any noble person would disdain, harming him by word and by deed, yet he (ﷺ) endured, and his companions endured, and they were harmed in their persons and their wealth.

The one who reflects finds that this harm is intended and has a philosophy. Allah willed it in order to test the believers and to see, while He is most knowing, who stands firm in faith. Therefore He said:

﴿Do people think that they will be left to say, "We believe," and they will not be tested?﴾ [Al-Ankabut: 2].

We have already explained that faith is not a word that is said; rather, faith is responsibility and action. For this reason the Meccan disbelievers refrained from uttering the word of faith, because they knew its reality, and they were people of faith and understanding of styles and meanings.

The steadfastness of our master, the Messenger of Allah, and his patience, together with those who believed with him, is evidence that they made a comparison between this harm in this world from a human being of limited power, and the harm of Allah the Exalted in the Hereafter, a harm that befits His power, from which no one can flee.

So we say: harm has an intended philosophy. Otherwise, Allah could have seized the enemies of His religion with the seizure of the Mighty, the Omnipotent, as He seized the people of Noah with the flood, the people of Pharaoh with drowning, and as He caused the earth to swallow Qarun. But He willed to punish these people by the hands of the believers and by the hand of the Messenger of Allah. And perhaps, had a general seizure descended upon them, they would have said: a cosmic sign, like earthquakes and volcanoes, for example. Therefore He said, addressing the believers:

﴿Fight them; Allah will punish them by your hands and will disgrace them and give you victory over them...﴾ [At-Tawbah: 14].

Then the Exalted Lord comforts His Prophet and consoles him:

﴿So whether We show you some of what We promise them or We take you in death, to Us they will be returned﴾ [Ghafir: 77].

So the response of the Exalted Lord to this harm came in two kinds: one in this world, that Allah gives His Prophet victory over them, as Allah gave him good news in His saying:

﴿The multitude will be defeated and they will turn their backs﴾ [Al-Qamar: 45].

And the other is a response in the Hereafter on the Day of Resurrection. Therefore He said:

﴿They ask you about the Hour...﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 63].

The question that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked was directed toward two matters. The first is related to i'jaz (inimitability), because they knew from their scriptures and their prophets some matters, and they wished to embarrass the Messenger by asking him about them, but they found no answer. They knew that the Messenger of Allah was ummi (unlettered), who could neither read nor write, and had never sat with a teacher. Yet the Exalted Lord would assist His Messenger and teach him the answer, so he would give them the correct answer, and they would die of rage, and they would dispute any matter in order to establish for themselves that Muhammad did not know it.

For example, their question about the People of the Cave: how long did they remain? Allah answered them:

﴿And they remained in their cave three hundred years and exceeded by nine﴾ [Al-Kahf: 25]. They said: we know it is three hundred; where is this addition from? They were ignorant that the timing of divine rites in the religion rests upon the lunar calendar, not on the movement of the sun, because what the sun gives us is that we know by it the beginning and end of the day, but we do not know by it the beginning or end of the month.

As for the Arabic lunar timing, it has a distinctive sign: the appearance of the crescent at the beginning of the month. If you compare the lunar calendar with the Gregorian calendar, you will find that each Hijri year is eleven days shorter than the solar year, so three hundred Gregorian years equal three hundred and nine Hijri years.

It was as if they wished to make Muhammad appear ignorant, so Allah alerted them that they themselves were the ignorant ones. It is strange that the Jews object to this timing, although it is the worship timing of our master Musa (peace be upon him). Did He not say:

﴿And We appointed for Musa thirty nights and completed them with ten, so the appointed time of his Lord was complete...﴾ [Al-A'raf: 142].

So His saying ﴿and exceeded by nine﴾ [Al-Kahf: 25] contains an eloquent inimitability of expression, indicating that the nine years came as an addition from within the three hundred, and not outside of them.

Then they asked him about a wandering man, and Allah revealed: ﴿And they ask you about Dhul-Qarnayn...﴾ [Al-Kahf: 83].

It should have drawn their attention to the truthfulness of Muhammad (ﷺ), and they should have asked themselves: from where does he have this knowledge, being the unlettered one who never once sat with a teacher?

Therefore we say: illiteracy is a defect for every person, except that for the Messenger of Allah in particular it was a nobility and a distinction, because in regard to the Messenger of Allah it means that no human taught him, as they accused him, rather his Lord taught him.

Likewise, the nation in which the Qur'an was revealed was an unlettered nation, and this too is a nobility for it. Had this nation been a nation of knowledge and culture, they would have said about Islam that it is a civilizational leap. But it was an unlettered nation, dominated by the tribal system: every tribe had its law and its order, and every tribe had its chief. Yet from among them came one who brought a system that rejects compromise for the politics of the whole world until the Hour is established, and this could not be achieved except by a divine method.

So the illiteracy of the Arabs is a nobility, and their inability to imitate the Qur'an and to produce its like is also a nobility for them. That Allah the Exalted challenges them with the style of the Qur'an is evidence of their greatness in this field; otherwise, you do not challenge the weak, but you challenge the strong in the domain of challenge. So Allah's challenge to the Arabs is, as it were, a testimony from Him that they were the most eloquent of creation, and therefore He brought them a miracle of the same kind in which they excelled.

Then the Jews ask the Messenger of Allah about the Hour: ﴿They ask you about the Hour...﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 63]. They are asking about the Hour, meaning the Day of Resurrection, because they deny it, and it is in their interest that this day should not happen, so that they do not stand in the position of being questioned and held to account for what they committed in the world of oppression, polytheism, tyranny, shedding of blood, and vain talk about people's honor.

If these people examined the question of the Resurrection and the reckoning by reason rather than by the texts of the Qur'an, they would find that it is a logical matter that must occur. For example, we lived through the Communist Party in Russia in 1917, and we saw how they seized the feudal lords and the capitalists, tortured them, did to them terrible deeds, and confiscated their property as a recompense for their oppression of people. We used to say to them: yes, it is logical that you should take retribution from the oppressor. But what about the many oppressors who died, or whom you did not reach, and who escaped your grip?

By Allah, if a person came and pointed you to the place of one of those oppressors, would you not thank him for this help? So what if he said: rather, I will bring him and hold him to account and take retribution from him; is this not a help to you in the task of avenging yourselves on the oppressors?

Therefore we say: the Communists should have been the first of people to believe in the Day of Resurrection, the resurrection and the reckoning, so that they might overtake those who escaped their hands.

Another matter: do you not, in any of your man-made systems, place organized laws? What is the meaning of law? Law is rules that define for the citizen what is his and what is upon him. Does not your law contain the principle of reward for the good-doer and punishment for the negligent?

So every society must have elements that step outside its order and deserve punishment. Whoever is able to deceive society and conceal his crime, what is his share of punishment, when his corruption has spread and his oppression has multiplied?

Therefore we must believe in another power that nothing is hidden from, that no one can deceive, and that no one can escape. A power that knows the hidden things, exposes them, and holds their owners to account. This matter must lead you to the natural (fitrah) faith in Allah the Exalted, and that He is the All-Aware, the All-Knowing: ﴿And not a leaf falls but He knows it, nor a grain in the darknesses of the earth, nor anything fresh or dry but that it is in a clear record﴾ [Al-An'am: 59].

Why then do you deny the Resurrection, while in your worldly systems you mobilize spies and intelligence services and count the whispers of people in order to know those who scheme so that the law does not see them? Is it not among the grace of Allah upon you that He knows what is hidden from you and takes retribution for you against your opponents?

The matter of the Resurrection and the reckoning is clear by nature. Therefore you find that those who deny it are those who have been wasteful toward themselves and fear what awaits them of punishment on that Day, and they have nothing but to deny it and not acknowledge it, as if this flight were the solution.

Surah al-Kahf gives us a model of these people: the owner of the garden who said: ﴿And I do not think the Hour will ever occur﴾ [Al-Kahf: 36], after he had been wasteful toward himself and denied the blessing of Allah upon him. When he came to his senses and reconsidered his nature, he said: ﴿And if I should be returned to my Lord, I will surely find better than this as a destination﴾ [Al-Kahf: 36].

So denial of the Day of Resurrection is the more prevalent, more emphatic position, and the doubt in ﴿And if I should be returned to my Lord...﴾ [Al-Kahf: 36] means: even supposing I am returned to my Lord on the Day of Resurrection, I will have with Him something better than what He gave me in this world; just as He honored me here, He will honor me there.

This is a mistaken belief and a foolish understanding, for Allah the Exalted honors in the Hereafter only the one who has honored himself by following His method in this world, and whoever does not honor himself here by Allah's method, Allah will not honor him in the Hereafter.

Therefore we often hear: "I prayed and was not answered," especially from women. One of them came to me complaining that she had turned to Allah in supplication, yet her daughter did not marry, the son is such-and-such, and the husband is such-and-such. I used to say to her: "May your goodness be increased" (kutr khayrik) — first, that you know you have a Lord to whom you turn in time of hardship, as Allah the Exalted said:

﴿So why, when Our punishment came to them, did they not humble themselves?﴾ [Al-An'am: 43].

But I ask you: did you first answer Allah in what He asked of you, so that you could expect Him to answer what you asked? Did you answer Allah in this hair of yours? Did you answer Allah in your (lips) and your alteration of the creation of Allah? Then she would find no answer, except to say: "Wal..."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 33, verses 64–65:

"La'anahum" means: He expelled them from His mercy, may He be exalted, and removed them far away, that is, in this world. "And He has prepared for them a blazing fire" [al-Ahzab: 64], meaning a fire that flares, blazes and glows. This is in the Hereafter, on the day of which Allah said: "The day We say to Hell, 'Are you filled?' and it says, 'Is there any more?'" [Qaf: 30].

This blazing fire is lasting and permanent, never ending: "Abiding therein forever..." [al-Ahzab: 65]. We have heard some scholars say concerning eternity (al-abadiyyah) that it is mentioned in every verse that speaks of the bliss of Paradise, but it is not mentioned in the punishment of the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection.

The one who holds this view has not carefully surveyed the Book of Allah, for this expression, "abiding therein forever..." [al-Ahzab: 65], is mentioned in two places: one of them is this one we are dealing with, and the other is in Surah al-Jinn, in His saying, glory be to Him: "And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger, then indeed for him is the fire of Hell, abiding therein forever" [al-Jinn: 23].

This is one of the manifestations of the mercy of Allah, may He be exalted, toward His servants: that the word of eternity (al-ta'bid) comes in every verse about Paradise, and does not come except in two places concerning the people of the Fire. That is because the mercy of Allah precedes His wrath, and so this requires that He give the believers good news of the eternity and perpetuity of bliss.

As for the recompense of the disbelievers, He says: "Abiding therein..." [al-Ahzab: 65] and does not mention the word of eternity, perhaps so that this softens the hearts of these people and inclines them to the path of the Compassionate One who is merciful to them.

The mention of the word of eternity in these two verses is only to affirm and establish the principle, and it is among His mercy, may He be exalted, that His mercy precedes in the good news and is gentle in the warning.

So this divine wisdom is intended, and it bore its desired fruits. It became a gateway to the faith of many disbelievers. We have previously mentioned the story of our master Ibrahim (peace be upon him), when a guest came and knocked on his door, and he asked him about his religion. When he learned that he was not a believer, he closed the door in his face, and the man departed. But swiftly Allah rebuked His Prophet Ibrahim for that and said to him: "O Ibrahim, I have sustained him throughout his life in My dominion while he disbelieves in Me; would you want him to change his religion on a night in which you host him?"

So Ibrahim (peace be upon him) hurried until he caught up with the man and brought him back to his hospitality. The man said: "Did you not turn me away from your door a little while ago?" He said: "Yes, but my Lord rebuked me concerning you." He said: "What a Lord, a Lord who rebukes His friends concerning His enemies! I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and that you are the Messenger of Allah."

As for them, in their abiding in the Fire, "they will find for themselves no protector and no helper" [al-Ahzab: 65], meaning: no master who takes charge of their affair, "nor any helper" [al-Ahzab: 65] who gives them victory or defends them.
