Having mentioned the eternal abode that awaits the disbelievers in the Fire, Allah, glorified is He, now describes the state they will be in within it: ﴿The Day their faces are turned over in the Fire...﴾ [al-Ahzab: 66]. At-taqlib (turning over) means changing a matter and shifting it from one state to another. Among its uses is His saying: ﴿Let not the movement of those who disbelieve through the land deceive you. It is a brief enjoyment; then their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the resting place﴾ [Al 'Imran: 196-197].

That is, their journeys and their activity in the trade movement between al-Sham and Yemen, and the wealth and riches that result from this movement.

So His saying ﴿The Day their faces are turned over in the Fire...﴾ [al-Ahzab: 66] means that the angels turn them over. Whenever one side is cooked, they turn them onto the other side, just as we turn the skewer of kebab over the fire so that all of it is exposed, and it is cooked completely.

He singled out the face because it is the mark by which a person is recognised, and it is the most noble and honoured of his limbs. From it come the words wijahah (distinction) and wajih (distinguished), and all of these indicate nobility. And since it is the most noble of the limbs, all the other limbs protect it and defend it. We have said before: if a car sped past you and splattered your clothes and face with mud, for example, what would you do? First, you would attend to your face and remove the harm that has reached it, and then you would turn to your clothes.

To know the importance and station of the face, read His saying: ﴿Is one who shields his face from the terrible punishment on the Day of Resurrection...﴾ [al-Zumar: 24]. Because of the severity of the punishment, he shields himself with his face, which is the most noble of his limbs.

Or: the meaning of turning over is from one punishment to another. Allah, glorified is He, has given us several depictions of the faces of the disbelievers in the Fire, and we seek refuge with Allah. He said once: ﴿You will see those who lied about Allah with their faces blackened...﴾ [al-Zumar: 60].

He said: ﴿And faces that Day will be dust-covered, overcast by darkness. Those are the disbelievers, the wicked﴾ [Abasa: 40-42].

And He said: ﴿And faces that Day will be bright, looking toward their Lord. And faces that Day will be scowling, thinking that a calamity is about to be inflicted on them﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 24-25].

Thus the face here does not take one form; rather it takes various colours and different conditions, indicating the variety of the torment and pain they undergo. The face is the first evidence of its owner, and the translator of what is within him. When your companion changes toward you, for example, you notice it on his face, and you say: What is the matter with you, that your face has changed toward me? Or: why has your face turned away from me?

And these people, while their faces are being turned over in the Fire, say: ﴿Oh, would that we had obeyed Allah and obeyed the Messenger!﴾ [al-Ahzab: 66]. These are the ones who, only yesterday, used to harm Allah, harm the Messenger, and harm the believers.

The phrase ﴿Oh, would that...﴾ [al-Ahzab: 66] (ya layta) is an expression of wishing, a kind of request to which the soul is attached and which it desires. But it is far-fetched, for it usually occurs with the impossible and the unattainable, as in the words of the poet:

Ah, would that youth might return one day, so that I could tell it what old age has done.

And the words of another:

Would that the stars would draw near to me, so that I might string them into a necklace of praise; for I am not content with a wound for you.

Youth does not return, and the stars do not draw near to anyone, but these are the wishes of the soul. Likewise, these people wish that they had obeyed Allah and obeyed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), but it is far-fetched that this would benefit them, for the time has passed.

Then Allah, glorified is He, mentions the opposite: they did not obey Allah and did not obey the Messenger, but their argument is:

﴿And they will say: Our Lord, we obeyed our leaders and our elders...﴾ [al-Ahzab: 67].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 33, verse 67–68:

Al-sadah (the masters): the plural of sayyid, who is the one who commands and executes over others, and no one contests him. Al-kubara' (the elders/notables) are those who take positions among their people in proportion to the services they render to them. The master or chief of a people does not attain this station from nothing; it comes from gifts and capabilities that qualify him for it. Therefore he feels no discomfort when people say to him, "O my master," because he has paid the price of this mastery, and this is the true master.

Mastery may also be taken by force, tyranny and coercion, without the master offering anything by which he leads his people. This is a theft of mastery that people hate. Therefore the Islamic law (al-shar' al-islami) did not overlook this true mastery, nor did it overlook people's standing and status. It valued all of that in financial terms in a partnership it called shirkat al-wujuh (the partnership of reputations): your capital in the partnership is wealth, and your capital is your standing, the people's love for you, and your position in society.

People love the true mastery that its holder has taken rightfully, because they gain its benefit and profit from it, unlike the stolen mastery that its holder seized by force, from which they gain nothing; rather, it is a mastery that harms them and devours their goods.

Therefore we have said regarding servitude ('ubudiyyah): it is a word we dislike if it is the servitude of one human to another human, because it is a servitude that gives the servant's good to his master. Rather, all honour lies in servitude being to Allah, the Exalted, where the servant takes the good of his Master.

Consider how servitude was a nobility and honour for our master, the Messenger of Allah, when his Lord addressed him saying: ﴿Glory be to Him who took His servant by night from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque...﴾ [al-Isra': 1]. It was the servitude of Muhammad to Allah that brought him to this station, which no human other than him has attained.

The poet spoke truly when he said:

Enough for my self honour that I am a servant, whom a Lord welcomes me without appointments

He is in His holy, most mighty sanctuary, but I meet whenever and wherever I love

So if you want to meet your Lord, the matter is in your hand: you determine the place of the meeting, its time and its subject, in the street, in the house, at work, in the mosque. Merely by performing ablution and saying "Allahu akbar" you are in the presence of your Lord. Then you are the one who ends the meeting if you wish, and your Lord, Mighty and Majestic, does not tire until you tire. So what honour is greater than this?

Whereas if you wish to meet a president, for example, or a minister, there are obstacles and difficulties before this meeting, and you have no say in the matter of this meeting; rather, he sets for you the time and the place, even what you say, and he is the one who ends the meeting.

You, in your servitude to Allah, the Exalted, your Lord is the one who calls you into His presence, and He becomes angry if He calls you and you do not respond. How excellent a Lord is your Lord, and how excellent is your servitude to Him, glory be to Him.

Here the disbelievers will blame their masters and elders: ﴿Indeed we obeyed our masters and our elders, and they led us astray from the way.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 67] They wish to take revenge on them and to relieve themselves by seeing them in punishment, in return for what they brought them into polytheism and made disobedience attractive to them.

So they say: ﴿Our Lord, give them double the punishment...﴾ [al-Ahzab: 68], i.e., a doubled punishment, because their misguidance was likewise doubled: they went astray themselves and led others astray.

In another place the Qur'an relates to us the words of the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿Our Lord, show us those who misled us of the jinn and humankind, that we may place them under our feet so that they will be among the lowest.﴾ [Fussilat: 29].

In many verses the Qur'an relates to us dialogues among the disbelievers, in which each of them places the blame on the other, as it recounts of Iblis saying: ﴿And I had no authority over you except that I invited you, and you responded to me. So do not blame me; blame yourselves. I cannot help you, nor can you help me. Indeed, I deny your associating me with Allah before. Indeed, for the wrongdoers is a painful punishment.﴾ [Ibrahim: 22].

They were not content with doubling the punishment for their masters; they also asked for a curse upon them, a great curse: ﴿and curse them with a great curse﴾ [al-Ahzab: 68]. The curse is for their having gone astray in their own selves, and it should be great because they led others astray.

We note here that every call to the Lord, blessed and exalted, comes always without the particle of calling. Why? They said: because calling has particles that differ according to the distance between you and the one called, and calling is a request for attention. If the one called is beside you, you say: "Muhammad, do such-and-such." If he is far from you, you say: "Amuhammad" (a-Muhammad). Farther than that: "Ya Muhammad." And farther still: "Aya Muhammad." These particles are built on the lengthening of the voice according to the distance.

So: what do you say when you call your Lord, even if you are not near to Allah, while Allah is near to you? Do not use the particle of calling, neither for the near nor for the far. Therefore the word (Rabb) as a vocative appears in the Qur'an in sixty-five verses without a particle of calling. The first of them is the words of our master Ibrahim, peace be upon him: ﴿My Lord, make this a secure city...﴾ [al-Baqarah: 126].

Up to the words of Nuh, peace be upon him: ﴿My Lord, forgive me and my parents and whoever enters my house as a believer, and the believing men and believing women...﴾ [Nuh: 28].

Sufficient for this nearness is the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And We have certainly created man, and We know what his soul whispers to him, and We are closer to him than his jugular vein.﴾ [Qaf: 16].

Therefore, when our master the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was asked: "Is our Lord near that we may confide in Him, or far that we should call out to Him?" Allah revealed: ﴿And when My servants ask you concerning Me, indeed I am near...﴾ [al-Baqarah: 186].

So: Allah, the Exalted, is near to us in actuality, and if distance occurs afterwards, it is from you, and a servant is at his nearest to Allah most often when he is compelled, even if he was far from Allah before the compulsion.

In only two verses of the Book of Allah is the Lord, blessed and exalted, called with the particle (Ya). The first: ﴿And the Messenger said, "My Lord, indeed my people have taken this Qur'an as abandoned."﴾ [al-Furqan: 30].

The other: ﴿And [He has knowledge of] his saying, "My Lord, indeed these are a people who will not believe."﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 88].

These two places are a recounting of the speech of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. So why did the particle of calling come only from Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in calling his Lord?

They said: because the Messenger of Allah was extremely eager for the guidance of his people and the support of his call, to the point that his Lord addressed him saying: ﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself through grief that they will not be believers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 3].

The Messenger of Allah passed through difficult situations to the degree that he became impatient for the help of Allah. Allah revealed to him: ﴿Indeed, We will surely support Our messengers and those who believe in the worldly life...﴾ [Ghafir: 51], yet the Messenger of Allah and those who believed with him were shaken, as He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿and they were shaken until the Messenger and those who believed with him said, "When is the help of Allah?"...﴾ [al-Baqarah: 214]. So he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, feared that he had become distant from his Lord, and this distance was nothing but a suspicion on the part of the Messenger, or an accusation against the self.

When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went to supplicate to his Lord and complain to Him that his people had abandoned the Qur'an, he called his Lord from the station of the distant, saying: "Ya Rabb" (O Lord). It was as though he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, thought within himself that there was shortcoming or failure in his mission and saw that this distanced him from his Lord. But his Lord did him justice and confirmed his call, and even swore by it, so the Truthful, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And [He has knowledge of] his saying, "My Lord, indeed these are a people who will not believe." So turn away from them and say, "Peace." But they are going to know.﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 88-89].

That is: He swore by your saying, O Muhammad: ﴿My Lord, indeed my people have taken this Qur'an as abandoned.﴾ [al-Furqan: 30]. The Truthful, glory be to Him, swears by what He wills, over what He wills: He swears by the angels and by inanimate things, He swears by plants. But the Truthful, glory be to Him and exalted, has sworn by none of creation except the Messenger of Allah, in His saying: ﴿By your life, [O Muhammad], indeed, they were, in their intoxication, wandering blindly.﴾ [al-Hijr: 72].

That is: "by your long life" (ta'mirak), or "by your life, O Muhammad."

And just as He, glory be to Him, swore by the life of His prophet Muhammad, He swore by his saying, so He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And [He has knowledge of] his saying, "My Lord, indeed these are a people who will not believe."﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 88].

Then the Truthful, glory be to Him, addresses His believing servants, saying, exalted is He:

﴿O you who have believed, do not be like those who abused Musa...﴾.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 33, verse 67–68:

Al-sadah (the masters): the plural of sayyid, who is the one who commands and executes over others, and no one contests him. Al-kubara' (the elders/notables) are those who take positions among their people in proportion to the services they render to them. The master or chief of a people does not attain this station from nothing; it comes from gifts and capabilities that qualify him for it. Therefore he feels no discomfort when people say to him, "O my master," because he has paid the price of this mastery, and this is the true master.

Mastery may also be taken by force, tyranny and coercion, without the master offering anything by which he leads his people. This is a theft of mastery that people hate. Therefore the Islamic law (al-shar' al-islami) did not overlook this true mastery, nor did it overlook people's standing and status. It valued all of that in financial terms in a partnership it called shirkat al-wujuh (the partnership of reputations): your capital in the partnership is wealth, and your capital is your standing, the people's love for you, and your position in society.

People love the true mastery that its holder has taken rightfully, because they gain its benefit and profit from it, unlike the stolen mastery that its holder seized by force, from which they gain nothing; rather, it is a mastery that harms them and devours their goods.

Therefore we have said regarding servitude ('ubudiyyah): it is a word we dislike if it is the servitude of one human to another human, because it is a servitude that gives the servant's good to his master. Rather, all honour lies in servitude being to Allah, the Exalted, where the servant takes the good of his Master.

Consider how servitude was a nobility and honour for our master, the Messenger of Allah, when his Lord addressed him saying: ﴿Glory be to Him who took His servant by night from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque...﴾ [al-Isra': 1]. It was the servitude of Muhammad to Allah that brought him to this station, which no human other than him has attained.

The poet spoke truly when he said:

Enough for my self honour that I am a servant, whom a Lord welcomes me without appointments

He is in His holy, most mighty sanctuary, but I meet whenever and wherever I love

So if you want to meet your Lord, the matter is in your hand: you determine the place of the meeting, its time and its subject, in the street, in the house, at work, in the mosque. Merely by performing ablution and saying "Allahu akbar" you are in the presence of your Lord. Then you are the one who ends the meeting if you wish, and your Lord, Mighty and Majestic, does not tire until you tire. So what honour is greater than this?

Whereas if you wish to meet a president, for example, or a minister, there are obstacles and difficulties before this meeting, and you have no say in the matter of this meeting; rather, he sets for you the time and the place, even what you say, and he is the one who ends the meeting.

You, in your servitude to Allah, the Exalted, your Lord is the one who calls you into His presence, and He becomes angry if He calls you and you do not respond. How excellent a Lord is your Lord, and how excellent is your servitude to Him, glory be to Him.

Here the disbelievers will blame their masters and elders: ﴿Indeed we obeyed our masters and our elders, and they led us astray from the way.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 67] They wish to take revenge on them and to relieve themselves by seeing them in punishment, in return for what they brought them into polytheism and made disobedience attractive to them.

So they say: ﴿Our Lord, give them double the punishment...﴾ [al-Ahzab: 68], i.e., a doubled punishment, because their misguidance was likewise doubled: they went astray themselves and led others astray.

In another place the Qur'an relates to us the words of the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿Our Lord, show us those who misled us of the jinn and humankind, that we may place them under our feet so that they will be among the lowest.﴾ [Fussilat: 29].

In many verses the Qur'an relates to us dialogues among the disbelievers, in which each of them places the blame on the other, as it recounts of Iblis saying: ﴿And I had no authority over you except that I invited you, and you responded to me. So do not blame me; blame yourselves. I cannot help you, nor can you help me. Indeed, I deny your associating me with Allah before. Indeed, for the wrongdoers is a painful punishment.﴾ [Ibrahim: 22].

They were not content with doubling the punishment for their masters; they also asked for a curse upon them, a great curse: ﴿and curse them with a great curse﴾ [al-Ahzab: 68]. The curse is for their having gone astray in their own selves, and it should be great because they led others astray.

We note here that every call to the Lord, blessed and exalted, comes always without the particle of calling. Why? They said: because calling has particles that differ according to the distance between you and the one called, and calling is a request for attention. If the one called is beside you, you say: "Muhammad, do such-and-such." If he is far from you, you say: "Amuhammad" (a-Muhammad). Farther than that: "Ya Muhammad." And farther still: "Aya Muhammad." These particles are built on the lengthening of the voice according to the distance.

So: what do you say when you call your Lord, even if you are not near to Allah, while Allah is near to you? Do not use the particle of calling, neither for the near nor for the far. Therefore the word (Rabb) as a vocative appears in the Qur'an in sixty-five verses without a particle of calling. The first of them is the words of our master Ibrahim, peace be upon him: ﴿My Lord, make this a secure city...﴾ [al-Baqarah: 126].

Up to the words of Nuh, peace be upon him: ﴿My Lord, forgive me and my parents and whoever enters my house as a believer, and the believing men and believing women...﴾ [Nuh: 28].

Sufficient for this nearness is the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And We have certainly created man, and We know what his soul whispers to him, and We are closer to him than his jugular vein.﴾ [Qaf: 16].

Therefore, when our master the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was asked: "Is our Lord near that we may confide in Him, or far that we should call out to Him?" Allah revealed: ﴿And when My servants ask you concerning Me, indeed I am near...﴾ [al-Baqarah: 186].

So: Allah, the Exalted, is near to us in actuality, and if distance occurs afterwards, it is from you, and a servant is at his nearest to Allah most often when he is compelled, even if he was far from Allah before the compulsion.

In only two verses of the Book of Allah is the Lord, blessed and exalted, called with the particle (Ya). The first: ﴿And the Messenger said, "My Lord, indeed my people have taken this Qur'an as abandoned."﴾ [al-Furqan: 30].

The other: ﴿And [He has knowledge of] his saying, "My Lord, indeed these are a people who will not believe."﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 88].

These two places are a recounting of the speech of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. So why did the particle of calling come only from Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in calling his Lord?

They said: because the Messenger of Allah was extremely eager for the guidance of his people and the support of his call, to the point that his Lord addressed him saying: ﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself through grief that they will not be believers.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 3].

The Messenger of Allah passed through difficult situations to the degree that he became impatient for the help of Allah. Allah revealed to him: ﴿Indeed, We will surely support Our messengers and those who believe in the worldly life...﴾ [Ghafir: 51], yet the Messenger of Allah and those who believed with him were shaken, as He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿and they were shaken until the Messenger and those who believed with him said, "When is the help of Allah?"...﴾ [al-Baqarah: 214]. So he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, feared that he had become distant from his Lord, and this distance was nothing but a suspicion on the part of the Messenger, or an accusation against the self.

When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went to supplicate to his Lord and complain to Him that his people had abandoned the Qur'an, he called his Lord from the station of the distant, saying: "Ya Rabb" (O Lord). It was as though he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, thought within himself that there was shortcoming or failure in his mission and saw that this distanced him from his Lord. But his Lord did him justice and confirmed his call, and even swore by it, so the Truthful, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And [He has knowledge of] his saying, "My Lord, indeed these are a people who will not believe." So turn away from them and say, "Peace." But they are going to know.﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 88-89].

That is: He swore by your saying, O Muhammad: ﴿My Lord, indeed my people have taken this Qur'an as abandoned.﴾ [al-Furqan: 30]. The Truthful, glory be to Him, swears by what He wills, over what He wills: He swears by the angels and by inanimate things, He swears by plants. But the Truthful, glory be to Him and exalted, has sworn by none of creation except the Messenger of Allah, in His saying: ﴿By your life, [O Muhammad], indeed, they were, in their intoxication, wandering blindly.﴾ [al-Hijr: 72].

That is: "by your long life" (ta'mirak), or "by your life, O Muhammad."

And just as He, glory be to Him, swore by the life of His prophet Muhammad, He swore by his saying, so He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And [He has knowledge of] his saying, "My Lord, indeed these are a people who will not believe."﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 88].

Then the Truthful, glory be to Him, addresses His believing servants, saying, exalted is He:

﴿O you who have believed, do not be like those who abused Musa...﴾.

Following the speech of the Exalted about those who harmed Allah, harmed the Messenger of Allah, and harmed the believers, He showed that the matter is not partisanship for Muhammad; rather, this is a principle prevailing among all the messengers of Allah. The prohibition of harming Muhammad does not mean that you may harm his brother messengers. So the Exalted says:

﴿O you who have believed, do not be like those who harmed Moses, but Allah cleared him of what they said..﴾ [al-Ahzab: 69]

Moses (peace be upon him) had two relationships in the course of his mission: a relationship with the Pharaohs and a relationship with the Children of Israel. Moses (peace be upon him) was not a messenger to the Pharaohs; he was sent to the Children of Israel. Therefore Moses and Aaron said to Pharaoh: ﴿Indeed, we are two messengers of your Lord, so send with us the Children of Israel and do not torment them..﴾ [Ta-Ha: 47]. His aim was the deliverance of the Children of Israel from Pharaoh's enslavement.

As for his calling Pharaoh to faith in Allah and displaying the miracle before him, in the hope that he would believe, it came as a side matter to his essential mission to the Children of Israel. Nevertheless, Moses (peace be upon him) was not spared the harm of Pharaoh, who said of him: ﴿a lying sorcerer﴾ [Ghafir: 24].

And he said: ﴿Indeed, your messenger who has been sent to you is mad!﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 27].

And he said: ﴿Am I not better than this one who is contemptible and can hardly express himself?﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 52].

It is natural that Moses (peace be upon him) would be harmed by Pharaoh, since he came to nullify Pharaoh's claimed divinity. But how is he harmed by the Children of Israel, when he is the one who came to rescue them from the grip of Pharaoh and from the torment and enslavement they were suffering?

The scholars said: the Children of Israel harmed Moses when they harmed the One who sent him, Allah the Exalted and Most High, when they said to him: ﴿Show us Allah openly..﴾ [al-Nisa': 153].

And they said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is poor and we are rich..﴾ [Al 'Imran: 181].

And they harmed Moses when they objected to what Allah had provided them of manna and quails, saying: ﴿We will not endure one kind of food, so call upon your Lord to bring forth for us from what the earth grows—of its herbs, its cucumbers, its garlic, its lentils, and its onions.' He said, 'Would you exchange what is better for what is inferior? Go down to a city, and indeed you will have what you asked..﴾ [al-Baqarah: 61].

It is well known that manna is a substance resembling honey, which falls like dew in the morning from the trees, and quails are a bird resembling the quail that Allah drove to them without any toil on their part. But they were a people who did not believe in the unseen, and did not want this ready food; they wanted something tangible that they would plant and prepare with their own hands.

Then they harmed Moses (peace be upon him) in his person, when they accused him of killing his brother Aaron when the two of them ascended the mountain and Aaron died there. They said that Moses had resented his brother and killed him. So Allah caused the angels to carry Aaron's body and pass it by the Children of Israel while it was sound, with no wound in it. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿but Allah cleared him of what they said..﴾ [al-Ahzab: 69].

Others said: rather, they accused Moses (peace be upon him) of a bodily defect, because he (peace be upon him) was extremely modest and reserved, taking great care to conceal himself when bathing and when relieving himself. So they said: he does this only because of a defect that he wants to hide.

Some of them said: he has leprosy (baras). Others dared to accuse him of a defect in his genitals. Allah willed to clear him of what they said. One day he went down to the river to bathe, and Allah commanded a stone, which took his garments far from him. Moses (peace be upon him) ran after the stone saying: "My garment, O stone! My garment, O stone!" Then they saw him cleared of the defects with which they had accused him.

Or: when a dispute arose between Qarun and Moses (peace be upon him), Qarun hired a prostitute and said to her: accuse Moses in front of people. Allah willed that the people gathered and she spoke and said: Qarun did such-and-such. Thus Allah cleared him by that.

The Exalted and Most High says here: ﴿O you who have believed, do not be like those who harmed Moses, but Allah cleared him of what they said..﴾ [al-Ahzab: 69], negating the defect from him, and then affirming for him dignity and honor.

﴿And he was distinguished in the sight of Allah.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 69]. And what dignity is greater than after Allah has displayed his innocence and made clear the lies of his enemies? Dignity (wajaha) is a state indicating that his hope is accepted and his supplication is accepted; no one dares to hurl a defect at him after that, nor to accuse him of a sin he did not commit, because they knew that Moses has a Lord who protects him and defends him.

Among the justice of the Exalted with His creation is that whoever is accused of a sin he did not commit is compensated for it by having a sin he did commit concealed for him, and is not disgraced by it. So it is one for one. Except for one thing that happened with Moses (peace be upon him): when he met the answer of Allah, as if the generosity of his Lord had deceived him, he said: "O Lord, since they have said about me such-and-such, I ask You that nothing be said about me that is not in me." He said: "O Moses, I did not do that for Myself, so how would I do it for you?" The meaning is that they say about the right of Allah, the Exalted, even more than that.

So, Allah left disbelief in place so that everyone who denied His favor would be reassured, as if He were saying to him: Do not grieve, for I am the Creator, and I am the Provider; and yet they disbelieved in Me and denied the favor.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 33, verses 70–71:

We have previously spoken about the meaning of taqwa (God-consciousness, literally "placing a shield"), which is that you place between yourself and Allah a protective barrier. Allah, glorified is He, has attributes of beauty (jamal) and attributes of majesty (jalal). The attributes of beauty are grace (al-fadl), tenderness (al-ra'fah), forgiveness (al-maghfirah), self-sufficiency (al-ghina), and benefit (al-naf')... etc. The attributes of majesty are al-Jabbar, al-Muntaqim, Dhu al-Batsh... etc. So taqwa is that you place between yourself and the attributes of majesty a shield that protects you from them, because you are not able to withstand the might (batsh) and vengeance of Allah.

Nevertheless, one of the knowers ('arifun) says: "Be eager for your nearness (ma'iyyah) with Allah." Yes, because when you place between yourself and the attributes of majesty a shield, you draw near to the attributes of beauty.

As for when the saying of the Exalted, ﴿Fear Allah...﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 112] and His saying, ﴿and fear the Fire...﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 131], become confusing to you, know that the Fire is one of the armies of the anger of Allah. Whoever fears Allah fears the Fire, so there is no contradiction then.

The meaning of ﴿and speak a upright word﴾ [al-Ahzab: 70] is: a truthful word that leads to the truth. The word sadid (upright, true) derives from sadad al-sahm (the straightness of an arrow), when it hits its target and does not miss it. Your target is that you enjoy the Essence of Allah in the Hereafter, and that you shake off the means (al-asbab) that are in this world, and live with the Causer (al-musabbib), glorified is He.

So in this world, when you want to eat, for example, look at the food that was prepared for you: how much time, capacities and money it took... etc. But in the Hereafter, merely as a thing comes to your mind you find it before your hands. Therefore, this is a nearness (ma'iyyah) that you must be eager for with the utmost eagerness.

Then the Exalted tells us the result of the upright word: ﴿He will amend for you your deeds and forgive you your sins. And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly attained a great attainment﴾ [al-Ahzab: 71]. That is, in the Hereafter. The attainment is described as great because in this world you receive the bounty of Allah through the means of Allah, whereas in the Hereafter you receive the bounty of Allah from the Essence of Allah, and there is nothing greater than this.

Then the Exalted says:

﴿Indeed, We offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth...﴾.

Then the Exalted tells us the result of the upright word: ﴿He will amend for you your deeds and forgive you your sins. And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly attained a great attainment﴾ [al-Ahzab: 71]. That is, in the Hereafter. The attainment is described as great because in this world you receive the bounty of Allah through the means of Allah, whereas in the Hereafter you receive the bounty of Allah from the Essence of Allah, and there is nothing greater than this.

Then the Exalted says:

﴿Indeed, We offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth...﴾.

Al-'Ard: the presentation of something to someone, as we see for instance in a military parade, where models of armies and weapons pass before the commander. From it is the Almighty's words about the story of our master Sulayman, peace be upon him: ﴿When there were displayed before him, at eventide, the poised, swift-footed steeds﴾ [Sad: 31].

From it is your saying: "I presented the matter to so-and-so," meaning: I made him aware of it, so that he may see his opinion in it, whether he accepts or does not accept. So al-'ard (presentation) is an offering of choice, not a compulsion.

So the Almighty says: "We presented the trust (al-amanah) to My creation, every creature of Mine," including humans, animals, inanimate objects and plants, to see which of them would accept bearing it and which would refuse. Thus the meaning of al-'ard is that there are those who will accept and those who will refuse.

Therefore we have said: it is an error to say that the earth, the heavens, the mountains, and so on, are driven and subjugated. Rather, we must amend the statement and say they are subjugated by their own choice; for when God presented the trust to them, they refused to bear it and were apprehensive of it, and said: "We will leave by the door of beauty," so they chose not to be choosers.

In our custom, the meaning of amanah (trust) is money, or precious things that one fears may be lost, so you deposit them with someone in whom you find that he will safeguard them until you need them. You may not take a written bond from the one you entrusted, nor bring witnesses; otherwise it would no longer be a trust. Thus there is no proof required except the trustee's own honesty: if he wishes, he acknowledges it and returns it; if he wishes, he denies it.

So the amanah is the self's commitment to be a chooser in action and otherwise. If it is compelled by a bond, or by the testimony of witnesses, it ceases to be a trust.

The trust which the Almighty presented to His creation is the trust of choice: that one be a chooser in whether to believe or disbelieve, in whether to obey or disobey. All beings other than man refused to bear it, because the zeal did not take them at the time of presentation and acceptance, fearing that the time of fulfilment would come and they would find no pledge for it.

There is a difference between the time of acceptance and the time of fulfilment. Whoever considers only the time of acceptance advances and accepts it, but whoever considers fulfilment along with acceptance refuses. For perhaps, even with good intention and desire to fulfil, circumstances change, or one's integrity changes, or something arises that makes you need it, and your hand reaches out to it, and the time of fulfilment comes and you are unable.

All kinds of existence other than man refused to bear the trust, and they chose subjugation and being driven for the Creator, Mighty and Majestic; because man, as his Lord described him: ﴿he was wrongdoing, ignorant﴾ [al-Ahzab: 72].

Likewise, the righteous servants of God attained the station of servanthood to God when they directed their choice according to their Lord's will. God gave them choice in faith or disbelief, so they believed; He gave them choice in obedience and in disobedience, so they obeyed. They directed their choice to what their Lord loves, and so they became among His close servants.

So it is as if you have relinquished your own choice in freedom of movement, and you became like the heavens, the earth and the mountains, when they relinquished their choice for the choice of their Lord; and you have reached, though you are a chooser, a state where you choose nothing except what God has laid down for you as a method.

Here some like to say: how was the trust presented to the heavens, the earth and the mountains, when they are inanimate, and how could they refuse...? We say: you have put yourself into a maze. Was the presentation from you, so that the inanimate would need to understand you? Or was the presentation from their Lord and Creator?

Whenever you see an act done by you and by God, beware of separating the event from its doer, and God says: ﴿Does He not know who created? And He is the Subtle, the All-Aware﴾ [al-Mulk: 14].

He, glory be to Him, is their Creator, and He is the One who addresses them, and they did not deny that. God taught some of His messengers, for example, the language of birds, so he understood it and communicated with it, as He, glory be to Him, said of His prophet Sulayman that he said: ﴿We have been taught the speech of birds, and given of everything...﴾ [al-Naml: 16].

And He said: ﴿So he smiled, laughing at her saying...﴾ [al-Naml: 19].

And He said of the glorification of the mountains with our master Dawud, peace be upon him: ﴿O mountains, repeat with him the praises, and the birds...﴾ [Saba: 10]. The mountains, yes, glorify in every state, but what distinguished our master Dawud was that his glorification coincided with the glorification of the angels, as though they were all one group chanting one anthem.

So: the Creator, glory be to Him, is the One who addresses whomever He wills of His creation, and if He had taught you to address inanimate things, you would have addressed them. Consider, for example, the story of the hoopoe and our master Sulayman when he went to the people of Sheba, and found them worshipping the sun instead of God, and how he had a complete understanding of the matter of monotheism.

So give yourself rest, and attribute the act to its doer while you rest; and you have an example in the conduct of your life. For instance, if your son came in to you with torn clothes, bleeding, before you ask him anything you ask: who did this to you?

You must identify the doer first, for upon him you will build your judgment and decision. If the doer is the neighbour's son, for example, you raise the world and do not let it sit; but if he says: "My uncle so-and-so hit me," your nerves calm down, and you tell the boy: you must have done something that deserved punishment; and if you went to his uncle you would indeed learn that the boy had committed a mistake. So the one act may be bad, or may be good; the important question is: who is the doer?

The verses of the Qur'an support one another and assist us in this matter, for the One who said ﴿Indeed, We offered the trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains...﴾ [al-Ahzab: 72] said ﴿And there is not a thing but glorifies Him with His praise...﴾ [al-Isra: 44].

So everything in all existence glorifies, which indicates that existing things have a signification in themselves, and can express what they intend. We are astonished at some scholars who say: this is an indication by state, not by speech; and this view is refuted by His saying: ﴿But you do not understand their glorification...﴾ [al-Isra: 44].

We understand the glorification of indication, and see it in the harmony of the universe's parts and its wondrous order, but the Truth establishes that we will not understand this glorification. So it is a glorification of speech in reality, which no one knows except whom God has made to know. Why should we rule out the glorification of created beings, when we see that some groups and professions have (codes) and signs that no one else understands, and within a single language you can hear words whose meaning you do not know, let alone the differences between languages among different nationalities?

If you do not know some meanings in your own language, and if you do not know the languages of others who are of your own kind, why do you deny that other kinds in existence have languages by which they recognise one another and express themselves?

Moreover, are all languages and means of understanding spoken? Is there not, for example, sign language, which some agree upon and understand by? Yet there is a common measure and a logic of signification upon which everyone agrees in all languages and by which they communicate, as deaf people communicate, and as there are things in which all natures agree, such as laughing and weeping; there is no Arab laughter nor French weeping, for example.

The meaning of bearing the trust (haml al-amanah) is: undertaking it and applying it, as in His saying regarding the meaning of bearing: ﴿The likeness of those who were charged with the Torah, then did not bear it, is the likeness of a donkey carrying books...﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 5].

They bore it as a method and preserved what is in it, but they did not bear it in the sense of: they did not apply this method. So their likeness with God became that of the donkey which carries books and does not benefit from what is in them. This in itself is not a reproach to the donkey, nor an accusation of stupidity as some claim; for the donkey's task is not understanding but carrying. So whoever carries a method without benefiting from it is like the donkey in this matter; and this is a peculiarity of the donkey, that it carries what it does not understand.

In other matters, the donkey does understand and performs its duty in a manner that man may sometimes fail to. It is well known of the donkey that if it goes to a place it does not forget it nor lose its way to it even after a long time, whereas a person may lose the way he travelled some time ago. If you leave the donkey free to move, it will take you back to the very same place. So who is the foolish one?

Therefore some ask: why then do they accuse the donkey of stupidity? They say: because they burdened it with what God did not burden it with. The donkey was created for carrying, and you want it to have a degree of understanding that you may find lacking even in a rational man.

We have said before: if you want the donkey to leap over a canal that is wider than its capabilities, it will never obey you; however much you beat it, it will not venture the leap. If it is within its power, it looks at the canal as though it measures its width exactly, then leaps without your forcing it; and this behaviour is that of one who calculates consequences well and understands what he does.

So: a thing is not separated from its task, and it is not asked for beyond what it was prepared for. We gave as an example the iron rod: you see its beauty in its straightness; but if you want it as a hook, for instance, its beauty and fulfilment of its task are achieved only through its bend, and then you cannot call it crooked, because this bend is the very essence of straightness for its task.

Therefore we said regarding the Almighty's words: ﴿Indeed, the most hateful of voices is the braying of donkeys﴾ [Luqman: 19], it is not a reproach to the donkey's voice; for God made the donkey's voice loud in this way because it lives in the desert, and often hides behind a height, a rock or a tree, or goes a long distance away from its companion; so its voice came in this form to indicate its location and guide its companion to its place.

So a loud voice becomes objectionable if it has no task, and if it is used in the wrong place; and a thing may differ in form while its task remains one.

For example, blood, by which a human lives, if it clots inside its vessels leads to paralysis of the organ and needs medicines to restore its fluidity; and on the other hand, if the fluidity of the blood increases, it leads to haemorrhage; and if a wound occurs that does not heal, because the blood does not clot and does not block the points of its escape. So clotting of blood is required outside the vessels, and fluidity of blood is required inside the vessels. Thus each has wisdom in its place.

The meaning of ﴿and they were apprehensive of it﴾ [al-Ahzab: 72]: they feared at the time of acceptance, lest the time of fulfilment come and they not fulfil it. ﴿And man bore it﴾ [al-Ahzab: 72], because of what he has of thought, choice and effort; but his thought may bring him harm.

We have said: man eats, for example, until he is satisfied, then sweet and cold things are offered to him, and his belly fills to indigestion and to sickness; whereas the donkey or the buffalo, for example, does not eat a single stalk beyond satiety, because it is governed by instinct which does not know how to manage things; and the animal's distinction lies in this instinct and in its not acting arbitrarily.

Therefore man is described here as ﴿wrongdoing, ignorant﴾ [al-Ahzab: 72], and this is the form fa'ul, indicating intensity in wrongdoing and intensity in ignorance. Wronging others may be understood, since the wrongdoer thinks he benefits from it; but that a person wrongs himself by withholding good from himself, or bringing harm upon himself, this is not reasonable and is a sign of foolishness.

So when he is lazy in obedience for the sake of a fleeting appetite of the soul, withholding from himself a lasting good and an unlimited enjoyment, he is an enemy to himself. Therefore the scholars said: the soul of man is his greatest enemy; for if the enemy is from outside you, you can see him and take precautions against him; but if he is from within you, his affair is difficult.

The Almighty has shown that the greatest wrong is shirk with God, as He said: ﴿Indeed, shirk is a great wrong﴾ [Luqman: 13]. This wrong too does not harm God, Exalted; it returns only upon the one who associates others with God. Therefore after wrongdoing He describes man as ignorant, because he wrongs himself; and this indicates ignorance and lack of knowledge. The ignorant one is the one who falls into error and turns away from truth out of ignorance; so the description here indicates the wisdom of the outcome: ﴿Indeed, he was wrongdoing, ignorant﴾ [al-Ahzab: 72].

Then the Almighty says:

﴿That God may punish the hypocrite men and hypocrite women, and the polytheist men and polytheist women...﴾.

Firstly, our attention is drawn to the fact that the preceding verse was concluded with the words of the Exalted, ﴿Indeed, he was ever wrongdoing and ignorant﴾ [al-Ahzab: 72], while this verse was concluded with His words, glorified is He, ﴿And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Ahzab: 73]. It is as if the description (ظَلُومَاً, zalūman, "wrongdoing") was answered by (غَفُورَاً, ghafūran, "Forgiving"), and (جَهُولاً, jahūlan, "ignorant") was answered by (رَحيماً, raḥīman, "Merciful").

So the Truth, glorified is He, is Forgiving to the one who wrongs, and Merciful to the one who is ignorant. The Qur'anic pattern is thus a manifestation of the mercy of Allah. Allah, glorified and exalted is He, is known by those who believe in Him to be Forgiving and Merciful. But the attributes of beauty in your Lord, Mighty and Majestic, should not deceive you so that you venture into sin and do wrong, relying on the fact that your Lord will forgive and will show mercy.

Therefore, concerning His words, the Exalted, ﴿O mankind, what has deceived you concerning your Generous Lord?﴾ [al-Infitar: 6], they said that what deceived man concerning his Lord, so that he disobeyed Him or disbelieved in Him, was his reliance on the fact that his Lord is Generous. Thus the attribute of generosity in Allah is what emboldened him to disobey.

It is as if the Truth, glorified is He, taught man the answer to this question. If he is asked, "What has deceived you concerning your Lord?", he should say, "His generosity." In our countryside, one of the peasants asks another: "Why do you not settle in your prayer and peck at it this way? Suppose you owed someone a (shilling), would it be right to give him a (worn-out shilling)?" The man replied: "By God, if he were generous, he would accept it."

There is another subtle point in His words in the verse: ﴿That Allah may punish the hypocrite men and the hypocrite women..﴾ [al-Ahzab: 73]. Was the offering of the trust and the obligation to people for the purpose of punishing them? Is punishment intended by Allah in the ruling?

They said: No; because the lam here in ﴿li-yu'adhdhiba..﴾ [al-Ahzab: 73] is the lam of consequence (lām al-'āqibah), for the Truth, glorified is He, made the obligation so that people would follow it and not be punished. The lam thus indicates the outcome, as in His words: ﴿Then the people of Pharaoh picked him up, so that he might become for them an enemy and a grief﴾ [al-Qasas: 8].

For when the people of Pharaoh picked him up, they picked him up, peace be upon him, so that he might be a comfort of the eye for them, not so that he would become an enemy. But what happened was that he became an enemy and a grief. So the lam is not for causation; rather it is the lam of outcome and consequence, which means that you do a thing for an aim you have in mind, and then the consequence comes to show the foolishness of the one who acted.

As for His words: ﴿the hypocrite men and the hypocrite women..﴾ [al-Ahzab: 73], we have already defined hypocrisy (nifāq), and we said that hypocrisy is worse than disbelief (kufr), because the disbeliever is consistent with himself, since he disbelieves with his heart and with his tongue. That is, his tongue agrees with what is in his heart. The hypocrite, however, is not consistent with himself, for he believes in something and utters the opposite: he hides disbelief and displays belief. So he is scattered in thought. Therefore he deserves to be the worst of enemies, and to be in the lowest depth of the Fire. It is enough that he has in him deceit and trickery: he is with you in appearance, while in reality he is your enemy.

We also observe in this verse that the Truth, glorified is He, wished to make a complete separation between the recompense of the hypocrite men and hypocrite women and the polytheist men and polytheist women, and the recompense of the believing men and believing women. Human style would require that after it He say: ﴿That Allah may punish the hypocrite men and the hypocrite women and the polytheist men and the polytheist women..﴾ [al-Ahzab: 73], and turn in mercy to the believing men and believing women.

But the Qur'anic context here did not join repentance to punishment, and it separated the two verbs by repeating the explicit subject, which is the divine name, so He said ﴿That Allah may punish..﴾ [al-Ahzab: 73], and said: ﴿and Allah may turn (in mercy)..﴾ [al-Ahzab: 73], in order to separate this from that, and to set it apart with a ruling specific to it. This is because Allah, the Exalted, as we have mentioned, has attributes of majesty (jalāl) which pertain to the disbelievers and hypocrites, and attributes of beauty (jamāl) which pertain to the believers, and each of the two categories has a separate, independent context.
